Removed, reordered or retyped items or buttons Refused; restart Revit. Changed stack placement, membership or row boundaries, or an item added to a retained stack Refused; restart Revit. Changed assembly path or command class Refused; restart Revit. New panel items or grouped-button children after the retained items Appended. Tests Pure tests cover the idle gate (role and load-context decisions), ribbon planning, settings and startup state. They compile only the source needed for platform-neutral behavior, must not run Revit startup and must not load Revit-typed members. Local (Revit-hosted) tests reference the real App project and cover entry behavior, real ribbon composition, command availability, lifecycle cleanup and Revit window ownership. A Revit-hosted test initializes the selected Revit year and uses the shared call gate. Revit-hosted tests take runtime ownership from the staged product tree. Tool project references stay compile references and do not add separate product images to the test dependency closure. Hosted inputs include the complete year root with Tools/ preserved; test assemblies, NUnit files and companions are separate inputs. The daemon's ProductLoadContext forwards product references to the same product instances that App uses. Release checks validate App's entry identity, embedded manifest ownership, command and availability owners, the stable Presentation resources, source-map freshness and the placement in the year tree. See Assembly Loading Contract, Project References and Test Pipeline.

developer-guide/projects/core.html.title: DBTools.Core | DB Tools
developer-guide/projects/core.html.summary: DBTools.Core DBTools.Core is the shared infrastructure library of DB Tools. It contains the Revit execution layer (call gates and run scopes), transaction management, safe execution, logging, settings, the tool module system and shared UI components. Property Value Assembly DBTools.Core.dll Targets Desktop net10.0-windows (Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) and Revit 2027); portable net10.0 WPF Desktop target only (UseWPF=true) Nullable Enabled Responsibilities Revit execution: thread-safe Revit API access through call gates and run scopes. Transactions: transaction and sub-transaction handling with rollback on failure. Safe execution: central error handling with user notification and logging. Logging: Serilog-based structured logging with a UI sink. Settings: typed settings sections with persistence and validation. Tool modules: discovery, registration and lifecycle of tools. Shared UI: window support, alert dialogs, progress overlays and behaviors. Build Desktop builds compile the complete Core for one Revit year. Pure tests and the Sandbox use that same image. Revit references are compile-only. Portable builds ($(DBT_PortableTargetFramework)) compile only the explicit source list in DBTools.Core.csproj, without WPF, Revit, merging or content identity. Designer builds (DBT_IsDesignerBuild=true) exclude Revit sources so the XAML designer can load without the Revit SDK. _wpftmp builds (temporary projects during BAML compilation) exclude Revit-dependent sources and re-include the runtime files that XAML resolution needs. A default desktop build writes its assembly to the artifact locations that the shared build props select. Revit-hosted test projects reference the evaluated Core TargetPath, not the product staging tree. Dependencies Reference Purpose DBTools.Manifest (project, desktop only) Portable manifest parser; merged privately with YamlDotNet DBTools.Presentation (project, desktop only) Stable WPF resources and controls Serilog.Extensions.Logging Structured logging; Core supplies the ThreadId enricher Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection Dependency injection CommunityToolkit.Mvvm MVVM base classes CSharpFunctionalExtensions Result types LibTessDotNet Polygon tessellation InternalsVisibleTo These assemblies see Core internals: runtime: DBTools, DBTools.GM, DBTools.SGT, DBTools.ERFT, DBTools.Settings, DBTools.DialogSuppression, DBTools.FoundationTags; Core tests: DBTools.Core.Pure.Tests, DBTools.Core.Local.Tests, DBTools.Core.HostedTurns.Local.Tests, DBTools.Core.Portable.Pure.Tests; App tests: DBTools.App.Pure.Tests, DBTools.App.Local.Tests; tool tests: DBTools.AnalyticalSnapToLevel.Local.Tests, DBTools.DialogSuppression.Local.Tests, DBTools.ElevationTags.Local.Tests, DBTools.ERFT.Local.Tests, DBTools.FoundationTags.Local.Tests, DBTools.FramingJoins.Local.Tests, DBTools.GM.Local.Tests, DBTools.JoistGirderWeight.Local.Tests, DBTools.OrganizeFoundationTypes.Local.Tests, DBTools.RecordSet.Pure.Tests, DBTools.RecordSet.Local.Tests, DBTools.SGT.Local.Tests, DBTools.TDV.Local.Tests, DBTools.VTC.Local.Tests. Directory structure DBTools.Core/ +-- Alert/{Body,Composition,DesignTime,Domain,Selection,ViewModels,Views,Workflow} +-- AppRuntime/{Domain,Runtime} # Runtime contracts and the static accessor +-- Failure # FailurePrecedence +-- Guarding # Guard and analyzer marker +-- Hashing # SHA-256 operations +-- Json # Strict camel-case enum converter +-- Logging/{Composition,DebugMode,Files,LoggerWindow,Retention,Runtime,Sinks} +-- Notifications/{Composition,Domain,NotificationBanner,Runtime} +-- Paths # AppPaths +-- Progress/{Aggregation,Overlay} +-- Regex # Shared regex construction +-- Revit/{Composition,Context,DocumentSession,Execution,Transactions} +-- RevitInstance/{Identity,RevitYear} +-- Ribbon # ProductRibbon +-- SafeExecution/{Domain,Runtime} +-- Sandbox # SandboxMode +-- Settings/{Alerts,Catalog,Composition,DesignTime,Domain,Feedback,Persistence,RegexPattern,Reset,SettingsPack,State,Validation,ViewModels,Warnings} +-- TextFile # Text-file operations +-- Time # EasternTime +-- Tools/{Availability,Commands,Hooks,Manifest,Modules,Ribbon,Sandbox} +-- Transactions # Failure-definition contracts +-- UI/{ColorPicker,Commanding,DesignTime,Dispatching,FilePicker,Theming,Windows} +-- Tests # Core test projects Tests Project Target Content DBTools.Core.Portable.Pure.Tests net10.0 Portable Core behavior that runs on Linux: Guard, strict JSON enums, safe-execution names and monotonic progress. References Core directly. DBTools.Core.Pure.Tests net10.0-windows Desktop Core and merged-owner behavior without Revit, including collectible composition activation, the progress overlay and the logger window dispatcher routing. DBTools.Core.Local.Tests net10.0-windows Revit-hosted fixtures. Has a test-only reference to DBTools.Presentation, which owns the overlay control and the structural preview. DBTools.Core.HostedTurns.Local.Tests net10.0-windows Fixtures that need real native Revit turns (the RevitHostedTurns category). Core test projects use explicit <Compile> membership. Test files mirror the owner folders under Tests/; when a test file moves, update the compile links in the Pure and Local projects in the same change. Revit execution and transactions Revit Execution and Progress Overlay owns the design of run scopes, call gates, queued turns, ITransactionRunner, transaction groups and the progress overlay. Folder Content Revit/Execution/CallGate IRevitCallGate, InlineRevitCallGate, QueuedRevitCallGate, delegate admission, API-context admission (RevitCallGateApiContext) and the queued turn scheduler (RevitCallGateTask) Revit/Execution/RunScope IRevitRunScope, AppRunScope and AppRunScopeFactory Revit/Context RevitApplicationContext and ContextUnavailableException Revit/DocumentSession DocumentSessionKey Revit/Transactions ITransactionRunner, TransactionFailurePreprocessor and TransactionFailureException; under TransactionGroup/, ITransactionGroupService, IAtomicTransactionGroup and RevitTransactionGroups Revit/Composition RevitServiceCollectionExtensions: the Revit-scoped registrations Progress/Overlay, Progress/Aggregation IProgressOverlay, ProgressOverlay and MonotonicProgressAdapter ElementIdConverter.ToLong returns the full 64-bit element ID; use it for element identities, including the IDs in diagnostics. ToInt is a checked conversion for contracts that Revit defines as int, such as built-in category IDs. Safe execution ISafeExecutor Every tool entry point runs inside ISafeExecutor. public interface ISafeExecutor { Task RunAsync(Func<Task> action, ILogger logger, IErrorNotifier? notifier, SafeExecutionOptions opts, CancellationToken ct = default); Task<SafeExecutionResult> RunWithoutThrowingAsync(Func<Task> action, ILogger logger, IErrorNotifier? notifier, SafeExecutionOptions opts, CancellationToken ct = default); } SafeExecutor: gives each execution a GUID correlation ID and logs the elapsed milliseconds; checks the token immediately before it invokes the action inside the protected boundary, so pre-canceled work returns a canceled result without running; logs full exception details, including inner exceptions and XAML parse context. ExceptionDiagnosticsLogger owns the formatting of exception, cancellation, XAML and notifier-failure logs; shows success and error banners through IErrorNotifier and logs notifier failures; calls ISafeExecutionFailureSurface on fatal errors. App composition adapts the logger window's show action to this interface (SafeExecutionFailureSurface), so Logging does not depend on SafeExecution; propagates failures from RunAsync(...). RunWithoutThrowingAsync(...) is for event and UI callers that log and notify, then stop propagation. An expected refusal throws SafeExecutionRefusedException; the result status is SafeExecutionStatus.Refused and SafeExecutionRefusalReporter reports it once. SafeExecutionOptions Defined in SafeExecution/Domain/SafeExecutionOptions.cs. The constructor sets the operation name; every option is immutable after initialization. public sealed class SafeExecutionOptions { public enum Mode { SuccessAndError = 0, ErrorOnly = 1, SuppressAlways = 2 } public enum FailureSurfacePolicy { Surface, Suppress } public SafeExecutionOptions(string name); public string Name { get; } public bool LogStart { get; init; } = true; public bool LogCompletion { get; init; } = true; public bool LogFailure { get; init; } = true; public Mode BannerMode { get; init; } = Mode.SuccessAndError; public FailureSurfacePolicy FailureSurface { get; init; } = FailureSurfacePolicy.Surface; public Guid? CorrelationId { get; init; } public static SafeExecutionOptions ErrorBanner(string name, ...); public static SafeExecutionOptions SuppressFailurePresentation(string name); } Commands ToolCommand The abstract base class of Revit commands. public abstract class ToolCommand : IExternalCommand, IExternalCommandAvailability { public Result Execute(ExternalCommandData commandData, ref string message, ElementSet elements); internal Result ExecuteCore(UIApplication uiApplication, ref string message); protected abstract Task RunAsync(ICommandContext context); } Execute validates the Autodesk arguments, takes the non-null UIApplication and calls ExecuteCore. ExecuteCore resolves ISafeExecutor, ILogger and IErrorNotifier from the live IAppRuntime, runs CommandPreflight, and creates one CommandContext that owns its IAppRunScope before it calls RunAsync. ToolCommand has no service-resolution, call-gate or tool-window helpers. A command that owns a window composes its ToolWindowFactory and uses the returned IToolWindowSession. public class MyToolCommand : ToolCommand { protected override async Task RunAsync(ICommandContext context) { var transactionRunner = context.Resolve<ITransactionRunner>(); await transactionRunner.RunInActiveDocumentAsync("My Operation", tx => { var doc = tx.Document; // Modify the document. }); } } Command preflight CommandPreflight is the preflight contract of ToolCommand. Contextual edit ExternalEvent flows declare the registered command type on their ContextualRibbonInjector and call the same preflight before RunEditFlow(...). The preflight resolves an enabled registration, checks Revit availability through the supplied callback, then checks active settings warnings. Registry lookup, ribbon panel flags and settings-warning blocking stay inside it. internal sealed class CommandPreflight { internal CommandPreflight(ToolRegistry registry, ISettingsProvider settings, Action<RegisteredCommand, UIApplication> validateAvailability, ISettingsWarningService warnings); internal RegisteredCommand ResolveRegisteredCommand(Type commandType); internal Task<RegisteredCommand> ValidateAsync(RegisteredCommand command, UIApplication application, CancellationToken ct = default); } ICommandContext The command's view of its run scope, DI scope and captured UI state. public interface ICommandContext : IAppRunScope { UIApplication UIApplication { get; } UIDocument UIDocument { get; } Document Document { get; } IWindowOwnerHandleProvider OwnerHandleProvider { get; } ILogger Logger { get; } void ShowBanner(string title, string message); } Runtime public interface IAppRuntime { ILogger Logger { get; } ILoggerFactory LoggerFactory { get; } T Resolve<T>() where T : notnull; } public interface IAppRunScope : IDisposable // scoped DI container for one command { IRevitRunScope RevitRunScope { get; } T Resolve<T>() where T : notnull; } AppRuntimeAccessor is the static accessor for the current IAppRuntime, for code that cannot receive it through DI (for example, Revit's parameterless constructor): public static class AppRuntimeAccessor { public static bool IsInitialized { get; } public static void Initialize(IAppRuntime runtime); public static void Reset(); public static IAppRuntime RequireInProcessRuntime(string consumerName); public static ILogger Logger { get; } public static ILoggerFactory LoggerFactory { get; } public static ILogger CreateLogger(string categoryName); public static ILogger CreateLogger<T>(); public static T Resolve<T>() where T : notnull; } Logging Logging runtime The logging runtime owns the Serilog setup, the UI sink, the active log-file path and manual file rollover. public static class LoggingRuntimeFactory { public static ILoggingRuntime Create(LoggingOptions options); } internal sealed class LoggingRuntime : ILoggingRuntime, ILoggingDebugLevelController, ILoggingSinkSource, ILoggingFileSession, ILoggingInstanceMetadata { } ILoggingRuntime combines ILoggerFactory, lifecycle, the current log path, debug-level control and console mirroring. App composition uses the internal LoggingRuntime, which implements every narrow capability, and registers it through its interfaces, not as a concrete service. The sink, file-session and instance-metadata contracts are internal to Core. LoggingRuntime.CreateLogger(...) after disposal throws ObjectDisposedException. File sink: LogFileSink keeps the active file writer and its path. A file cutover publishes the new writer and path before it retires the previous writer. A retirement failure is logged as diagnostic data and does not roll back the new path. Manual rollover: the logger window can switch file logging to a new file on demand. Enrichment: every entry carries the thread ID. The process identity and Revit year come from RevitInstance/Identity (RevitInstanceIdentity, RevitInstanceIdGenerator). Retention: old log files are deleted by age, count and total size. Banners: user-visible banners are logged through the WindowDiagnostics category: error banners at Error, warning banners at Warning, info and success banners at Information. AppPaths.LogsDir is the only log-directory path: %APPDATA%/DBTools/Logs. Reading it does not create the directory; lifecycle owners call AppPaths.EnsureCreated() before they construct a logging runtime. Log file names: dbtools-{revitYear}-{instanceId}-{timestamp}-{nonce}.log dbtools-{instanceId}-{timestamp}-{nonce}.log # no Revit year dbtools-{revitYear}-{instanceId}-{timestamp}-{nonce}-manual-{timestamp}.log # manual rollover Logger window LoggerWindowHost, LoggerWindowSurfaceSession and LoggerWindowViewModel depend only on the narrow internal capability contracts registered by Core logging composition. Nothing outside Core references the concrete host. The view model keeps one bounded sequence of raw entries and derives the grouped Items collection from it. Display filters change only that projection; Copy All and Export enumerate the retained raw entries once, in arrival order. Buffering, filtering and file operations are in LoggerWindowViewModel.Buffering.cs, .Filtering.cs and .FileOperations.cs under Logging/LoggerWindow/ViewModels. Export is one operation: path selection, formatting and writing. A canceled picker does nothing. A picker or write failure records the diagnostic and keeps a visible export Error entry. File reload reads the active log through LogFileSession.ReadCurrentLogTail while the writer is open. The bounded UTF-8 reader drops only an incomplete first line when the byte window starts inside a line. Continuation lines are separate entries; they take metadata from a parsed header only when that header is inside the selected window. LoggerWindowHost registers the logger-window error relay through ILoggingSinkSource at host startup and toggles the debug level through ILoggingDebugLevelController. It implements the UI-owned IWindowErrorLogSurface. It passes the UI-owned IFilePicker to LoggerWindowSurfaceSession, which selects the save path with the owner window; the view model raises an internal export-path request and stores no Window or picker. The host supplies ILogger<LoggerWindowViewModel> to the view model directly. Posted logger-window operations go through one router, which observes rejection, abortion and callback failure exactly once. Host and session cleanup attempts every owned resource in order and keeps one original failure or an ordered aggregate. LoggerWindowDispatcherRouter runs inline work on the owning dispatcher and propagates its failure to the caller. For posted work, it reports an action, posting or cancellation failure to the supplied handler at most once. If the handler throws, the router writes both failures through Serilog SelfLog (which writes nothing when disabled). If that write also throws, one AggregateException holds the reported failure, the handler failure and the diagnostic failure, in that order. The aggregate escapes in the reporting context: the target dispatcher for a queued action, the posting caller for a rejected or already-aborted operation, or the thread that raises Aborted (including dispatcher shutdown). The router does not guarantee that a WPF error handler exists or that shutdown continues. ContainedDiagnostic.TryWrite(...) returns null after a successful write. After a write failure it reports through Serilog SelfLog. If SelfLog returns (also when disabled), it returns the original exception. If SelfLog throws, it returns an AggregateException with the write failure first and the SelfLog failure second. It never throws. Callers can ignore the result; WindowErrorPresenter keeps it as secondary presentation-failure data. Notification banners Notifications/Composition constructs IErrorNotifier. public interface IErrorNotifier : IWindowErrorBanner { void ShowWarningBanner(string title, string message); void ShowSuccessBanner(string title, string message); void ShowInfoBanner(string title, string message); } IWindowErrorBanner (UI/Windows/ErrorBoundary) lets window error boundaries request error banners without a dependency on the notification implementation. The notification contract is in Notifications/Domain; owner-handle contracts are in UI/Windows/Ownership. NotificationBannerService holds the public banner API and logging policy, the ShowError error route, the action-free ShowToast route, the action-bearing ShowToastActions route and the surfacing of action failures. A banner action is one cancellation-aware asynchronous callback. The action command awaits it, closes the banner after success when requested, and keeps the banner open on failure or cancellation. NotificationBannerHostRegistry owns dispatcher resolution, owner HWND selection, host creation, top-warning replacement, dismissal and cleanup of all hosts. Only an explicit zero owner HWND, or no usable anchor position, suppresses a banner. WindowOwnerHandleProvider resolves a closing or closed window to the registered default owner (Revit's main window), so a banner from a tool whose window closed before delivery still shows. Dialog and file-picker owners resolve the same way. ModalWindow and ModelessWindow start lifecycle tracking in their constructors. A raw WPF window first seen after it closes uses the default owner only when it was not tracked from construction and has no HWND after EnsureHandle fails; other failures propagate. The lifecycle record (WindowOwnerHandleLifecycle) is in Presentation, so a retained shell never keeps a retired Core instance reachable. A call on the UI thread resolves the owner and shows the banner synchronously. A worker-thread request queues owner resolution and banner creation together and does not wait. Its handle can cancel delivery before it starts or dismiss the banner after it shows. Worker requests use normal dispatcher priority, so a UI-thread request made while one is queued can appear first. Queue and callback failures are logged with the request title and kind; a disposed, reset or retired request logs why it was dropped. Host construction and showing run outside the registry lock; generation and registration are checked again before presentation. Each host checks its disposed state around the final AddBanner steps. Default-owner registration captures the existing UI dispatcher without calling the HWND supplier, refreshes stale entries and never creates a dispatcher. A registry reset invalidates pending requests. It takes and clears the registrations first, attempts each host on its own dispatcher and reports cleanup failures after all attempts. Synchronous owner resolution, banner addition and new-host cleanup failures propagate; an add failure is ordered before a cleanup failure. Later timer and window-close cleanup callbacks are logged and do not propagate. NotificationBannerWindowViewModel owns banner item state, the visible-item projection, overflow state, action commands, expanded state and per-item auto-close cancellation. NotificationBannerTimingController runs every delayed close under one window-lifetime cancellation source with TimeProvider.System, keeps only in-flight operations, dispatches callbacks to the owning dispatcher and logs callback failures. Disposal cancels the lifetime before the window can receive late callbacks. Tests use FakeTimeProvider. WpfDispatcher.Invoke is synchronous and can wait for its dispatcher; so do the file-picker and alert APIs that return a value. WpfDispatcher.Post always queues and returns a completion task. A callback failure faults that task with the original exception and is not rethrown to the dispatcher error boundary; an aborted operation cancels the task. Direct dispatcher callbacks use the dispatcher error boundary. Banner dismissal observes and logs its completion task. File picker IFilePicker takes one request type per result cardinality: FilePickerPathRequest for a single file, a folder or a save path, and FilePickerPathsRequest for several files. The concrete FilePicker keeps path admission and file-type mapping private and uses WPF's OpenFolderDialog for folder selection with an owner. Workflow text and defaults belong to the caller: the logger window names exported logs, TDV settings sets the library and fallback RVT picker titles, and RecordSet sets the target-folder, host-file and DWG picker titles. Sources: src/DBTools.Core/UI/FilePicker/, src/DBTools.Core/Paths/AppPaths.cs, src/DBTools.App/Logging/AppLoggingRuntimeFactory.cs. Settings ISettingsProvider public interface ISettingsProvider { TSettings Get<TSettings>(SettingsSection<TSettings> section) where TSettings : class, new(); Task CommitAsync(IReadOnlyCollection<SettingsSectionWrite> writes, CancellationToken ct = default); } SettingsSection<T> identifies a settings section for reads and persistence. Its source-generated JSON metadata keeps defaults and typed values. CreateWrite(value) carries the section name, declared type and value into an atomic commit. Get(section) returns the current file values. SettingsCatalog The internal, read-only catalog of settings pack definitions. The Settings window, SettingsWarningService and SettingsStartupWarningWorkflow all use it. It rejects null pack definitions, duplicate pack keys, null warning definitions, warning pack-key mismatches and duplicate warning IDs before warning publication or startup evaluation. internal sealed class SettingsCatalog { internal SettingsCatalog(IEnumerable<ISettingsPackDefinition> definitions); public IReadOnlyCollection<ISettingsPackDefinition> Definitions { get; } public IReadOnlyCollection<ISettingsWarningDefinition> WarningDefinitions { get; } } Settings packs public interface ISettingsPackDefinition { string Key { get; } string Title { get; } string RibbonPanel { get; } SettingsPackApplyBehavior ApplyBehavior { get; } IReadOnlyCollection<ISettingsWarningDefinition> WarningDefinitions { get; } ISettingsPackRuntime CreateRuntime(SettingsPackHostContext hostContext); } SettingsPackDefinition<TOptions, TContext> keeps the typed factories and the SettingsSection<TOptions> together and creates a SettingsPackRuntime<TOptions, TContext> per settings row. The runtime owns its TContext, binds every warning getter and setter to that instance, loads through the typed section and stages current and default writes; it accepts no context from the caller. SettingsPackViewModel receives only the runtime, so definitions, contexts, sections and warnings cannot be recombined after catalog admission. ISettingsPackRuntime exposes pack metadata, ValidationContext, bound warnings, lazy view creation, provider-based load, staging of current and default writes, and applying baselines and defaults after commit. A failed cleanup of the owned context can be retried. Disposing a row attempts every warning row and the runtime, keeps the pack and warning identity of each failure and reports the aggregate. ISettingsWarningDefinition is metadata only; ISettingsPackRuntimeWarning.IsActive and SetActive(bool) change the bound state. ISettingsPackContext contains only validation. ISettingsPackContext<TOptions> adds Load(TOptions) and BuildOptionsSnapshot(). Tool modules register packs through SettingsPackRegistration<TOptions, TContext>. The config section, pack key, title, panel, context factory and view factory are required members; a warning also requires its ID, title, message and flag delegates. DI admission checks for non-empty strings and non-null delegates, so reflection or default values cannot admit an invalid registration. SettingsPackHostContext is created only through Empty or FromApplication(...). Source: src/DBTools.Core/Settings/Composition/SettingsPackServiceCollectionExtensions.cs. SettingsPackAutoUpdateContext<TSettings> (Settings/SettingsPack/AutoUpdate) is the base of auto-update pack contexts. It owns the header text, the AutoUpdateEnabled and HasWarning toggles, ClearWarningCommand, WarningId, BlockSaveOnInvalid, baseline-driven HasPendingChanges, MarkSaved after commit, StateChanged and the validation envelope. Derived contexts own typed load, snapshot, baseline equality and validation. ElevationTags and JoistGirderWeight SettingsPackContext derive from it. FoundationTags SettingsPackContext implements the context interfaces directly because it has prerequisite and warning-fix behavior. AutoUpdateViewModel<TSettings> under Settings/DesignTime is designer sample data only. Settings/State/ISettingsStateContext.cs is the shared state-notification contract. RegexPatternListContext (Settings/RegexPattern) is the shared context for editable regex pattern rows: the RegexPatternEntry collection, add and remove commands, a maximum row count, a default row for empty loads, omission of blank values from snapshots and StateChanged. ElevationTags PatternContext and the FoundationTags pattern partial (SettingsPackContext.Patterns.cs) expose their own binding names over it. Settings window Settings/ViewModels owns SettingsPanelBlock, SettingsPackCollection, SettingsPackViewModel, SettingsWarningViewModel and the settings-window partials. Regex rows are in Settings/RegexPattern. Save state, save validation, pending changes and owner-aware pack contracts are in Settings/SettingsPack. Settings/Feedback and Settings/Reset hold the feedback and reset workflows; Settings/DesignTime holds the designer sample pack graph. The Settings window XAML is in Presentation (src/DBTools.Presentation/Settings/Views/SettingsWindow.xaml). SettingsWindowFactory loads the embedded Settings view through ToolWindowFactory and returns a registered modal IToolWindowSession with the owner, title, size, initializer and view model applied. SettingsCommand calls session.ShowDialog(). The session owns teardown on close and retirement. The view model owns Save, Reset All, cancel and close, validation, warnings and the success banner, and is the session's close gate: it refuses to close while Save Settings, Reset All Settings, a pack Reset or the load-problem Reset Settings runs. Save requests its close through the gate, so a running reset keeps Settings open. Construction cleanup: From the first pack runtime it acquires, construction owns cleanup. If warning or row construction fails, the row disposes its warnings and runtime. If a later pack fails, the collection removes cleanly disposed rows and keeps failed cleanup owners for retry. The construction failure stays primary when cleanup also fails. The window factory keeps the view model until window setup completes. Failed setup detaches handlers, clears owner bindings, closes the incomplete window and disposes the view model. Each cleanup step runs independently; the aggregate reports the construction error first. Validation and persistence: SettingsWarningValidator takes pack runtimes, not presentation rows. It checks warning ownership, updates the bound flags and publishes warning state. Its result fixes the counters, the ordered state transitions and every evaluated (PackKey, WarningId, IsActive) decision; the persistence workflow and the window apply those decisions to their rows, also for unchanged states. Startup has its own activation-only workflow with error logging and runtime cleanup. The validator wraps each validation failure with its pack key and title and does not log or show it. Validate Library logs and shows feedback; silent initialization passes the same wrapper to SettingsWindowFactory. For a blocked save, the outer message of the pack validation exception contains the pack title, key and validation text; the original exception is the inner cause. Save feedback shows the outer message. SettingsPersistenceWorkflow owns pre-commit validation, post-commit failure wrapping and baseline ordering. Settings/Persistence owns provider-based storage. Catalog and warning validation do not depend on Settings/ViewModels. Change publication: SettingsChangePublisher delivers events synchronously to ordinary consumers and has a SettingsChangeDelivery.BestEffort path for immediate ribbon UI changes. App's ribbon composition (RibbonSettingsObserver) registers one callback for flag, warning-set and single-warning updates. Awaited publication delivers the ordinary events, then calls that callback with SettingsChangeDelivery.Required, which must apply on the ribbon dispatcher; it adds no second best-effort post. A skipped, retired or failed ribbon application propagates as SettingsPostCommitException after persistence commits, so the UI keeps the committed baseline and shows no success feedback. Core-only and Sandbox use without a ribbon observer publishes the ordinary events only. Sources: src/DBTools.Core/Settings/State/{SettingsChangePublisher,SettingsChangeDelivery}.cs, src/DBTools.Core/Settings/ViewModels/{SettingsPersistenceWorkflow,SettingsWindowViewModel.Commands}.cs. Tool module system Tool infrastructure under src/DBTools.Core/Tools/: Path Content Manifest/ Promotion of parse results, immutable manifest values, extensions and cross-manifest validation Modules/Catalog/ Public discovery: module construction and the complete manifest and error result Modules/Composition/ The ToolModule base class ToolRegistry.cs, ToolAssemblyResolver.cs, ToolTypeResolver.cs Registration and explicit type resolution Commands/ ToolCommand, command context and preflight Availability/ Generic Revit command availability predicates Ribbon/ Revit-free ribbon specs and projection Sandbox/ Sandbox window projection (SandboxCatalog) Hooks/ Hook hosting and lifecycle composition Manifest loading ManifestResourceParser.Parse (project DBTools.Manifest) owns the YAML shape and the semantic checks of each document. Build tooling references that project; Core merges it privately. YAML is deserialized only into parser-private nullable DTOs, and the parser's mappers convert admitted values without a second validation policy. Core promotes each resource into immutable, constructor-validated public manifest values; a partly populated public manifest is not a valid state. Core constructors keep their guards for direct callers. ToolManifestValidationPolicy then applies ManifestResourceValidationPolicy over all promoted entries: duplicate manifest IDs and module types, and every warning-disable target against the complete set of declared ribbon-tool names. Parse, promotion and cross-resource errors keep the declaring resource and the original cause. ToolModuleCatalog.Discover(...) calls the internal manifest loader once and returns one result with all promoted manifest entries, all created modules and every load, promotion and discovery error. App and the Sandbox's SandboxCatalog use that result in the load context that owns the product assembly. ThrowIfErrors() throws one AggregateException whose inner exceptions are the original causes in source order. App logs each error with its manifest and resource before it calls ThrowIfErrors(). ToolModuleCatalog.LoadManifestEntries(...) validates and promotes manifest values but never resolves or constructs moduleType. The Sandbox uses it for later metadata checks, so its compile-time Core cannot discover modules again against a different ToolModule type identity. ToolManifest public sealed class ToolManifest { public ToolManifest(string id, string assembly, int order, string? moduleType = null, string? panel = null, IEnumerable<SandboxWindowManifest>? sandboxWindows = null, ToolMetadataManifest? tool = null); public string Id { get; } public string Assembly { get; } public string? ModuleType { get; } public int Order { get; } public string? Panel { get; } public IReadOnlyList<SandboxWindowManifest> SandboxWindows { get; } public ToolMetadataManifest? Tool { get; } } A manifest without a module must declare a panel and at least one ribbon command, and cannot declare settings or settings packs. A manifest with a module must declare at least one responsibility: tool.ribbonTools, tool.settings, tool.settingsPacks or a registered hook. App checks that after RegisterHooks(...), against the temporary registry, before it merges the module's registrations into the root container. Type resolution and availability ToolTypeResolver resolves a manifest type only from the assemblies the caller supplies; it never scans all loaded assemblies. Command types resolve against the manifest's tool assembly. Availability types resolve against the tool assembly, Core and the App runtime assembly, so startup cannot bind to a stale or unrelated assembly. Generic availability predicates (active document, active view, selection) are in Tools/Availability. Manifests reference them for common requirements; a tool-specific predicate stays with the tool feature that owns the rule. ToolModule public abstract class ToolModule { public virtual void RegisterSettings(IServiceCollection services, ToolManifest manifest) { } public virtual void RegisterServices(IServiceCollection services, ToolManifest manifest) { } public virtual void RegisterSettingsPacks(IServiceCollection services, ToolManifest manifest) { } public virtual void RegisterHooks(ToolRegistry registry, ToolManifest manifest) { } } public class MyToolModule : ToolModule { public override void RegisterServices(IServiceCollection services, ToolManifest manifest) { services.AddSingleton<IMyService, MyService>(); services.AddSingleton<IViewActivationTask, MyViewActivatedTask>(); } public override void RegisterHooks(ToolRegistry registry, ToolManifest manifest) { registry.RegisterHook<IHookLifecycle, MyContextualRibbonInjector>(); } } ToolRegistry The registry of tool registrations and hook handlers. Command execution reads registration metadata through CommandPreflight; hook hosting resolves hook implementations through HookCatalog. public sealed class ToolRegistry { public ReadOnlyCollection<ToolRegistration> Tools { get; } public bool HasHookRegistrations { get; } public IReadOnlyDictionary<Type, IReadOnlyCollection<Type>> HookRegistrations { get; } public void RegisterTool(ToolRegistration registration); public ToolRegistration ResolveCommandRegistration(Type commandType); public void RegisterHook<THook, TImplementation>() where THook : class where TImplementation : class, THook; public void RegisterHook(Type hookType, Type implementation); public void MergeFrom(ToolRegistry source); } App owns assembly loading and the validation of command and availability types. With the concrete types resolved, ToolRegistration.FromManifest(...) builds the registration and the registry accepts it. ToolRegistration and ToolRibbonSpec public sealed class ToolRegistration { public Type CommandType { get; } public Type? AvailabilityType { get; } public AppRunScopeProfile ExecutionProfile { get; } // manifest RunProfile; default InlineUi public ToolRibbonSpec Ribbon { get; } public static ToolRegistration FromManifest(Type commandType, ToolManifest manifest, RibbonToolManifest tool, Type? availabilityType = null); } ToolRibbonSpec is the Revit-free ribbon metadata that App ribbon composition consumes. FromManifest(...) is the only place that holds both the tool manifest and the ribbon manifest. It selects the internal ToolRibbonSpec.CreatePushButton(...) or CreateGroupedControl(...) factory and keeps the manifest display text and group metadata. A push control cannot carry group fields; a grouped control requires a non-push control kind and a non-blank split-group identity. Hooks Supported hook types: ViewActivationHook: the Core dispatcher for view-activated work, run by IViewActivationTask services. IHookLifecycle: module-owned lifecycle work, such as contextual ribbon setup or dialog-showing event subscriptions. internal sealed class HookHost { internal Task AttachAsync(UIControlledApplication application, CancellationToken ct); internal Task RollbackAttachAsync(CancellationToken ct); internal void Detach(); } IHookLifecycle defines asynchronous initialization, asynchronous rollback after an attach failure and synchronous shutdown at the application boundary. Shutdown has no cancellation token or task; HookShutdownAction holds a plain Action. HookCatalog owns the supported-hook policy and resolves handlers from DI through that contract only. HookHost adds its own ViewActivated subscription as the last HookAttachAction, queues subscription and the unsubscription after an attach failure through the call gate, and publishes the attached state only after the whole attach succeeds. HookLifecycleCoordinator keeps the attach actions that initialized successfully, rolls them back in reverse order after a later attach failure and runs their shutdown actions in reverse initialization order. Normal detach clears that ownership only after every action succeeds; after a failure the complete, idempotent action set stays available for retry. Each lifecycle implementation cleans up its own resources when its initialization fails after it acquired them. ViewActivationHookDispatcher owns the safe-executor dispatch policy for this high-frequency event. ViewActivationHook keeps a runtime-failure gate per task and per document. The gate keys on DocumentSessionKey (title, path and instance hash): a reopened model starts clean, and after Save As or the first save of a new model the task can run once more under the new key. Dialog Suppression records ownership immediately after its adapter subscribes and calls its unsubscribe path if later initialization fails. Contextual ribbon: Initialization cleanup runs in the queued initialization context. It attempts the selection detach, every contextual UI removal and the edit-event disposal, and keeps both the initialization and the cleanup failures. Each registration keeps its tab, panel and button, and whether the injection created the panel or only the button. Cleanup removes a panel only when it owns it; a reused panel loses only the created button. A foreign button with the same ID, and its handler, are kept. The injection registry removes only registrations that cleaned up successfully, keeps failed ones for retry and throws one aggregate after it attempts them all. Injection and button-state sweeps attempt every target, keep the original causes with their tab, panel and button, and throw one aggregate after the sweep. The selection controller keeps the exact detach action captured at subscription, so shutdown needs no new UIApplication. The selection refresh completion callback runs only after all injection, toggle or cleanup changes succeed. OnEvaluateAndToggleCompleted is an extension point of ContextualRibbonInjector; ERFT overrides it. Sources: src/DBTools.Core/Tools/Hooks/{Lifecycle,Host,ContextualRibbon}/, src/Tools/Services/DialogSuppression/Features/DialogSuppressionHook.cs. UI components Windows Presentation (DBTools.Presentation.Windows) owns the stable window surface: WPF Window inheritance, owner-handle support through IWindowOwnerHandleTarget and the IThemeOptOut contract. public class ModalWindow : Window, IWindowOwnerHandleTarget, IThemeOptOut { public IWindowOwnerHandleProvider? OwnerHandleProvider { get; set; } public bool UseDefaultTheme { get; set; } } public class ModelessWindow : Window, IWindowOwnerHandleTarget, IThemeOptOut { /* same members */ } ToolWindowHost constructs the stable shell. Core's ToolWindowFactory installs the owner, theme, icon, error boundary and progress lifecycle before the raw view loads; for a modeless window the session's shell initializer selects the modeless owner policy. Retiring the session releases all of it. Settings, Alert, Logger and notification banners are raw views hosted by ToolWindowSession. ToolWindowFactory registers modal Settings and Alert sessions and modeless Logger sessions in the window registry. The banner host registry retires its modeless sessions when banners close or reset. Sandbox previews load the same raw resources with manifest-declared design-time view models. ToolWindowRegistry.RetireAll retires child sessions first, then each session's registered cleanups, then closes the shell. App shutdown calls it before other runtime owners reset. Window error boundary DBTools.Core.UI.Windows.ErrorBoundary holds the window error workflow. WindowStaticRuntime.Configure(...) is the one composition point where App startup supplies the banner notifier. The runtime receives IWindowErrorLogSurface and IWindowErrorBanner, so boundaries can surface the logger window and show handled-error banners without depending on the concrete shells. WindowErrorBoundaryRegistry owns one exception subscription per dispatcher. It routes each failure to the most recently activated attached window, then through activation history, then the attached list, skipping windows that have closed. WindowErrorBoundary classifies the original exception and every nested branch, including every aggregate branch. A branch is a DB Tools failure when its throwing method or a frame on its stack belongs to an assembly named exactly DBTools or starting with DBTools. (ordinal). Vendor code qualifies only as DBTools.HandyControl (the renamed HandyControl build) or DBTools.Presentation (which merges Helix). A raw HandyControl or HelixToolkit* assembly belongs to another add-in and never qualifies. A framework or Revit API failure raised from DB Tools code is therefore handled; another add-in's vendor failure is not. A bare DB Tools OperationCanceledException whose token was canceled is marked handled with a Warning log only: no banner and no handled-failure signal. The boundary presents and publishes the original outer exception, with its wrappers and causes, and returns the handled decision to the registry. An exception tree with no DB Tools branch stays unhandled and gets no notification. A window seen as closed keeps a weak tombstone and cannot be attached again. A closed WPF window that was never attached or seen is outside this registry; classifying it would need reflection or a new HWND. A lifecycle owner can subscribe through WindowErrorBoundaryRegistry to the handled-failure signal of its window. The subscription requires the attached per-window host and throws if it is missing. The notification carries the original failure and any presentation failure. Detaching clears the window's observers. WindowErrorPresenter owns the banner and logger-window show policy. WindowStaticRuntime configures and resets Core UI for App and Sandbox. It serializes the whole lifecycle and reports ready only after diagnostics, window error boundaries and progress overlays are all configured. It rejects duplicate or partial existing configuration before it changes anything. A failed configuration rolls back only what that attempt installed, in reverse order, so it can be retried; cleanup failures are kept with the primary failure. Reset attempts every Core UI cleanup step, clears readiness even when a step fails and reports cleanup failures in one aggregate. The progress-overlay capability owns its host registry and visual attachment, so this reset disposes every registered host. The progress capability exposes only a getter for the attached overlay-visibility state, so tool XAML can collapse airspace content. WindowRuntimeCapabilities.CreateSandbox(...) builds the Sandbox logger factory, logger, error-log surface, notification surface and a no-op progress capability inside the Core that owns the window interfaces. App startup configures its own notification, logging and progress capabilities. Sources: src/DBTools.Core/UI/Windows/Runtime/{WindowRuntimeCapabilities,WindowStaticRuntime}.cs, src/DBTools.Sandbox/Composition/AppRuntime.cs. Alerts public interface IAlertService { AlertResult Show(AlertRequest request); bool Confirm(string message, IWindowOwnerHandleProvider ownerHandleProvider, string title = "DB Tools"); T? SelectSingle<T>(AlertSelectionRequest<T> request) where T : class; IReadOnlyList<T> SelectMultiple<T>(AlertSelectionRequest<T> request) where T : class; } AlertServiceFactory and IAlertService are public. The internal AlertService, AlertBodyBuilder, AlertSelectionPolicy, AlertWindowPresenter and AlertWindowViewModel own request planning, body composition, selection, modal presentation and shell state. Confirm takes an IWindowOwnerHandleProvider; other alerts take owner and size policy in AlertWindowOptions. Implement IAlertBody for custom alert content. Alerts open with WindowStartupLocation.CenterScreen, which WPF centers on the work area of the owner's monitor in device pixels. An alert therefore opens on its owner's monitor (Revit or the DB Tools window that raised it) at any display scaling. WPF does not clamp the position, so an alert larger than the work area extends past it. Structural preview DBTools.Presentation.StructuralPreview.IStructuralPreview3D owns structural preview navigation and rendering. ERFT and SGT pass immutable scene and emphasis snapshots and consume stable pointer events. Core compiles against Presentation; the Helix and SharpDX assets are private to Presentation. Each tool registers the viewport's synchronous disposal as a session cleanup. ToolWindowRegistry.RetireAll releases the viewport handlers, timers, camera, material and device state and payload subscriptions before it closes the shell. See Structural Preview. Extension points Call gates: implement IRevitCallGate for another execution mode. Hooks: register IHookLifecycle implementations, or IViewActivationTask services for view-activated work. Settings packs: register packs with SettingsPackRegistration<TOptions, TContext>. Alert bodies: implement IAlertBody. Related pages Architecture Overview Project References DBTools.App

developer-guide/projects/presentation.ht.title: DBTools.Presentation | DB Tools
developer-guide/projects/presentation.ht.summary: DBTools.Presentation DBTools.Presentation.dll is the WPF assembly that stays loaded for the life of the Revit process. It is staged at the root of each product year, beside DBTools.dll, DBTools.Core.dll and DBTools.HandyControl.dll. Item Value Project src/DBTools.Presentation/DBTools.Presentation.csproj Assembly DBTools.Presentation.dll Target framework net10.0-windows (Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) and Revit 2027) References WPF, DBTools.HandyControl; Helix, Serilog and the logging and DI abstractions are merged in Contents Presentation holds only types that must live for the whole process: theme dictionaries, resource keys, styles, converters and pack resources; controls whose code-behind is limited to binding, dependency-property, routed-event, input and lifecycle mechanics; the ModalWindow and ModelessWindow base types with their owner-handle contracts, and the tool window shells ToolWindowModalShell and ToolWindowModelessShell; tool-specific behaviors, converters and controls under Tools/<TOOL>/; the structural 3D viewport (see Structural Preview). Production source is under src/DBTools.Presentation, with namespaces DBTools.Presentation.* that follow the folder tree. The project also compiles four tool settings views linked from their tool folders; these keep their tool namespaces and do not make Presentation depend on the tool assemblies. Presentation does not reference DBTools.dll, Core, tool types, view models, commands, services or the Revit API. App, Core and the tools may reference Presentation. ColorPickerPopup exposes and binds dependency properties by property path, and popup dismissal updates the stable IsPopupOpen property. ProgressOverlayControl binds to the command that the host supplies. Tool windows Tool views are raw embedded XAML. ToolWindowHost creates a modal or modeless shell, parses the view inside ToolWindowReflectionScope and sets the tool's view model. Core's ToolWindowFactory runs WindowInitializer on the shell first, which installs owner, theme, progress and error handling, and then registers the session. Hosts call session.ShowDialog() or session.Show() and get named controls with session.Require<T>(name). When a session closes or is retired, Presentation tears down bindings, automation roots, resources and callbacks. See Theme System. UI Automation item lifetime Retirement does not clear cached automation peers. In WPF 10.0.0, item peers hold reference-type rows weakly (ItemAutomationPeer._item uses ItemWeakReference, and DataGridCellItemAutomationPeer._item is weak), and teardown cuts the strong column, row-item and DataContext references. Tool items in a DataGrid, ListBox or TreeView, their types and a collectible tool context can therefore be released after retirement, also while a UI Automation client is attached. Rows are held strongly, and a collectible tool assembly stays loaded, in these cases: the first item cached by a peer store has an unreliable hash code (for example ComponentResourceKey); the store switches to list mode and holds every later key strongly; the items are boxed value types; the ItemAutomationPeerKeepsItsItemAlive switch makes _item strong; a UI Automation client holds an item element, which keeps its control alive through ElementProxy._peer. Enumerating ItemPeersStorage or _WeakRefElementProxyStorage materializes the weak keys, so their contents do not show an owning reference. Resource URIs /DBTools.Presentation;V<PresentationVersion>;component/Resources/Theme.xaml Raw and reloadable XAML declares stable namespaces with assembly=DBTools.Presentation. XAML compiled inside Presentation uses the form without assembly=. See Theme System for URI rules and Assembly Loading Contract for the distribution layout.

developer-guide/projects/sandbox.html.title: DBTools.Sandbox | DB Tools
developer-guide/projects/sandbox.html.summary: DBTools.Sandbox DBTools.Sandbox is a standalone executable that validates one product year and hosts tool windows for UI development without Revit. It targets net10.0-windows for Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) and Revit 2027; build/Distribution/RevitYearContract.cs defines the supported years. Source layout Path Contents App/Startup/ SandboxEntry (BCL-only entry point), CLIOptions, SandboxCandidate, the SandboxMode enum (Interactive, Headless) App/ The WPF application Composition/ Sandbox runtime services and SandboxWindowFactory Features/WindowCatalog/ The window catalog shown in interactive mode Runtime/ Sandbox logging and window runtime configuration Validation/ Candidate, manifest, metadata and window validators Tests/ DBTools.Sandbox.Pure.Tests Runtime Sandbox starts a new default-context process for each candidate year. The entry point checks the year directory before any Core, Presentation or WPF type loads, loads the candidate's top-level assemblies and Tools/ assemblies from their paths, and then starts WPF. The candidate files are the only product assemblies in the process; the project compiles against Core, Presentation and HandyControl without copying their runtime files. Sandbox reads window specifications from the tool manifests through Core's SandboxCatalog and hosts them in the stable Presentation window shells. At startup it calls DBTools.Core.Sandbox.SandboxMode.Activate, so SandboxMode.IsActive is true in this process; tool code checks it to avoid Revit-only services. Building real windows and checking their cleanup requires the Windows process. For the options, the validation steps and the manifest rules, see Sandbox Validator. See also Sandbox Integration and Assembly Loading Contract.

developer-guide/tools/common/elevation-t.title: Elevation Tags | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/common/elevation-t.summary: Elevation Tags Overview Elevation Tags aligns spot elevation text relative to leader endpoints in floor, structural, and ceiling plans. Manual alignment runs on the active view. Automatic alignment runs when a supported view activates. Architecture Ownership and registration Source: src/Tools/Structural/ElevationTags/. The manifest places the tool on the Common panel. Owner Responsibility App/Composition/ElevationTagsCommand Ribbon entry point and active-view availability App/Composition/ElevationTagsToolModule Settings and pack registration App/Composition/ServiceCollectionExtensions Feature registration App/Composition/SettingsPackContextFactory Settings context and live type snapshots Features/AlignElevationTagsWorkflow Manual validation and completion toasts Features/ViewActivatedTask Supported-view automatic execution Features/ElevationTagsUpdater Shared inline call gate, transaction runner, and updater construction Features/AutoUpdater Filtering, layout, mutation, and counts Features/SpotElevationSymbolResolver Spot marker-symbol resolution Features/SpotElevationTypeProjector Live type snapshots for settings Settings/SettingsPackContext Pattern, type, and preview wiring and validation Settings/PatternContext Core RegexPatternListContext adapter Settings/TypeContext, TypeSelection Type filtering, navigation, and offsets Settings/PreviewContext Preview formatting and image state Settings/Views/ElevationTagsSettingsPackView.xaml Settings layout The assembly and tool ID are DBTools.ElevationTags. The module type is DBTools.ElevationTags.App.Composition.ElevationTagsToolModule. Command and availability both use DBTools.ElevationTags.App.Composition.ElevationTagsCommand. The button uses InlineUi, icon key align_elevation_tags, and order 20. The icon asset is Assets/align_elevation_tags_icon.png. Data and contracts Settings Settings use configuration section Tools.ElevationTags and pack key common.elevation_tags. Property Default Meaning AutoUpdateEnabled true Run on supported view activation TagNamePatterns Empty list Regex patterns. An empty or all-blank list uses the static defaults TypeOffsets Empty dictionary TypeAlignmentOffsets keyed by spot elevation type name The default pattern is: ^DB Elevation Tag - (?:Concrete|Steel|Wall) Label$ The UI permits up to three patterns and validates their syntax. At least one nonblank pattern is required to save settings. Runtime compiles nonblank patterns case-insensitively. Invalid patterns log warnings and are skipped. With no valid compiled patterns, no tags match. TypeAlignmentOffsets contains AlongLeaderOffset and PerpendicularOffset. Both default to zero for an unconfigured type. Runtime multiplies these values by view.Scale / 12. The signs follow the computed text side relative to the leader endpoint. Filtering AutoUpdater collects non-type OST_SpotElevations elements from the active view as SpotDimension instances. A match against any configured regex includes the spot. Candidate strings include the spot name, spot type and family names, and resolved marker-symbol type and family names. The matcher tests these strings separately. A failure reading a spot's names increments FailedCount. The first such failure in a run logs its exception. Leaderless spots, missing types, and Relative-base spots require no update. Results and errors AutoUpdater.Run() returns ElevationTagRunResult with: Field Meaning TotalSpotsInView Collected spots PatternMatches Spots accepted by name patterns UpdatedCount Spots whose position changed FailedCount Name-reading or per-spot update failures Candidate updates share DB Tools - Autoupdating spot elevations. The updater catches per-spot update faults, counts them, and continues. The first update fault logs its exception. Collection, layout preparation, and transaction-level failures can propagate. The manual workflow shows a Warning toast when failures exist, Success when tags change, and Info for no spots, no pattern matches, or matching spots requiring no changes. See Limitations for cases that require no position change. Automatic updates log a summary warning for partial failures. Uncaught automatic-update failures reach Core's view-activation handling, which shows a runtime-failure banner and skips that task for the document session. This runtime failure does not set a persistent settings warning. Warning core.structural.elevation_tags disables DBTools.AlignElevationTagsInView and automatic updates. The settings context exposes the warning state and disables its automatic-update toggle while the warning is active. Workflows Use Open a FloorPlan, EngineeringPlan, or CeilingPlan view. Configure Elevation Tags in Settings. Run Align Elevation Tags, or enable automatic updates. The command requires an active view. An unsupported view produces a warning toast without running alignment. The settings preview redraws as per-type offsets change. Alignment algorithm Read the origin, leader end, current text position, and spot type. Resolve elevation and format its text using document units and the type's unit options. Measure the text with GDI+ using font, text size, width scale, and display DPI. Compute placement relative to the leader end and current above/below text side. Apply the configured per-type offsets. Write TextPosition when X or Y differs after rounding to two decimal places in internal coordinates. Z remains the existing text Z. The view factor is view.Scale / 12. The measured horizontal half-width receives margins of 2 * factor / 128 + factor / 8. The vertical margin is factor / 64. Placement below the leader also accounts for measured text height. The elevation base uses the type's displayed SPOT_ELEV_BASE value: Display value Calculation Project Base Point Subtract project base point Z only when project and survey point positions differ by at least 1e-9 on an axis Relative Skip alignment Other values, including Survey Point Use spot origin Z An Elevation Indicator becomes the prefix only when Elevation Indicator as Prefix/Suffix equals Prefix and the indicator is nonblank. Otherwise the measured prefix is EL. . The calculation does not append a configured suffix. Font defaults to Arial and width scale defaults to 1 when their parameters are absent. A units-format lookup failure logs once and uses default formatting. Troubleshooting Symptom Check No matches Compare patterns with spot, type, family, and marker-symbol names Automatic updates absent Check the toggle, warning state, supported view type, and runtime log Matching spots unchanged Check leader presence, elevation base, and rounded position Partial alignment Inspect the first filtering or update exception in the DB Tools log Testing Pure tests cover the runner, symbol resolution, settings state, preview, and manual summaries. Revit-hosted tests under Tests/Integration/Revit/ cover the command, module, workflow, view activation, live updater, and type projection. See architecture and themes. Limitations Elevation-base and prefix comparisons require English display strings and use ordinal matching. No-change counts combine already aligned spots, leaderless spots, and spots with a Relative elevation base.

developer-guide/tools/common/gm-producti.title: GM Production Contracts | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/common/gm-producti.summary: GM Production Contracts These Global Mapper (GM) behaviors are performance or correctness requirements. Each section names the source that implements the contract and the effect of breaking it. A change to a contract is a product change; update this page with it. See Global Mapper for the tool design. Paths are relative to src/Tools/Common/GM/. Usage index sampling cap Features/Usage/Revit/Operations/Indexing/UsageIndexSource.Families.cs, QuerySampleInstanceIdsBySymbol The usage index samples one family instance per family type (symbol), at most 2500 instances (MaxSampleInstances in UsageIndexSource.cs). It streams view-independent (model) instances first and returns as soon as it has 2250 samples. Only when the model instances give fewer than 2250 samples does it add view-owned instances of the active view, up to the cap. Unbounded iteration scales with views times instances: a project with 200 views and 50,000 instances stalls for minutes. One geometry pass per usage kind Features/Usage/Revit/Operations/Indexing/StyleMaterial/UsageStyleMaterialCollector.cs, QueryStyleMaterialUsageChunk Style and material usage are captured from the same sample. Instance geometry is requested once for styles and once for materials, both with IncludeNonVisibleObjects = true. Symbol geometry is requested only when the instance has no geometry. Style geometry uses the owning or active view; material geometry uses view-independent Fine detail. Sharing one geometry result between them changes coverage. The combined chunk shares element lookup and the traversal of family-dependent styles. One instance for parameter discovery Features/Families/Revit/FamilyScanner.ParameterNames.cs, QueryMappableParamNamesForFamily Parameter-name discovery reads the parameters of every type of the family and of one instance. Parameter definitions are family-level, so every instance has the same definitions; scanning more instances adds cost and no data. Deep scan runs only on request Features/DeepScan/Workflow/DeepScanWorkflow.cs A deep scan opens family documents with EditFamily, which takes seconds per family. It runs only from a user action: Scan Family on a family row, deep scan of all visible families, or deep scan of unscanned families with zero instances (after a confirmation). Background prewarm only reads the deep scan cache; it never starts a scan. See GM specification. Parameter discovery filter Revit/ParameterDiscovery/ParameterDiscoveryEligibility.cs Discovery excludes read-only parameters, built-in parameters (InternalDefinition with a valid BuiltInParameter) and blank definition names. It does not filter on UserModifiable, because Revit can report a parameter that the API can write as not user-modifiable. Removing the read-only or built-in filter offers parameters that cannot be written or should not be mapped. Adding a UserModifiable filter hides valid mapping targets. Simple style canonicalization UsageStyleMaterialCollector.RecordStyle; Features/Usage/Revit/Operations/Indexing/UsageIndexSource.StyleMaterial.cs, BuildStyleCanonicalizationMap Style usage records the raw style ID and its canonical projection ID only. Recording every equivalent alias multiplies dictionary insertions per geometry object without improving the result. Style maps built once per usage build UsageIndexSource.StyleMaterial.cs, BuildStyleMaterialUsageAsync Style canonicalization, category projection and object-style classification run once per usage build, and their results are passed to each chunk of 25 instances (UsageChunkSize). Rebuilding them per chunk repeats a full FilteredElementCollector scan for every chunk.
