developer-guide/tools/common/gm-spec.htm.summary: Global Mapper architecture specification Overview Global Mapper (GM) collects Revit content, builds mapping intent, and executes reviewed replacement plans. This specification describes its state, execution, persistence, and lifetime contracts. Source: src/Tools/Common/GM/. GM describes entry points and test surfaces. Architecture Composition and document scope App/Composition/Revit/GmModelessSessionFactory captures the launch UIDocument and Document, creates a QueuedModeless App run scope, and binds its concrete GmSessionDocumentGate once before resolving modeless work. The gate compares ordinal DocumentSessionKey values on each callback. The key uses the document hash code for session scoping. It does not guarantee collision-free identity. The persistence key is the nonblank document path, or that captured session key for an unsaved document. Unsaved documents load saved data only under their captured session key. AddGm() registers the concrete GM gate without replacing shared IRevitCallGate registrations. GM Revit readers, writers, family batches, transaction runners, and Commit Review consume the concrete gate. RevitMappingPlanExecutor rejects an invalid document or session-key mismatch before writers begin. RunCleanupAsync uses the underlying gate with CancellationToken.None so owned documents can close after authority or work cancellation ends. Commit Review uses the bound parent gate to create an InlineUi child scope. It binds the child gate once to the expected document before running apply services. One outer Revit callback contains planning, modal review, apply, finalization, and refresh. During that modal session, forced-queue, off-thread, or second-callback work is refused. AppSessionProjectionBuilder receives a host-neutral MappingProjectionContext, workspace/dialog state, a required IViewOps implementation, and feature services. The runtime wraps that same projection in MappingExecutionContext with its ExpectedDocument. The bound gate carries the session authorization key. Host-neutral panes and rows receive the projection context. Commit Review receives the execution context. Authorization identity and persistence identity have separate consumers. WindowSessionServices supplies the attached owner and progress overlay. ErrorNotifierFactory uses that owner. GmWindowAttachment supplies feature dialogs with a late-bound getter for the attached window. Design-time composition uses explicit host-neutral collaborators, including DesignTimeViewOps. AppSessionBuilder constructs startup, initialization, Deep Scan, preference clearing, background prewarm, Family Mapping commands, pane lifecycle, and disposal workflows. RowRefreshFactory builds one row collaboration graph per session. Its outputs include CrossPaneRowRefresh, RowRefreshCoreServices, CommitReviewRowServices, UIStateFactory, and OptionRenderingRefresh. App/Sessions/RowRefresh/CrossPaneRowRefresh sequences Usage rows, Family Mapping refresh, selected-family state, indicators, live-update suppression, row locks, and workspace events. It implements feature-owned ICommitReviewRowRefresh, IFamilyMappingCrossPaneCommands, and IDeepScanUsageRefresh. FilterRefreshWorkflow, StartupRowWorkflow, and PageActivationWorkflow consume that runtime. App/Sessions owns session records and runtime lifetime. Composition owns construction. Feature implementations do not import DBTools.GM.App. FamilyMappingFactory returns FamilyMappingViewModel, FamilyMappingScanWorkflow, FamilyMappingRowRefresh, FamilyMappingTypeCreation, and one MappingRowSet spanning family/type and supplied Usage rows. FamilyMappingScanStateApplier belongs to scan sequencing. The row builders and refresh owners receive the same row set. Public surface and resources GM production payload types default to internal. Manifest activation requires public GmToolModule and GmCommand. Public conflict projection values retain their public binding properties. Dependency objects, converters, selectors, and attached behaviors are stable public Presentation types. The design-time view models are internal with public binding/fragment properties. Sandbox and production consume the same raw resources and fragments. Compiled resource validation checks manifest logical names. Source reference Paths below are relative to src/Tools/Common/GM/. Contract Source Launch and document gate App/Composition/Revit/GmModelessSessionFactory.cs, Revit/Document/GmSessionDocumentGate.cs Session graph App/Composition/Revit/AppSessionBuilder.cs, App/Composition/AppSessionProjectionBuilder.cs, App/Composition/RowRefresh/RowRefreshFactory.cs Modeless lifetime App/Sessions/Revit/GmModelessSession.cs, App/Sessions/SessionOperationGate.cs State and names Domain/ProjectState/ProjectStateStore.cs, Domain/ElementNames/ElementNamesCache.cs Persistence App/Persistence/StatePersistence.cs, App/Persistence/UIStateLifecycle.cs, App/Persistence/UIStateCache.cs Scan admission Features/DeepScan/DeepScanOrchestrator.cs, Features/DeepScan/Refresh/DeepScanRefreshWorkflow.cs Usage publication Features/Usage/Index/UsageIndexLoader.cs, Features/Usage/Index/UsageIndexSnapshotBuilder.cs, Features/Usage/Index/UsageMatchIndex.cs Options and similarity Features/Mapping/State/MappingOptionCache.cs, Features/Similarity/Naming/NamingSimilarity.cs Execution Features/Mapping/Domain/Execution/MappingPlanExecutor.cs, Features/Mapping/Domain/Execution/MappingApplyResultBuilder.cs, Features/Mapping/Revit/Execution/Batch/FamilyBatchExecutor.cs Review Features/CommitReview/Workflow/CommitReviewApplyWorkflow.cs, Features/CommitReview/Workflow/CommitReviewFinalizer.cs Intent identity Features/Mapping/Domain/MappingIntent/MappingIntentKey.cs, Features/Mapping/Domain/MappingIntent/MappingIntentStore.cs Data and contracts Domain and feature contracts Project state Domain/ProjectState owns ProjectState, family/type records, reference index/values, project parameters, scan state, projection, and the scoped ProjectStateStore. The store imports no feature or App namespace. CurrentProjectState and CurrentProjectStateCategoryId identify the loaded snapshot and its category in one replacement operation. IProjectStateBuilder and ProjectStateBuildRequest are inward contracts. App/State/ProjectStateBuilder queries Families, Usage, Shared Parameters, and Previews and projects their results into those values. Family-only refresh retains loaded Usage and Shared Parameters sections and invalidates derived usage caches before preparing rows. A failed build preserves published state. Commit Review planning builds the selected category plus pending-intent owner families without publishing. CarryForwardInto supplies loaded sections and unchanged-family Deep Scan evidence to that planning state. Duplicate detection also stays unpublished. CarryDeepScanEvidenceInto supplies only unchanged-family evidence to its fresh full state. The ProjectStateStore retains evidence across category-filtered state replacement. A rebuild restores it only when the family's type set and per-type instance counts remain unchanged. After commit, ReplaceProjectStateAfterCommit discards directly changed families and containing ancestors across all categories. Direct changes include mapped/owning families, families of mapped types, and material/object-style families found by AffectedFamilyResolver. Commit Review planning uses that same resolver. Its plan context owns planning identity and evidence. Discarding evidence removes scan state, type payloads, DeepScanResults, and fast parameter discovery together. Element names and categories Domain/ElementNames owns IElementNameQuery, ElementNamesCache, and ElementNameLookupKind. Revit/ElementName/ElementNameQuery implements the Revit adapter. App registers it with state/cache wiring. Categories registers curated-category services. Strict name loading requires a nonblank cached name for every requested ID. Blank entries are queried again. Omitted/blank provider values stay unresolved. GetResolvedFamilyName prefers cache, then project-state family name, and throws if neither exists. Display getters retain explicit ID/unavailable-name fallbacks. WorkspaceState.SelectedCategory is the single typed CategoryOption value exposed by IWorkspaceState. CategoryFilter derives its display label. Null and Id zero select every family. Other signed IDs select exactly that category, including negative built-in Revit IDs. Both IFamilyQuery methods use those rules. GetFamiliesAsync reuses state only when category identity matches, families exist, and all family names are nonblank. It still filters the reused result by the requested category. WorkspaceState.SortMode uses MatchingOptionSortMode through mutation, persistence, restoration, and option projection. CurrentProjectStateCategoryId identifies loaded state. FamilyMappingState.AppliedCategoryId identifies applied rows. Applying a different category resets category-scoped rows before application and records the category only after rows apply. Cancellation between state publication and row application therefore causes a reset on retry. Mapping intent, rows, and conflicts Features/Mapping/Domain owns immutable intent, conflict, operation, plan, and host-free execution values. It does not import mutable Rows types. MappingIntentKey validates its nine-field shape through named factories and FromPersisted. It rejects invalid zero identities while retaining signed category IDs such as -2000011. The Rows package owns row-to-intent translation, projection, origin mutation, and family-apply behavior. Conflict/Rows owns row conflict matching. Detection consumes an immutable MappingSelectionSnapshot. MappingConflictWorkflow hydrates returned MappingIntentKey values into loaded rows. MappingConflictTarget defines three closed variants: a positive element selection, a type-parameter policy, or a display-only message. Resolution chooses an original side or an explicit MappingConflictBulkAction. Display labels and sentinel IDs do not encode executable policy. Duplicates implements Mapping-owned neutral selection/resolution contracts without exporting its own selection types. Mapping owns projection/execution contexts, row signals, navigation values/lifetimes, MappingUpdateSuppression, and OriginClearSuppression. Mapping Domain/Planning owns nested-family, style, and type-reference plan language. Commit Review's CommitReviewDocumentEditBuilder owns mutable family-batch assembly. Mapping's neutral composition registers MappingIntentStore. Commit Review composition registers CommitReviewPlanVerifier. Revit/Composition registers mutation adapters, attached by App's AddGm root. Shared Parameters implements Mapping's focused embed port and uses Mapping operation identities. Domain/Parameters/FamilyParameterDiscoveryResult carries normalized ScopedParameterName values, complete/partial state, and contextual read errors. Family Mapping and Shared Parameters publish choices only from complete discovery. Duplicate parameter scoring requires complete discovery on both sides. Instance/Type suffixes are display labels. Parameter mappings retain scope and require equal source/target scope. Element identities Revit family, type, instance, material, style, view, and category IDs use long. Revit boundaries use ElementIdConverter.ToLong and FromLong. Saved-mapping and UI-state JSON accept integer-valued number tokens, including values in the 32-bit range. Family-document materials resolve by name rather than host numeric ID. Counts, indexes, depths, enum/order casts, synthetic duplicate group IDs, SharedParameterDuplicateMatcher sequence IDs, and MappingOption.StableStringId hashes use int. SharedParameterValueCopier rejects Map From values outside Int32 for Revit Integer storage. ElementId parameter destinations parse Map From text as long. Persistence and saved mappings Domain/Cache owns tool-wide cache paths, metadata, and recovery policy. App/Persistence owns document UI-state storage and session persistence sequencing. StatePersistence requires both IUIStateCache and ISavedMappingStore in production. Design-time projection does not construct unused persistence. JSON writes flush a unique sibling temporary file and publish it atomically. Cancellation or I/O failure preserves the last good snapshot. Only confirmed missing files/directories count as absent. Access, sharing, invalid-path, and other I/O faults propagate. UI-state and Deep Scan snapshots are disposable caches: malformed, invalid, or old snapshots are discarded and logged. Saved mappings are user data and use strict nullable-ingress validation with contextual failures. Cache results are immutable hit/miss values. Hits always contain data. IUIStateCache serializes asynchronous writes and clears across scoped instances with a process-wide mutation gate. StatePersistence serializes document loads, clears, and saves and tracks separate UI-state/saved-mapping clear generations. An older open session cannot restore either snapshot after another window clears it. A freshly loaded window can persist new state. UIStateLifecycle attempts enabled close writes independently, retains failures in write order, and resets one-shot suppression even on failure. Confirmed clears drain before close persistence and disposal. PaneStateProjector supplies SavedAt. Saving preserves the supplied timestamp. Saved Mappings validates exact document identity and every persisted key before admission. Parameter mappings retain ScopedParameterName scope. The persistence port exposes load, save, and clear. MappingIntentStore owns merging. Commit Review constructs the restore workflow, merges persisted intent, and reapplies through row owners. Clearing saved mappings follows this order: Remove saved origins/selections from loaded rows. Clear mapping intent, duplicate intent, and the in-memory persisted list. Clear storage. Run the required App-bound refreshRowsAfterSavedMappingClear operation. CrossPaneRowRefresh rebuilds loaded Usage rows, refreshes Family Mapping rows, reconciles indicators under suppression, releases suppression, refreshes locks, and publishes cache status. Reapply calls Usage, FamilyMappingRowRefresh, Shared Parameters, and row locks directly. Option cache and similarity MappingOptionCache keys candidates by mapping kind, source ID, category, ordered target ID/name pairs, and source label. Category lookup does not fall back to general entries. Prewarm uses the same identity. Candidate snapshots use private read-only lists, so replacing entries cannot mutate earlier results. NamingSimilarity.Normalize and numeric-suffix stem comparison retain letters/digits in invariant lowercase. Numeric-suffix siblings with equal cleaned stems score 1.0 before Dice evaluation. Dice uses lowercased raw-name bigrams, including punctuation and whitespace, with multiplicities. Its score is twice the multiset intersection divided by the sum of raw lengths minus two. For a raw length below two, equal raw lengths score 1.0 only with equal nonempty cleaned stems. Other short-name pairs score zero. Each scoring pass owns its immutable name-profile cache. Deep Scan Deep Scan owns family scans, projection, usage resolution, feature cache, and refresh workflow. A user scan collects a complete family batch and finishes cache preparation before one validated ApplyBatch admission. Usage refresh data is prepared before completed scan state publishes. Cancellation or required failure before admission preserves the prior projection. Host lookup completeness is separate for styles, materials, and families. An item failure marks only its domain incomplete and prevents partial singleton-name resolution or resolver-cache reuse. Other complete requested domains remain usable. Affected families retain warning diagnostics and incomplete usage. Unexpected collector/category traversal failures abort construction. Partial parameter discovery invalidates fast choices, is omitted from duplicate scoring, and removes prior reusable cache entries before admission. A later complete query can repopulate choices. Partial usage remains visible but cannot become reusable complete cache data. DeepScanCacheCoordinator removes prior reusable entries for incomplete parameter discovery or usage scans before admission. Failure to resolve a removal identity or remove an entry propagates and prevents admission. A cache write failure without required removals logs a warning. Cache operations use a local persistence gate plus an exclusive per-file process lock. Each batch reloads authoritative disk state once while holding both. Startup hydration reads eligible families against one load. User scan removes/writes its family batch with one load and one atomic save. This serializes owners across Revit processes. Disposal drains persistence before releasing the DI-root owner. Snapshot admission validates entries and parameter/usage completeness flags as a whole. It discards incompatible snapshots rather than salvaging entries. Clear Cache holds a session-lifetime registration through deletion, projection/UI refresh, and completion. It shares session-operation admission with scans. Shutdown drains it before disposing collaborators. A confirmed clear increments DeepScanOrchestrator's generation after disk deletion and before projection clearing. Hydration rejects its whole candidate batch if that generation changes or the captured ProjectState reference changes during reading. It never replaces an already completed family scan. CrossPaneRowRefresh implements IDeepScanUsageRefresh: apply Usage data, rebuild loaded rows when needed, reconcile Family Mapping state/indicators under suppression, then refresh locks. DeepScanRefreshWorkflow invalidates options and awaits the App-bound Shared Parameters authoring rebuild. That rebuild evicts authoring snapshots and rebuilds the loaded tree with pending intent and selection. Completion events describe changed cache state and publish even when rebuilding faults or cancels. The outcome then propagates to the operation boundary. Eligible-cache hydration finishes only after its queued UI refresh runs. AuthoringRebuildWorkflow serializes rebuild and application. If evidence invalidates during a build, including the first build, it builds again before applying. Disposal cancels held/queued rebuilds and prevents later application. Duplicates The Duplicates feature owns detection, selections, rows, resolution, tree, pane state, and type mapping. Detection/DuplicateDetectionEngine calls the family, style, material, and shared-parameter matchers, assigns aggregate group IDs, and returns DuplicateDetectionResult. The feature's Domain, Selection, Rows, Resolution, Tree, Pane, and TypeMapping folders own their respective contracts and behavior. SharedParameterDuplicateMatcher lives beside family/style/material matchers under Detection/Matching. CurrentDuplicateDetection owns the last fully completed artifact. Detection collects its unpublished full state, executes stable DuplicateKind stages, hydrates names, then publishes and returns the same artifact reference. Earlier failure/cancellation preserves the prior artifact. Family-row counts use that same detection state. The immediate rebuild receives the artifact explicitly. Other readers inject CurrentDuplicateDetection. Cached refresh waits for cross-dispatcher rebuilds. A reentrant request replaces the queued request. The outer refresh runs the latest queued rebuild before returning, including propagating its failure. PreviewDuplicateMatcher matches style/material candidates only when both resolve to the same signature. Unavailable previews never match, including each other. Duplicates imports neither Shared Parameters nor Commit Review. Families and Family Mapping Families' neutral composition registers FamilyQuery and IFamilyQuery. Its Revit composition registers FamilyDocumentService, FamilyScanner, and scanner ports. FamilyDocumentService owns document lifecycle/query, not Mapping material preparation. Families consumes its own IFamilyInstanceCountQuery, implemented by Usage's live source. A thrown Document.Close or false result is a cleanup failure under the shared strict close policy. FamilyMappingViewModel owns binding state and interactions. FamilyMappingScanWorkflow owns asynchronous scan/cache/post-commit sequencing and its private scan-state applier. FamilyMappingRowRefresh owns symbol projection, row build/refresh, saved-mapping reapply, and usage reconciliation. Ordinary category navigation reuses a category snapshot or matching loaded state. RescanFamiliesAfterCommitAsync discards every category snapshot and rebuilds from the document, including when category identity stays unchanged, so newly created types reach rows. App's CrossPaneRowRefresh sequences cross-pane work. Usage Usage owns indexing, matching/options, preview cache/versioning, rows, selection, traversal, and pane state. AppSessionProjectionBuilder constructs one UsageIndexLoader and FamilyUsage after session state, names, and operation gate exist. The loader retains those collaborators. It is not a context-free service. RebuildPlanningUsageIfNeededAsync returns Task and builds only a missing index when usage intent exists. RebuildUsageAfterCommitIfNeededAsync returns true only when it builds the index. UsageIndexSnapshotBuilder starts and drains five catalog/index tasks, aggregates non-cancellation faults, and creates an unpublished candidate without touching the match index. Name resolution, project-state usage storage, and Deep Scan refresh preparation precede publication. Index publication aligns the match index, target universe, hydration generation, and option cache. UsageMatchIndex shares one in-flight family hydration among concurrent callers. An index publication invalidates hydration started against the prior generation. UsageIndexPublished runs synchronously on the publishing thread, including workers. RowRefreshPublicationWiring dispatches row projection to the UI thread. Rows track publication version. Detect suppresses publication-driven duplicate rebuild and rebuilds once after scanning, retaining the keep target. Passive option projection suppresses intent capture. An unavailable saved target remains disabled for review. An explicit edit can clear or replace it. UsageViewModel owns target selection and bound collection/preview mutation. Selection-family flow performs one family lookup, name hydration, and row population. UsagePreviewService owns calculation, caching, and request-version order. UsageWorkflow consumes IUsageIndexLoader and its own rows without App/Family Mapping imports or row locks. App PageActivationWorkflow suppresses live-plan updates across loading, reconciliation, and indicators, then refreshes locks and cache state after suppression. Shared Parameters and UI execution Shared Parameters owns domain values, authoring, formulas, Revit adapters, rows, tree, views, and pane state. SharedParameterDuplicateReconciler owns stateful duplicate-row mutation and reentrancy. SharedParameterConflictProjector performs stateless tree/Commit Review projection. Map From reads numeric formula inputs at the Revit boundary. The preview evaluator does not parse displayed parameter text. Measured values use Revit's display unit. Preview output uses 15 significant digits. Numeric preview accepts signed/unsigned E/e exponents, including substituted invariant G15 values. Unresolved identifiers/functions produce preview-unavailable. Revit still validates authored formulas. Formula mode returns zero from the value copier without target resolution or writes. The embed applier counts authored formulas separately from value updates: one formula has authored=1, updated=0, affected=1. MapFrom retains copied-value counts. Detached Usage selection-preview and authoring property notifications use ISafeExecutor.RunWithoutThrowingAsync. The shared boundary owns logging/banners without rethrowing into WPF dispatch. Shared-parameter group/category/authoring work and contested overlay admission retain the UI context before collection mutation. Preview failures propagate to their owning command/tree-selection boundary for one report. Commit Review planning and continuation Commit Review planning resolves names, builds planning state, loads parameter groups, and prepares rows/usage inside one ISessionOperationGate operation. Collaborators do not reacquire that non-reentrant gate. The gate releases before the review dialog opens. Refresh takes a separate operation. Planning cancellation remains control flow. Other faults can produce invalid-plan state. Commit Review receives closing state and MappingSessionContext with IWorkspaceState rather than mutable App state. Planning/DocumentEdit owns mutable batch assembly. Report/OperationRows/OperationRowProjector produces family, pending, result, and error rows. Workflow owns apply/finalization. Revit/CommitReviewSessionFactory composes the child scope, planning, transaction groups, and modal presenter through the bound document gate. CommitReviewRowServices is feature-owned and constructed by App's row composition. Commit continuation uses ICommitReviewRowRefresh, implemented by CrossPaneRowRefresh. It returns Refreshed, Canceled, or NoSelectedCategory. Only a successful family scan proceeds to usage preparation, family reconciliation, and row locks. Canceled stops through cancellation. NoSelectedCategory skips refresh without a success log. Committed mappings remain persisted in either case. The refresh workflow consumes ISessionOperationGate for busy state. Commit-and-continue invalidates authoring snapshots, duplicates, and cached family views before rescanning. Returned outcomes rebuild the applied Shared Parameters tree. A successful continuation rescans Duplicates immediately when that page is active. View operations and catalogs ViewOps owns navigation. A positive missing element ID returns false without changing view or selection. Nonpositive IDs are argument errors. Unexpected Revit faults propagate. Previews owns cross-feature material/style catalogs and preview values. Line-style eligibility The shared line-style query checks the capability required by Revit commit. A grouped curve is restylable only when its group and every enclosing group have exactly one placed instance of their type. Attached detail groups also check their parent model group. Multi-instance groups are excluded before capture with their type name, placed count and Edit Group reason. GM never enters Edit Group mode and never ungroups elements. A style used only by those excluded members has no selectable source targets, even when the style remains available as a target for other sources. The writer captures every pair's population before the first pair mutates the document. Curves with no alternate Lines projection style, no resolvable projection or a non-Lines current style are also excluded. The query retains scalar curve IDs and per-source target intersections for restylable curves. It does not retain Revit wrappers for excluded members, and readback never revisits them. Each successful pair's affected count equals its pre-apply Usage quantity. A defensive group-edit failure at commit rolls back only that pair and surfaces the reason. Workflows Session operations and shutdown Domain/SessionOperation/ISessionOperationGate exposes serialized work, overlay progress, busy state, and UI cancellation. App/Sessions/SessionOperationGate implements admission and cancel-and-drain. MappingUpdateSuppression separately controls nested live-plan suppression. SessionOperationProgress carries operation progress or the Hidden no-display value. The Domain/Workspace IWorkspaceSignals port carries feature requests for whole-window refresh. App/Sessions/WorkspaceSignals implements that port, alongside WorkspaceState implementing IWorkspaceState. An operation failure remains primary. Caller cancellation propagated through the linked work token is translated back to the caller token. Teardown independently attempts stopped-step logging, busy-state reset, and busy-text reset. The resets run directly or in one dispatcher call. An aborted or unscheduled dispatcher call produces one teardown failure. The linked cancellation source is always released. One failure propagates unchanged. Multiple failures aggregate in primary-first order with contextual teardown wrappers. A failing StateChanged subscriber cannot hide the work failure or skip the other reset. BackgroundPrewarm and OptionRenderingRefresh retain their transitive task and cancellation source. Replacement cancels and drains the active pair before starting the next. The session refuses ordinary close while Commit Review or Type Mapping owns an interaction. The first admitted close publishes closing state, cancels Mapping/startup, observes startup, and retains one terminal shutdown task. Repeated closes join that completion. The shutdown workflow independently attempts prewarm drain, option-rendering drain, confirmed preference-clear drain, session-operation cancel-and-drain, close persistence, and synchronous graph disposal, in that order. It then issues one terminal Close. Closed performs idempotent view-model cleanup and App run-scope disposal. Failures retain lifecycle order and do not skip later cleanup. Pane and scope collaborators remain alive until running work drains. Dev Mode retirement is synchronous and requires Idle for immediate collection. Commit Review reports Busy, so reload waits for Keep, Roll back, X, or cancellation followed by close. Revit shutdown can force ToolWindowRegistry.RetireAll. Retirement diagnoses pending work, aborts owned dispatcher operations, cancels without draining, rolls back an open apply group through the inline commit gate, disposes child/session scopes, and skips close persistence with a log entry. It opens no dispatcher frame. An existing normal-close task stops before its next stage when retirement takes over. DevModeStatus exposes Idle or Busy: <operations> in the root UI Automation ItemStatus. It includes name lookup, navigation, both auto-zoom debounces, duplicate rebuilds, Type Mapping, Commit Review, cache posts, and pending page selection. App, Family Mapping, and Shared Parameters navigation use Mapping-owned NavigationLifetime leases. Leases start inside admitted callbacks or around awaited execution. Both feature auto-zoom debounces use 200 ms and the lease token. Disposal cancels outside the lifetime lock and prevents later selection, activation, or zoom. Core alerts use observed nested modal loops and diagnose reload during a dialog. Mapping execution RevitMappingPlanExecutor validates document identity and supplies document operations to MappingPlanExecutor. MappingPlanExecutor owns the stage loop, capture boundaries, and result builder. Result accounting The MappingApplyResult constructor validates and snapshots recorded operation results. Succeeded operations require positive affected counts. Skips require zero. Failed operations can retain counts for writes completed before failure. Root succeeded/failed/skipped and affected totals derive from one recorded-result snapshot. Caller collections cannot mutate the completed result. Family success requires changed work and a successful reload. Failed-rule totals and fatal operation diagnostics must agree. Exception-backed diagnostics retain the original exception internally. MappingApplyResultBuilder logs each exception reference once with operation context. Commit Review receives stable operation text, codes, IDs, and family context. Exception types, messages, and stacks stay in logs. Writer exceptions are attributed to every unrecorded operation owned by that writer. Family cleanup always attempts close and retains close diagnostics after primary errors. Cancellation plus cleanup failures propagate primary-first through family-batch and outer writer containment. Skipped group-owned references produce Mapping warnings. An Edit Group restriction rejecting a line-style transaction at commit fails that pair. Successful sibling results retain their affected counts, but Commit Review rolls back an attempt with fatal mapping diagnostics. Writer failures A writer exception after all owned operations are recorded is a workflow failure. The result builder logs writer/stage context once and rethrows the original exception with its stack. Recorded operations alone cannot produce a successful final result in this case. With unrecorded owned operations, the executor records their failures and continues to later writers. Population capture Replacement capture precedes the first mutation that can change its population. ApplyContext captures the original symbol populations, target occupancy and type-parameter source values before the writer loop. Host material references are captured at the fixed boundary after Host recreation and before Nested Families or Type Replacements, including plans with no Host operations. They refer to recreated element IDs without consuming values introduced by later type-parameter migration or family reloads. Each family document captures all applicable material, object-style and nested-symbol references before its operation loop. Missing sources are explicit capture results. An absent source in a traversed family is zero work with a non-fatal reason. A missing host source or an ambiguous family material name remains an error. Apply never discovers an incoming population. Family material capture includes writable type parameters and the per-type defaults of instance material parameters. Revit does not allow formulas on Material data type parameters. Formula-determined parameters are outside this material replacement population. Reference kinds are explicit. Blank type names are valid and match ordinally. Capture does not change FamilyManager.CurrentType. Transactional apply restores the captured type. Object-style capture identifies the actual subcategory parameter or boundary curves of each filled region. Family-owned execution uses BatchOperationSet keyed by MappingOperation.OperationId and FamilyBatchResult.ResultsByOperationId. Style and prepared-material payloads use the same IDs. Nested, style, material, and embed dispatch uses canonical operation types and direct appliers. Intermediate counts must be nonnegative, and succeeded plus failed documents cannot exceed attempted. Invalid producer output fails validation. Family document lifetime Family-owned batch execution discovers the complete applicable family tree and captures each original population before applying any family mutation. FamilyBatchDocuments retains one edit document for each family identity through capture, apply, and reload. Discovery spans the whole commit. After discovery, documents with no applicable work in themselves or their descendants are closed before apply. Remaining documents close after their last root-batch use. Final cleanup closes anything left, including after cancellation. Each release closes in reverse open order and reports individual close failures. Discovery logs the peak and retained counts and reports progress per root. Cleanup uses the underlying Revit gate without requiring the launch document to remain active or the work token to remain uncancelled. EditFamily creates independent copies, so no captured element key is carried into a second edit session. Family element references use UniqueId within their retained document plus parameter identity. Family type references use explicit reference kind, family type name, and family parameter name. Built-in parameter identity uses the typed Revit enum without narrowing its underlying 64-bit value. Document-local ElementId values remain diagnostics and population indexes only. Missing keys produce a diagnostic and do not trigger a live rescan. Shared family identity and reload Shared nested families use a name/category identity. Nonshared copies include their embedding path. Discovery opens the project's shared definition when one exists, so a parent's stale embedded copy cannot become the original population for another root. If the same shared family is reached through several roots, applicable operation populations are merged and each normalized operation is applied once. An equivalent alias receives a merged notice. If its representative fails, the alias is reported as failed as well. Conflicting targets for the same source fail preflight. After a nested or root reload, the load allowlist selects FamilySource.Family only for shared identities changed by that target traversal. Unchanged shared children use FamilySource.Project, which preserves the target document's existing child instead of reloading a stale source copy. Parent material capture excludes shared-symbol projections: the child owns those values and only surviving writes count. Before reload, project-owned shared material projections are restored from the target document explicitly. Revit can otherwise propagate those type values even when the shared-family load callback selects Project. Nonshared symbol overrides remain part of the parent population. Family results Family-document success requires both changed work and a successful reload. A failed family traversal or reload marks every operation actually executed in that traversal as failed, including merged aliases. An affected count can show writes made before the failure. The original exception remains attached to the diagnostic for logging and review. Family-document attempt/success/failure counts include every examined root and child document, including zero-work captures. A reload or close failure keeps the completed affected counts and marks the affected document operation results failed. Material projection ownership A parent FamilySymbol's material type value is a projection of the child's authored FamilyType value. When that child has the same planned material operation, the child owns the write and its count. For nonshared children, root-only operations and traversal-depth leaves retain their parent-side references. Shared projections are always child-owned. Missing captured host references produce a nonfatal diagnostic. Line-style verification Line-style query snapshots retain curve IDs and per-source offered intersections, not Revit element wrappers or target sets per curve. A line-style apply performs one fresh discovery sweep, then verifies actual styles by reading the captured IDs. Complete original-source intersections are regrouped under the final source styles. Unexpected population splits or missing curves fail verification for the committed pairs. Their operation results retain the committed affected counts, and the writer returns the errors instead of throwing away those operation results. Commit Review and the subsequent accepted Usage refresh share this result. A rollback does not publish it. CommitReviewLineStyleLifecycle exports it once, and only while the session's query cache still holds the snapshot that was current when post-apply verification succeeded. Explicit Detect and Usage refresh boundaries invalidate prior snapshots. Object-style attribution identifies the family returned by LoadFamily, its retained name, and its ownership of original instances. Style availability depends on the family category and kind. Post-apply verification Commit Review checks operation identity and successful operation results for all replacement kinds, including runtime replacements created by Create Type. Symbol and line-style counts can be checked against incoming populations. Family material and object-style Usage count families while operation results count references. An overlapping successful target is therefore checked through its operation result and writer readback, not by equating those different quantities. Commit Review results and finalization Result Contract Completed Requires MappingApplyResult and derives success from Outcome Canceled Contains neither Mapping result nor failure prose WorkflowFailed Requires a nonblank reason. Can retain a rolled-back Mapping result for diagnostics Warnings can complete successfully and remain committable. Only positive succeeded operations without fatal diagnostics project applied or persistable intent. Verification requires no planned type, host, style, or material source references to remain. Otherwise the verifier's four-field failure summary blocks mapping projection. One Global Mapper: Apply session group stays open through modal review. Apply and Retry Apply execute and verify inside an inner attempt group. Failure or cancellation rolls back the attempt and permits retry. Retry reuses the reviewed plan but constructs a new apply context and rereads the document. Keep + Continue and Keep + Close GM assimilate the session group into one Undo entry before recording mappings. Roll back, X's rollback answer, cancellation, and abnormal exit roll it back. An unknown rollback outcome propagates to the error banner rather than asserting that nothing was kept. Active-view refresh follows successful verification. A refresh warning does not disable Keep. After review closes, RefreshAfterReviewAsync refreshes GM after any admitted attempt, including failed or rolled-back attempts. Type replacements retain their selecting intent key, so acceptance records intent for its actual owner. Apply transactions log each Revit failure at Warning with definition ID and failing elements. Pre-commit issues retain their validation label. Family-document material replacement resolves source and target by material name. Errors retain planned operation ID and host source/target IDs. Family-document material IDs and affected elements are diagnostic details. Report grouping uses the owning operation even when operations share a host pair or family documents assign different IDs. Reloaded family identity Family-owned apply retains the family ID returned by Revit reload. Accepted mappings use that identity, including existing saved and pending mappings for the same family. Rollback leaves mapping identities unchanged. MappingApplyResult.ReloadedFamilyIds snapshots changed root identities. Finalization remaps applied/persistable family keys and targets before merging. MappingIntentStore also remaps existing saved/pending intents, manual family-apply state, and usage links. One replaced identity must not retain a second saved mapping. Host replacement Each host replacement is atomic per instance. Placement and required facing, hand, and point-rotation transfer must finish before source deletion. Ordinary parameter copies use best-effort transfer. A failed replacement becomes an item error only after its subtransaction reports a completed rollback. If rollback throws or reports any other status, the primary and rollback failures escape together so the enclosing transaction aborts instead of committing an uncertain document state. ParameterValueTransfer reads the target after Parameter.Set returns false. It accepts the copy as a no-op only when its storage type and value exactly match the requested source value. It applies no numeric tolerance to Double values. A remaining mismatch becomes a nonfatal HostParameterCopyWarning with the source instance, parameter, and reason. Setter exceptions remain failures. These warnings appear only after the replacement subtransaction commits. A later required-state failure rolls back and retains the fatal replacement error. Commit Review preserves each distinct diagnostic, opens the operation diagnostics section, and reports Completed with Warnings. It counts nonfatal diagnostics. Within each diagnostic-code group, it includes distinct messages in first-seen order. Code groups sort by descending diagnostic count, then by code ignoring case. Host parameter transfer treats a writable instance Phase Created value as instance-owned even when the family symbol exposes the same built-in parameter ID. The type-bound rule excludes generated IfcGUID. Revit read scheduling GmSessionDocumentGate validates Action callbacks as synchronous before wrapping their launch-document check. It rejects async void before Core can see only the synchronous decorator. Generic results also undergo synchronous-result validation. Independent reads for one action start together and are awaited in original order, so the first read's failure/cancellation remains primary. Startup starts family-category, shared-parameter-category, and parameter-group reads together. Family expansion starts view and parameter-name reads together. Selected-type instance examples are read once through type selection. Core's queued-turn policy determines which waiting calls share a callback. Testing See Global Mapper testing for fixture ownership, hidden-desktop dialog hosting, model baselines, and run commands. Limitations Family-tree discovery retains edit documents through capture and applicable writes, so peak open-document count grows with the discovered tree. Grouped curves are eligible only when each enclosing group type has one placed instance. Family-document material replacement resolves by name, not host numeric ID.

developer-guide/tools/common/gm.html.title: Global Mapper (GM) | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/common/gm.html.summary: Global Mapper (GM) Overview Global Mapper finds duplicate or related Revit content, captures mapping intent, and previews and applies replacements through Commit Review. Its main window is modeless. Commit Review is modal and keeps a reversible apply group open until the user keeps or rolls back changes. The architecture specification defines state, capture, execution, and lifetime contracts. The user guide describes mapping workflows. Architecture Source and registration Source: src/Tools/Common/GM/. The assembly and tool ID are DBTools.GM. manifest.yml registers: Surface Value Module DBTools.GM.App.Composition.Revit.GmToolModule Command and availability DBTools.GM.App.Composition.Revit.GmCommand Run profile QueuedModeless Ribbon Common panel, Global Mapper, order 30, icon key gm Main raw view DBTools.ToolViews.GM.GmWindow.xaml, Modeless Commit Review raw view DBTools.ToolViews.GM.GmCommitReviewWindow.xaml, Modal Sandbox uses internal design-time view models with public binding properties: DBTools.GM.App.DesignTime.GmWindowDesignTimeViewModel and DBTools.GM.Features.CommitReview.DesignTime.GmCommitReviewWindowDesignTimeViewModel. Generated src/Tools/Common/GM/MAP.md indexes source files and manifest values. Ownership Owner Responsibility App/Composition Service registration, session and row graph construction App/Sessions Workspace implementations, attachment, close, shutdown, modeless lifetime App/Startup, App/Navigation Initialization, page activation, prewarm, pending navigation App/Persistence, App/State UI-state sequencing and feature-to-domain state construction Domain Project state, identity, element names, parameters, categories, workspace, cache and operation contracts Features/Categories Curated categories Features/Families Family inventory and document lifecycle Features/FamilyMapping Family/type rows, nested usage, scan, selection, and type creation Features/Mapping Intent, row-to-intent translation, conflicts, plans, and replacement execution Features/CommitReview Review planning, modal workflow, reports, verification, finalization, refresh port Features/DeepScan Family scanning, completeness, cache, hydration, refresh Features/Duplicates Detection, matching, selections, tree, and type mapping Features/Usage Indexing, options, matching, preview, selection, and usage rows Features/SharedParameters Authoring, formulas, parameter operations, rows, and tree Features/Similarity Name scoring and score presentation Features/Previews Material/style catalogs and preview values Features/SavedMappings Strict persistence envelope, clear, and reapply Features/ViewOps View and element navigation Revit Tool-wide document and name adapters Feature packages own their local domain, planning, execution, Revit, views, and workflow where present. App composes cross-feature sequences through feature-owned ports. Features do not import App. WPF presentation GmWindowPresenter loads App/Views/GmWindow.xaml through ToolWindowFactory. Its binding source is App/ViewModels/GmWindowViewModel. Commit Review binds to Features/CommitReview/ViewModels/GmCommitReviewWindowViewModel. The runtime and design-time view models expose raw fragment bytes for six feature panes. Stable GmRawViewConverter parses those fragments. OneTime fragment bindings use the nearest categoryTabs ancestor. The host assigns shell and raw-root DataContext synchronously before the first dispatcher pump, so the first DataBind/layout pass can materialize each pane. OneTime retains it across tab switches. Feature panes bind to their feature view models. Parent commands, category selection, and empty-state labels address the shell DataContext. Stable WPF registrations, controls, converters, selectors, attached behaviors, and shared resources live in src/DBTools.Presentation/Tools/GM/, namespace DBTools.Presentation.Tools.GM. Each raw view merges Presentation’s Resources/Theme.xaml and references stable dictionaries with versioned ResourceUri values. GmViewResources.xaml owns Mapping and Similarity styles without a second theme merge. Payload views have no code-behind, dependency properties, or implicit payload-type templates. Bindings use INotifyPropertyChanged sources or OneTime for immutable values. Raw templates use string keys with explicit fallbacks. GmViewXaml exposes embedded bytes for raw-XAML tests and hosted views. App Pure reads the GM assembly's fixed logical resources directly. Commit Review owns one Revit callback around planning, ShowDialog, finalization, and refresh. Core WindowOwnerModalityScope disables Revit and other top-level windows through that callback and restores only the windows it disabled. During planning, the GM owner remains available for its overlay and Cancel action. ShowDialog disables that owner while the review dialog is visible. User close returns the session finalization. Forced retirement returns none. IsRetired is true for both outcomes and cannot distinguish them. Keep triggered from WPF Closing queues the final Close because WPF rejects reentrant Close there. Duplicate Type Mapping uses a registered modeless shell owned by GM, with Manual startup and a taskbar entry. Commit Review also retains Manual startup, an explicit finalization decision, and a cleanup close gate. Cleanup requests cancellation, waits for a safe rollback boundary, and propagates cancellation, timeout, or rollback failures. A failed cleanup leaves the review window open. Row refresh and owner closure follow successful cleanup. Design-time shared-parameter composition uses the production feature/projection graph with explicit host replacements, including NoopFamilyParameterQuery. Authoring receives a registered parameter-signature provider. Data and contracts The architecture specification defines project state, mapping intent, persistence, and execution results. Workflows Startup performance Startup logs Information-level elapsed time for five overlay steps. Usage indexing logs each catalog/index source duration and completion state. Failure or cancellation records the interrupted step and elapsed time, including queued Revit-call time. Overlay visibility is not the timing source. Family population counts use one symbol-count sweep. Type IDs retain collector order and cache per project state. View-owned collection discovers owner IDs through a quick filter, then visits eligible owners with instances, retaining Revit view-visibility filtering. Style/material indexing share one capped sample and 25-instance chunks with separate geometry options. Family-dependent styles are visited once per usage build. Each option-building pass owns immutable name profiles and retains numeric-suffix and multiset-bigram scoring. Testing Pure tests mirror App, Domain, and Features owners. Test builders, external fakes, and assertions live in Tests/Support. Project-state and name-cache tests live under Tests/Domain. Duplicate projection tests live under Tests/Features/Duplicates. The root Revit name adapter mirrors its complete path at Tests/Integration/Revit/Revit/ElementName/ElementNameQueryTests.cs. CommitReviewPlanContextTests mirrors Features/CommitReview/Planning. Saved mappings, authoring, and usage matching also mirror their subjects. Tests/Integration/Revit/App/Sessions/Revit/GmModelessSessionTests.cs launches the production session through its queued App run scope and GmWindowViewModelBuilder. It observes the raw view in the stable shell on the dispatcher. Normal-close tests overlap close requests and await shared completion, shutdown, one Closed event, cleanup, and scope disposal. Retirement tests wait for Idle, retire synchronously, and check collection without another dispatcher pump. ForcedRetirement_AfterApply_RollsBackTheOpenGroupAndReturnsWithoutHanging retires after a real apply and checks model restoration and group finalization before child-scope disposal in the same Revit turn. Revit-hosted Commit Review tests use testing/TestSupport/GM/Fakes/HiddenCommitReviewDialogHost in place of ShowDialog to satisfy hidden-desktop window ownership. Its dispatcher frame ends on retirement. IToolWindowSession.Closed does not complete after forced retirement, so awaiting that event would retain the Revit callback until timeout. A 60-second deadline retires a session left open and fails the test. GM Revit-hosted fixture models, named views, family symbols, line styles, materials, and expected production outcomes are required repository baselines. Missing baselines and false production results fail with the model path and running year. Fixture teardown and transaction-group finalization failures also fail and are aggregated with a primary test failure when both occur. DBTools.GM.Pure.Tests.csproj contains owner-local fixtures and shared test support and references the desktop DBTools.GM.csproj. The production assembly grants the Pure assembly internal access. Revit references are compile-only; loading a Revit-typed member requires a Revit host. Run the supported gates through the repository wrappers: ./build.sh BuildApp ./build.sh BuildTests ./test.sh test --tool GM --scope pure ./test.sh test --tool GM --scope local -y 2026 The Pure project targets net10.0-windows and requires Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App. Revit-hosted tests use the local scope through the daemon fleet. Limitations The session key uses the document hash code, which can collide. The specification describes family-document and line-style limits.

developer-guide/tools/common/tdv.html.title: Transfer Drafting Views (TDV) | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/common/tdv.html.summary: Transfer Drafting Views (TDV) Overview Transfer Drafting Views (TDV) copies drafting views between the active Revit document and a library .rvt file. Teams keep standard drafting views in the library and import them into projects. Export to Library copies drafting views from the active document to a library file. Import from Library copies drafting views from a library file to the active document. For a workshared library, TDV creates a local copy, and after an export it synchronizes the changes with central. Architecture Project structure src/Tools/Common/TDV/ ├── App/ │ ├── Composition/ # TdvToolModule, commands, AddTdv() │ ├── DesignTime/ │ ├── Persistence/ # CachePaths │ ├── Sessions/ # WindowSession, WindowSessionDialogRunner │ ├── ViewModels/ # TdvWindowViewModel partials │ └── Views/ # TdvWindow.xaml ├── Assets/ ├── Features/ │ ├── Library/{Domain,Operations,Settings,Workflow} │ ├── Preview/{Operations,State} │ └── Transfer/{Domain,Execution,Operations,ViewModels,Workflow} ├── Tests/ # DBTools.TDV.Pure.Tests, DBTools.TDV.Local.Tests ├── DBTools.TDV.csproj └── manifest.yml App/Composition holds the manifest entry points and DI. App/Sessions/WindowSession creates a registered stable modal shell through Core's ToolWindowFactory and owns the owner provider, logger display, alerts, banners, initial load, cleanup on close and result projection. WindowSessionDialogRunner owns the modal-loop result and retirement. App/Views/TdvWindow.xaml is embedded raw XAML with the header, grid, preview and actions sections inline. The library settings view (Features/Library/Settings/Views/LibrarySettingsView.xaml) is also raw XAML, loaded with ToolWindowXaml.LoadElement. Both resources have explicit logical names and contain only stable or framework WPF types. TdvWindowViewModel is the App orchestration edge. CachePaths supplies cache roots to the Library and Preview features. Transfer is one Revit-facing service split over partial files: shared guards (Transfer.cs), catalog queries (Transfer.Queries.cs), apply-selection orchestration (Transfer.ApplySelection.cs), per-row steps (Transfer.Execution.cs) and per-run accounting (Transfer.RunState.cs). The run state holds duplicate destination names, deferred successes, cancellation, rollback and unknown-finalization reporting and the final TransferResult. The split adds no service or transaction boundary. The drafting-view operations are in Features/Transfer/Operations/DraftingView: DraftingViewReader (enumeration and name lookup), DraftingViewTypeResolver (type lookup and creation of missing destination types) and DraftingViewWriter (create, copy, clear and overrides). Features/Preview/Operations/PreviewExporter and PreviewImageExporter export previews. TransferSession binds one Transfer to a destination and source document for the window. Transfer commands are split by direction. ExportTransferWorkflow and ImportTransferWorkflow make the document and outcome decisions of their direction. LibraryTransferWorkflow owns catalog selection, library open, close warnings and host reactivation. The Library workflow uses the ILibrarySelectionDialog port; the Transfer workflows use the ITransferDialog port. WindowSession implements both: it presents library selection, loads the embedded TDV view, shows the shell modally with the application IWindowOwnerHandleProvider and projects the window counts and errors into TransferDialogResult. LibraryDocumentService does the Revit document open, save, sync and close calls; LibraryCatalog validates library paths from the current settings snapshot. Service registration TdvToolModule registers the services through ServiceCollectionExtensions.AddTdv(). Registrations are scoped because they depend on run-scope services (IRevitCallGate, ITransactionRunner). The composition root supplies the current Revit year and the library-file year probe. services.AddScoped<Transfer>(sp => new Transfer(gate, tx, logger)); services.AddScoped<Func<LibraryCatalog>>(sp => () => new LibraryCatalog( settings.Get(settingsSection).Files.ToList(), RevitInstanceIdentity.RevitYear, RevitYearProbe.Probe)); services.AddScoped<LibraryDocumentService>(sp => new LibraryDocumentService(gate, logger, CachePaths.LibraryLocalsRoot, RevitInstanceIdentity.RevitYear, RevitYearProbe.Probe)); services.AddScoped<WindowSession>(sp => new WindowSession(transfer, alerts, loggerFactory, loggerWindowHost, ownerHandleProvider, windowFactory)); services.AddScoped<ILibrarySelectionDialog>(sp => sp.GetRequiredService<WindowSession>()); services.AddScoped<ITransferDialog>(sp => sp.GetRequiredService<WindowSession>()); // LibraryTransferWorkflow, ExportTransferWorkflow and ImportTransferWorkflow follow. Service Purpose Transfer Revit transfer operations and catalog queries LibraryCatalog Library path validation from a snapshot of library entries LibraryDocumentService Library document open, save, sync, close and host reactivation, with an App-supplied cache root ILibrarySelectionDialog Port for library selection (Library feature) ITransferDialog Port for the modal transfer window and its result (Transfer feature) WindowSession Implementation of both ports: owner reuse, modal window lifetime and result projection LibraryTransferWorkflow Catalog selection, library open, document cleanup and host reactivation Transfer methods Method Description BuildViewItemsAsync(destination, source, ct) Collects the drafting views of the source document. ApplySelectionAsync(TransferRequest) Runs the transfer in one continuous Revit API callback. WouldConflictAsync(destination, name, replace, ct) Checks a destination name for a conflict. ExportPreviewAsync(source, sourceViewId, tempDir, ct) Exports a preview image of a view. Manifest id: DBTools.TDV assembly: DBTools.TDV moduleType: DBTools.TDV.App.Composition.TdvToolModule order: 0 panel: Common sandboxWindows: - id: DBTools.TDV.Main displayName: "Transfer Drafting Views" group: "Common" xamlResource: "DBTools.ToolViews.TDV.TdvWindow.xaml" windowKind: Modal width: 1400 height: 700 minWidth: 1200 minHeight: 600 showInTaskbar: true startupLocation: CenterScreen designTimeViewModelType: "DBTools.TDV.App.DesignTime.TdvWindowDesignTimeViewModel" designTimeViewModelAssembly: "DBTools.TDV" designTimeViewModelVisibility: Public tool: settings: configSection: Core.MasterLibrary settingsPacks: - key: core.library title: "Library Files" warnings: - id: core.library.invalid title: "Library Paths Invalid" message: "One or more saved library file paths are invalid. Fix the paths and save the settings to re-enable import/export." disableTools: - DBTools.ExportToLibrary - DBTools.ImportFromLibrary ribbonTools: - internalName: DBTools.ExportToLibrary commandType: DBTools.TDV.App.Composition.TdvExportCommand availabilityType: DBTools.TDV.App.Composition.TdvExportCommand runProfile: InlineUi displayText: "Export\nTo Library" iconBaseKey: export tooltip: "Export drafting views to the library" controlKind: StackedButtonItem splitGroup: library_transfer order: 0 - internalName: DBTools.ImportFromLibrary commandType: DBTools.TDV.App.Composition.TdvImportCommand availabilityType: DBTools.TDV.App.Composition.TdvImportCommand runProfile: InlineUi displayText: "Import\nFrom Library" iconBaseKey: import tooltip: "Import drafting views from the library" controlKind: StackedButtonItem splitGroup: library_transfer order: 1 Data and contracts Capabilities Import and export of drafting views, several views in one batch. View type mapping: each row selects a destination drafting view type, or Retain Original. Conflict detection while editing: names that exist in the destination, and duplicate destination names in the current selection. Replace mode for views with the same name. A preview of the selected view, with pan and zoom. One destination transaction group per batch, bound to the explicit destination document (also a non-active library). Per-view progress during transfer. Callback requirement Transfer.ApplySelectionAsync must start inside an active Revit API callback, and the supplied call gate and transaction runner must keep the whole transfer in that callback. Before it reads a document or starts the destination group, it throws OperationCanceledException if the request token is canceled and InvalidOperationException ("TDV transfer requires one continuous Revit API callback.") if RevitCallGateApiContext.IsActive is false. Both ribbon commands use the InlineUi profile. The query methods (BuildViewItemsAsync, WouldConflictAsync, ExportPreviewAsync) can each queue as one complete operation. ApplySelectionAsync also checks that the source and destination are valid, open documents and not the same document. The run-start log entry contains a run ID and the title and path of the source and destination. Destination names TDV does not add suffixes to destination names. A row fails when its destination name is blank (DestinationNameRequired), exists in the destination while Replace is off (DestinationNameConflict), or duplicates the destination name of another selected row (DuplicateTargetName). View types The row View Type list contains the drafting view types of the destination: the host document for an import, the library document for an export. Retain Original resolves to the drafting type name of the source view. If the destination has no type with that name, TDV duplicates an existing destination drafting ViewFamilyType and gives the duplicate that name. If the source type name cannot be read, the row fails with SourceTypeNameUnavailable. Settings Library options The Core.MasterLibrary section stores LibraryOptions: public sealed class LibraryOptions { public IList<LibraryFile> Files { get; set; } = new List<LibraryFile>(); } public sealed class LibraryFile { public string? MainPath { get; set; } // primary library .rvt path public string? FallbackPath { get; set; } // alternative path, for example another network location public string? Alias { get; set; } // short name in the library picker } Settings pack LibrarySettingsContext gives the settings page a tree of library files with add and remove for files and fallback paths, path validation as the user edits, and pending-change tracking. The settings-pack factory receives the Revit year and year probe from the TDV composition root, so settings validation matches the runtime checks. LibraryTransferWorkflow receives a Func<LibraryCatalog> from the composition root and does not read the settings type. Each tree row shows a validation icon (green check or red error), a tooltip with the full path, and a short display text: the root, the file name and the last three folder levels. Path validation LibraryCatalog marks a path invalid, with a failure reason, when: the file does not exist (File not found); the extension is not .rvt (Not a .rvt file); the year probe cannot read the saved Revit version (the probe's failure reason; TDV logs the exception); the saved version differs from the session (Revit version mismatch (file: {0}, current: {1})). An invalid path raises the core.library.invalid settings warning, which disables both ribbon commands. Warnings are evaluated at startup, so the commands can be disabled as soon as Revit starts. LibraryDocumentService.OpenLibraryAsync checks the version again before it opens the file and throws InvalidOperationException ("Library file was saved in Revit {0} but the current session is Revit {1}. ...") on a mismatch. The command's ISafeExecutor boundary shows it as a banner. The check prevents two failures: for a workshared file, WorksharingUtils.CreateNewLocal() fails with a version error; for a non-workshared file, Revit upgrades the library file when it opens it. Open failures propagate through the import or export workflow to the command boundary; they are not treated as a canceled library selection. Errors Per-view error codes (TransferErrorCode) Code Description Unknown Unspecified error, or the finalization outcome is unknown DestinationTypeMissing Destination view type not found SourceTypeNameUnavailable Source view type name cannot be read CreateViewFailed Destination view could not be created or prepared CopyElementsFailed View elements could not be copied OverridesFailed Graphic overrides could not be copied ValidationFailed Row validation failed ClearDestinationViewFailed Contents of the existing destination view could not be cleared MetadataCopyFailed View scale or description could not be copied DestinationNameRequired Destination name is blank DuplicateTargetName Another selected row has the same destination name DestinationNameConflict Destination view exists and Replace is off TransactionRolledBack Revit discarded the attempted changes of the run Result reporting After each transfer, TDV shows: a banner on the TDV window (success or warning) with the selected, processed and result counts; a summary alert with the selected, processed, added, replaced, failed and not-attempted counts, a table of per-view issues when there are failures (rows can be copied to the clipboard), and the buttons Accept and Transfer More and Close Tool. TransferResult carries SelectedCount, ProcessedCount, Added, Replaced, FailedCount, UnprocessedCount, Cancelled, FinalizationOutcome (Unknown, Committed, RolledBack), Errors and ErrorDetails. AllChangesDiscarded is true only for RolledBack. Transfer logs include the identifiers and names of the selected views (a bounded list). Row state flows from Transfer to the row view models and XAML triggers as TransferRowState. TDV logs each per-view failure with its exception and records only the stable code and message in the row result. Success callbacks and committed add and replace counts are published only after a Committed outcome. A rollback marks attempted rows discarded. An unknown finalization sets the projected successes to zero, marks attempted rows failed with Unknown and reports that the destination state is not verified. Library close Save and sync always attempt to close the library document. Document.Close(...) == false is a failure of a required close. A single save, sync or close failure keeps its original exception. When the operation and the close both fail, TDV throws one ordered AggregateException with the operation failure first. Best-effort cleanup (TryCloseAsync) returns false only when Revit refuses to close the active document. Other cleanup failures propagate; after a failed export, TDV reports one ordered AggregateException with the export failure first and the cleanup failure second. Workflows Per-view steps For each selected row, TDV: validates the destination name before the transfer transaction; creates or prepares the destination view with the selected view type; copies the view scale and description parameters; copies the elements of the source view, except skipped categories; copies element graphic overrides from source to destination. If a step fails, the per-view transaction rolls back and the row is recorded as failed. DestinationTransactionGroup receives the destination Document at begin, rejects item and finalization calls for any other document and runs each item transaction against that document. Import (library to host) and export (host to a non-active library) therefore use the same real Revit group; the group is never resolved from ActiveUIDocument. It creates the Revit group through RevitTransactionGroups.Begin. Successful row states and the add and replace counts are held until the group reports Committed. A RolledBack outcome marks the attempted rows discarded. An unknown or failed finalization withholds success and claims neither commit nor rollback. Operation, finalization and disposal failures stay ordered in the logged exception chain; the row result keeps its stable per-view error code and message. Sources: src/Tools/Common/TDV/Features/Transfer/Execution/{DestinationTransactionGroup,Transfer.ApplySelection,Transfer.RunState}.cs, src/Tools/Common/TDV/Features/Transfer/Domain/TransferResult.cs. Copying view contents TDV collects the elements owned by the source view and copies them with ElementTransformUtils.CopyElements and a UseDestinationTypesHandler (an IDuplicateTypeNamesHandler that keeps destination types when type names collide). Groups are copied before other elements; group members are paired with their copies so overrides apply to them. Skipped elements: viewports, elements whose category name is Title Blocks, Viewports, Views, Schedules or Guide Grids, and elements whose name contains ExtentElem. The category check compares English category names. Drafting views are collected with: new FilteredElementCollector(doc) .OfClass(typeof(View)) .WhereElementIsNotElementType() .Cast<View>() .Where(v => v.ViewType == ViewType.DraftingView && !v.IsTemplate) UI Main window (TdvWindow) The registered modal shell has the title "Transfer Drafting Views", an initial size of 1400 × 700, a minimum size of 1200 × 600, centered placement, a taskbar entry and a resizable layout. The Sandbox manifest declares the same dimensions, taskbar visibility and placement. The raw view has these sections: TransferHeaderView: conflict warning, type filter, search and separator. TransferGridView: the transfer grid and row visuals. TransferActionsView: status, selection and transfer actions, and errors. TransferPreviewView: the preview panel, cursor-relative wheel zoom, mouse panning, a zoom button and zoom on image update. The main view merges Presentation's theme once at its root; the library settings view merges its own. String item lists and tooltips use explicit text templates. Row-state triggers compare enum names as strings. PreviewZoomBehavior (Presentation) zooms on image update, deferred until layout. DBTools.Presentation.Tools.TDV.TdvPanZoomBehavior handles mouse pan and zoom and releases capture, cursor state and subscriptions on retirement. Window lifetime ProgressOverlay.For(session.Window) attaches after the view loads and before the dialog shows. The normal Closed notification clears UI actions, cancels outdated preview and conflict requests, disposes the view model and deletes its cache files. The host then retires the session and releases subscriptions, behavior state, the initializer, the overlay registration and the owner. Cleanup and the result depend on the Closed notification, also for a window closed before ShowDialog; an early normal close still allows library-document cleanup. Late callbacks and catalog results do not touch a disposed view model. A load failure after close shows no alert and logs no load error. If the load-error alert cannot be shown, the window still requests close. Dev Mode retirement logs a pending load, preview, conflict refresh or transfer instead of canceling it. Idle retirement is synchronous and does not pump the dispatcher. The library settings page uses stable tree selection and a focus-request counter. Selecting a main library entry whose alias is empty or whitespace focuses and selects the alias text at Background priority. Entries with an alias, and fallback entries, do not take focus. Show the TDV modal session for view selection and run the transfer to the library. If views were added or replaced: for a workshared library, synchronize with central with the comment DB TOOLS - ADDED [n] DETAILS AND REPLACED [n] DETAILS. and close; otherwise save and close. If nothing changed, close without saving. Reactivate the original document. Show a warning only when Revit refuses to close the library because it is active. Any other close failure propagates, so an export is never reported as successful after a required close failed. Import Check that library paths are configured. Select a library file. For a workshared library, create a local copy under LibraryLocals\. Open the library document. Show the TDV modal session for view selection and run the transfer to the active document. Close the library without saving. Show a cleanup warning if the library document could not be closed. LibraryCatalogTests: path validation and catalog projection. TransferTests and the Transfer fixture in Transfer.ExecutionTests.cs: Revit-hosted transfers between source and destination documents. developer-guide/tools/experimental/erft-.title: ERFT technical specification | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/experimental/erft-.summary: ERFT technical specification Overview ERFT calculates vertical offset changes for structural columns and beams against a triangulated floor or roof bottom surface. It modifies offset parameters, not level parameters. All lengths and coordinates in domain calculations use feet. Source: src/Tools/Experimental/ERFT/. See ERFT for composition, presentation ownership, and use. Architecture Selection and Planning prepare AdjustmentPlan; Execution writes offsets and Persistence stores the system. ERFT architecture lists owners and the preview host. Data and contracts Plan and identity Features/Domain/Adjustment/AdjustmentPlan contains: State Contents Target HostTargetId, LinkedTargetId, LinkInstanceId, TargetGeometry, TargetDisplayName Sources Lists of ColumnAdjustment and BeamAdjustment Hierarchy FramingGraph Rounding ToleranceFeet, default 1/48 ft. RoundingMode, default Nearest Profiles ProfilesByTypeId and ProfileExtractionFailuresByTypeId Storage SystemId, initialized from a GUID Revit element, type, level, link, and graph identities use long. Target IDs and connection IDs are nullable where absent. Mesh indices and counts use int. JSON numeric IDs in the 32-bit range deserialize as long. ColumnAdjustment retains element/type identity, type name, base/top points, original top offset, and top-level identity/name. Calculation supplies target elevation, raw delta, rounded delta, new offset, status, and optional error text. BeamAdjustment retains element/type identity, type name, endpoints, original endpoint offsets, and reference-level identity/name. Each endpoint has a Free, ToColumn, or ToBeam connection and optional owner ID. Calculation supplies endpoint target elevations, deltas, rounded deltas, new offsets, status, and optional error text. Hybrid means one ToColumn end and one ToBeam end. Statuses are Pending, NoChangeNeeded, and Error. RequiresModification requires Pending and a rounded delta magnitude greater than 1e-9 at an affected end. Plan pending counts include only rows requiring modification. A Pending row without a required write contributes to no-change counts. Target geometry Features/Operations/TargetGeometry/Revit/TargetGeometryReader resolves host or linked targets. A linked target uses RevitLinkInstance.GetTotalTransform and requires a loaded link document. Geometry extraction uses Medium detail and ComputeReferences = false. It traverses solids, triangulates faces, and retains separate bottom-surface and full-element meshes. A bottom face has host-transformed normal Z at most -0.1, sampled at the midpoint of its UV bounds. No usable bottom surface returns no target geometry. Unexpected geometry faults log context and propagate. TargetSurface contains Vertices, TriangleIndices, Bounds, display/category names, ElementVertices, ElementTriangleIndices, and optional LinkTransformMatrix. Coordinates used by calculation are in the host frame. The link matrix contains 16 doubles in column-major order: [basisX.X, basisX.Y, basisX.Z, 0, basisY.X, basisY.Y, basisY.Z, 0, basisZ.X, basisZ.Y, basisZ.Z, 0, origin.X, origin.Y, origin.Z, 1] TransformLinkPointToHost requires exactly 16 values and applies the upper 3×3 basis plus translation. Features/Domain/TargetSurfaceProjector.ProjectToSurface visits every triangle, finds its nearest vertex, edge, or interior point, and retains the nearest point by squared 3D distance. GetTargetElevation returns that point's Z. An empty mesh returns no projection. See Limitations for projection behavior outside a triangle and mesh traversal cost. Framing graph FramingGraphBuilder.ResolveConnectionsAndBuildGraph resolves connections and emits ColumnToBeams, BeamToBeams, and ProcessingOrder. Connection tolerance is 0.5/12 feet (half an inch). Connect free beam ends to column top points within the tolerance, inclusive. For remaining free ends, find the closest other beam segment at a strictly smaller distance than the tolerance. Reject an edge that would form a dependency cycle, log a warning, and leave that end Free. Emit columns first, then topologically sort beam dependencies. Column connections use the first qualifying column in input order. Beam candidates use 3D distance to a segment with the projection parameter clamped to [0,1]. A nearly degenerate segment uses its start point. Each endpoint is independent, so hybrid connections are supported. Ready beams that frame to columns precede other ready beams. Element ID breaks ties. If unresolved dependencies remain, the builder logs and appends remaining beam IDs in sorted order. Adjustment and rounding Features/Planning/Adjustment/AdjustmentEvaluator.CalculateAdjustments follows ProcessingOrder. It keeps adjusted column-top and beam-end elevations in dictionaries without mutating Revit.
