For a column: targetZ = nearest surface point Z delta = targetZ - originalTopZ roundedDelta = round(delta, tolerance, mode) newTopOffset = originalTopOffset + roundedDelta adjustedTopZ = originalTopZ + roundedDelta For each beam end: Connection Target elevation ToColumn The connected column's adjusted top Z ToBeam Interpolated Z on the supporting beam's adjusted segment Free Nearest target-surface point Z Missing dependency elevations produce Error. For beam interpolation, only XY determines the segment parameter: dx = supportEnd.X - supportStart.X dy = supportEnd.Y - supportStart.Y t = clamp(((query.X - supportStart.X)*dx + (query.Y - supportStart.Y)*dy) / (dx*dx + dy*dy), 0, 1) Z = adjustedStartZ + (adjustedEndZ - adjustedStartZ)*t When XY length squared is less than 1e-10, use adjustedStartZ. The query's Z does not influence interpolation. Each new endpoint offset is its original offset plus rounded target-minus-original-Z delta. RoundingEvaluator.ApplyRounding uses: Mode Rounded delta Nearest Math.Round(delta / tolerance) * tolerance, including .NET's midpoint-to-even rule Up Math.Ceiling(delta / tolerance) * tolerance Down Math.Floor(delta / tolerance) * tolerance Up and Down refer to signed numeric direction, including negative deltas. At helper level, nonpositive tolerance or an undefined mode returns the raw delta. UI and stored-data admission reject invalid settings before normal use. IsWithinTolerance tests abs(delta) < tolerance/2. Columns with a rounded delta within that interval become NoChangeNeeded. Beams become NoChangeNeeded when both rounded deltas satisfy it. Missing target geometry marks every row Error. Profiles and preview MemberProfileExtractor creates temporary placements for unique source types and extracts section loops. It owns each temporary instance immediately after creation, before commit and geometry bake. Creation, bake, and cleanup transaction starts/commits must return Started/Committed. Any subsequent creation, commit, disposal, bake, or extraction fault reaches cleanup. Concurrent extraction and cleanup failures preserve both causes. Expected ProfileLoops/* conditions return structured per-type failures. Unexpected faults and cancellation propagate. One Info summary reports total, extracted, and unsupported counts. Per-type progress uses Debug. PreviewSceneBuilder.Build renders adjusted endpoints using extracted profiles. Missing profiles omit affected members and log counts. No successful profile still permits target-only preview. Target selection prefers bottom-surface TargetSurface. Full TargetElement is a fallback only when that mesh is unavailable. No usable mesh throws Preview/TargetMeshMissing. Mesh Color Opacity Target #4080C0 0.12 Pending member #00CC00 1.0 No-change member #808080 0.7 Error member #CC0000 1.0 PreviewProjector maps meshes, colors, tooltips, IDs, and bounds into immutable StructuralScene3D snapshots. It clamps opacity to [0,1] and uses a fixed Vector3.UnitZ exterior normal. A null mesh, empty vertices, incomplete triangle indices, out-of-range indices, or non-finite vertices throws InvalidOperationException. Missing or invalid RGB/ARGB hexadecimal color text throws FormatException. RGB input receives an opaque FF alpha prefix. A leading # is optional. The projector does not replace invalid mesh or color input with default data. The Presentation presenter owns camera/navigation, device lifetime, hit testing, and cleanup. ERFT selects PreserveAngle and FitRedefinesHome. See preview interaction. Storage formats Features/Persistence/StorageSchema/Revit/StorageSchema defines public-read/public-write String fields: Schema GUID Fields DBTools_ERFT_V2 C736C6F5-34C8-4E50-A890-E5420C3E5391 Tag, SystemId, MemberRole, OriginalOffset, Timestamp DBTools_ERFT_System_V2 06C087B9-DA5B-4E3B-9496-13C7C8732B0E SystemIdString, DataJson Vendor is DBTools. Element Tag is ERFT, MemberRole is Column or Beam, and Timestamp is UTC round-trip text. OriginalOffset contains an invariant number for columns or start;end invariant numbers for beams. Lookup validates schema name and required simple String fields before use. Apply removes legacy element entities at B2C3D4E5-F6A7-4B8C-9D0E-1F2A3B4C5D6E and legacy system entities at C3D4E5F6-A7B8-4C9D-0E1F-2A3B4C5D6E7F only when vendor/name identify DBTools_ERFT or DBTools_ERFT_System respectively. It deletes an emptied DataStorage carrier and logs removals. Foreign registrations under those GUIDs remain untouched and log a warning. This cleanup shares the apply transaction. SystemPlanRepository.Save(Document, StoredPlan) and Load(Document, systemId) return structured failures for expected missing/duplicate/incompatible storage states. Duplicate records for a system fail explicitly. Unexpected Revit repository faults log the system ID and propagate. StoredPlan serializes target IDs/name, ToleranceFeet, RoundingMode, Columns, Beams, SystemId, and Timestamp. Stored columns retain ElementId, OriginalTopOffsetFeet, NewTopOffsetFeet, and AppliedDeltaFeet. Stored beams retain ElementId, original/new endpoint offsets, and applied endpoint deltas. CreateSnapshot includes rows with Pending status before the writer changes statuses after commit. It does not store geometry or profiles. StoredPlanMapper.Deserialize requires serialized tolerance, mode, both collections, and SystemId. Both collections and every member must be non-null. Element IDs must be positive. SystemId must be nonblank and match the DataStorage key ignoring case. A positive host target or a positive link-instance/linked-target pair is required. Tolerance must be positive and rounding mode defined. No schema-version migration participates in admission. Null display name or timestamp normalizes to empty text. Failure code Condition Storage/EmptyPayload Blank JSON Storage/InvalidJson Malformed JSON or missing required serialized members Storage/NullPayload JSON null Storage/IncompatiblePayload Invalid collection/member identity, tolerance, or enum Storage/SystemIdMissing Blank payload SystemId Storage/SystemIdMismatch Record key and payload disagree Storage/TargetMissing No positive target identity Workflows Selection and preparation Features/Selection/Revit/TargetSelectionPicker first picks a linked Floor or RoofBase. Esc switches to host selection through Selection/HostTarget/Revit/HostTargetSelectionFilter. Esc during host selection cancels launch. Each picker owns a yellow guidance banner and disposes its handle in finally. SourceSelectionFilter admits host FamilyInstance elements with: Category Requirement Structural Columns LocationPoint Structural Framing LocationCurve containing a Line, and StructuralType other than Brace SourceSelectionPicker excludes structural materials matching \bconcrete\b, case-insensitively, and reports the filtered count. It reads the instance material, then the type material when absent. Missing or blank material names do not match. Unexpected inspection failures retain element context and propagate. SourceSelectionCollector compares selected and extracted counts. Any extraction mismatch fails with Selection/SourceExtractionFailed. SourceSelectionValidator requires a selected column or a selected beam connected to a column. Beam-only validation extracts model columns and evaluates cloned beam values, so validation does not alter the live plan's connections. No connection produces Selection/NoColumnConnection. Features/Planning/PlanPreparation/Revit/PlanPreparationBuilder prepares the target, source values, framing graph, profiles, and initial adjustments before opening the window. Tolerance and window behavior Presets are 1/16, 1/8, 1/4, 1/2, and 1 inch, plus Custom. The default is 1/4 inch. Custom text parses with invariant culture and must be finite and at least 0.01 inch. Invalid input appears inline and disables Apply. ErftWindowViewModel.CanApply also requires a positive pending count and zero errors. The modal window contains the target/re-pick control, rounding controls, 3D preview, column/beam comparison grids, summary, Cancel, and Apply. Both grids end with a stretch Status column and a minimum width. Re-pick calls HideForPick, performs selection, recomputes the plan, and shows the same shell and preview presenter. An expected apply failure leaves the dialog available with error feedback. Successful apply reports modified and unchanged element counts, then closes the window. WindowSession.Interaction ignores duplicate Apply and Re-pick requests while IsApplyInProgress is true. The view model's close gate blocks Cancel and ordinary close during that interval. An apply exception triggers a gated-close bypass and propagates when the interaction result is collected. A concurrent close failure is retained with the apply exception. Escape clears both grid selections and marks the key event handled, so it never closes the window. The Cancel button has no IsCancel route. A mouse-down outside a grid row clears both selections regardless of button. Alerts WindowSession uses the active ERFT window as the owner for apply alerts. If that session is absent or retired, it uses the injected owner-handle provider. Selection diagnostics always use the injected provider. Event Presentation No plan to apply Info alert Expected apply failure Error alert Apply success Success alert with modified column/beam and unchanged counts Selected or stored target geometry extraction failed Top Warning banner Source extraction failed or source selection invalid Warning alert All stored sources missing Error alert Some stored sources missing Warning alert with missing count Invalid stored tolerance or rounding mode Error alert Alerts use the tool name as title and window title, with a default OK button. Apply transaction AdjustmentPlanExecutor rejects row errors with Apply/PlanHasErrors. With no pending writes it returns all elements unchanged without invoking the writer. AdjustmentWriter selects RequiresModification rows, sorts columns by ID, and applies beams in graph order followed by any omitted beams in ID order. One ERFT Apply Adjustments transaction performs: Purge recognized legacy ERFT entities. Obtain and validate the element schema. Set column FAMILY_TOP_LEVEL_OFFSET_PARAM. Set beam STRUCTURAL_BEAM_END0_ELEVATION and STRUCTURAL_BEAM_END1_ELEVATION. Tag changed elements and save the system snapshot in DataStorage. Missing elements/parameters, read-only or wrong-storage parameters, and a false Set result fail apply. Offset, tag, and storage writes must all succeed or the transaction rolls back. After commit, changed rows become NoChangeNeeded. Cancellation propagates. Expected FramingAdjustmentFailureException becomes a structured result. Other exceptions retain their chain and reach the safe-execution boundary. Contextual edit App/Composition/ErftContextualRibbonInjector adapts Core's contextual ribbon runtime. It targets Modify tabs for Structural Columns, Structural Framing, Multi-Select, Multi, or Multi-Category. Eligible selected elements have a supported category, compatible V2 entity, Tag ERFT, and a SystemId. Selection evaluation logs only when (hasErftElements, systemCount, buttonCount) changes. Missing-schema logging occurs once until a schema becomes available again. Selection-hook safe execution suppresses start/completion noise and banners. Edit clicks require a system ID, an initialized ExternalEvent, and an Accepted raise result. The event executes through ISafeExecutor with ErrorOnly notification and an owned InlineUi App run scope. Multiple systems use the system selector. The repository loads the chosen system. A failed repository load logs its code/context and shows this banner before returning: Cannot edit the selected ERFT system because stored plan data is missing or invalid. {Error.Tag} The banner retains the repository failure tag. Edit does not enter new-flow selection. The scope resolves FramingAdjustmentWorkflow and clears its current RevitRunScope before disposal. EditReconstructionBuilder resolves stored source IDs and reads current geometry/offsets. Partially missing sources produce diagnostics and permit remaining sources. No resolvable sources prevents reconstruction. EditReconstructionValidator rejects nonpositive tolerance and undefined modes with Edit/InvalidStoredTolerance or Edit/InvalidStoredRoundingMode. Reconstruction retains SystemId and stored rounding settings, then recomputes adjustments against the target. Re-apply uses current offsets, rather than adding a stored applied delta again. Failures FramingAdjustmentFailure carries expected codes, messages, and context, formatted with [SpecFail/*] tags. These results represent expected contract failures, not every runtime exception. Unexpected selection, material inspection, extraction, cleanup, reconstruction, repository, and apply failures propagate with context. Cancellation is not converted to failed data. Testing See ERFT testing for the single fixture inventory, model requirements, and commands. Limitations Target elevation uses the nearest point in 3D, including triangle edges and vertices; it does not use a vertical intersection. Projection visits every triangle. Legacy storage is removed in the apply transaction without migration.

developer-guide/tools/experimental/erft..title: Extreme Roof Framing Tool (ERFT) | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/experimental/erft..summary: Extreme Roof Framing Tool (ERFT) Overview ERFT adjusts host structural column and beam offsets to follow a host or linked floor/roof bottom surface. It preserves level associations, previews calculated changes, and applies offsets and storage in one transaction. See the technical specification for geometry, rounding, storage, and failure contracts, and the user guide page for the window. Architecture Ownership Source: src/Tools/Experimental/ERFT/. The manifest registers DBTools.ERFT, module DBTools.ERFT.App.Composition.ErftToolModule, and command/availability DBTools.ERFT.App.Composition.ErftNewCommand. The command uses InlineUi, icon key erft, and order 60 on the Testing panel. Owner Responsibility App/Composition Command, module, registration, contextual ribbon adapter App/Sessions/WindowSession Modal shell, alerts, banners, and lifetime App/ViewModels Tolerance, row selection, commands, and binding state App/Views/ErftWindow.xaml Raw embedded view Features/Domain Plan values, target projection, and framing graph Features/Selection Source rules, diagnostics, and Revit pickers Features/Operations Revit column, beam, target-geometry, and member-profile readers Features/Planning Preparation, edit reconstruction, target re-pick, adjustment, and rounding Features/Execution Apply orchestration and Revit writer Features/Persistence JSON, schemas, and system DataStorage repository Features/Preview Domain meshes and stable scene projection Features/State/AdjustmentPlanStore Current plan state Features/Workflow/FramingAdjustmentWorkflow New/edit/re-pick/apply interaction through feature-owned IWindowSession Feature decisions remain behind IWindowSession and WindowSessionAction. App implements their typed presentation methods. ERFT production has no dependency on another tool. A missing active document returns Failed before opening the window. The per-run DI scope owns and disposes WindowSession on every exit path. The workflow does not dispose it. Normal-close cleanup diagnostics belong to the shared window host. ERFT logs failures from its own close-and-retire release path without replacing the caller's primary failure. The shell explicitly sets the title Extreme Roof Framing Tool and loads the raw EmbeddedResource DBTools.ToolViews.ERFT.ErftWindow.xaml. The view merges its theme directly and uses the stable string-based EnumMatchConverter for rounding radio buttons. Preview PreviewSceneBuilder creates target and member meshes. PreviewProjector maps them into StructuralScene3D snapshots. DBTools.Presentation.StructuralPreview owns device lifetime, camera state, navigation, hit testing, hover tooltips, emphasis, outlines, target crease edges, and cleanup. DBTools.Presentation.Tools.ERFT.ErftPreviewOptions chooses the preserve-angle camera and fit-as-Home policy. The initial look direction is parallel to (0, 20, -10), with Z up. The camera home angle does not derive from the target mesh. Scene bounds include every rendered mesh vertex. Geometry updates within unchanged bounds preserve Home. Changed bounds fit the scene at the current angle and capture a new Home. Zoom to Fit also replaces Home and the viewport's default camera. Re-pick retains the current angle rather than constructing a new camera. Hover text uses the themed WPF ToolTip with a 16-pixel cursor offset. Member identities use element:<ElementId> and connect preview clicks to comparison rows. Targets are non-pickable context. Empty-space clicks clear row selection. Target hover does not replace member tooltips. Selected members use cyan emphasis and a 1.6-pixel all-edge outline. Target fill opacity is 0.12. Target and member edges use the palette’s cyan-gray color. The stable presenter owns lighting and camera bounds constraints. Status remains visible while the scene prepares or degrades. Navigation buttons disable when no scene exists. Both grids use a final stretch Status column with a minimum width. Thrown zoom/reset exceptions log a warning and appear in the preview status line. Fit failures log a diagnostic; reset without a Home attempts Zoom to Fit. A projection failure clears the rendered scene and shows its cause until the scene changes or the presenter becomes unavailable. Without a specific reason, the placeholder reads 3D Preview is unavailable: the presenter is unavailable. A graphics-device or WPF D3DImage failure permanently disables the presenter for that window. StructuralPreviewDevice releases resources once and does not forward Reinitialize to the native effects manager. It does not substitute WARP for the D3DImage bridge. The placeholder asks the user to update the graphics driver or enable GPU acceleration and reopen the tool. Preview navigation disables, but adjustment, Apply, Cancel, and target re-pick remain available outside an active apply. Re-pick retains the unavailable presenter and does not retry graphics initialization. Profile extraction reports expected unsupported geometry per type. Unexpected geometry, transaction, cleanup, or cancellation faults propagate. One Info summary records total/extracted/unsupported counts. Per-type progress is Debug. Selection-hook logs suppress per-event start/completion banners and report evaluation changes only when state changes. Data and contracts The technical specification defines AdjustmentPlan, target meshes, graph ordering, rounding, element tags, and system storage. Workflows Use Run Extreme Roof Framing on the Testing panel. Pick a linked floor or roof. Press Esc to switch to host target selection. Pick a host target if needed. Esc at this stage cancels launch. Select source columns and beams, then Finish. Review the target, comparison rows, tolerance, and preview. Apply when the tolerance is valid, at least one row requires modification, and no row has Error status. Sources must be point-based structural columns or straight non-brace framing in the host document. Material names matching \bconcrete\b case-insensitively exclude members. The source set needs a column or a beam that connects to a model column under ERFT's hierarchy rule. Unsupported extracted sources fail launch rather than disappearing from the plan. Edit ERFT on contextual Modify tabs restores a selected system's stored plan and settings. Missing or incompatible storage fails edit launch. Re-pick hides the window with HideForPick, selects another target, and reuses the same shell and preview presenter with the rebuilt plan. Re-applying calculates from current model geometry and offsets. During apply, a second Apply or Re-pick request is ignored. Cancel and window close are blocked. A successful apply reports its result and closes the window. An expected apply failure keeps the window open. A thrown apply exception closes the window and propagates to safe execution. Escape clears both comparison-grid selections and does not close the window. Cancel has no WPF IsCancel route. Clicking an empty area of either grid with any mouse button clears both selections. See the alert and preview contracts for event severity, ownership, and validation. Testing Pure tests cover graph construction, target projection, adjustment/rounding, storage admission, scene projection, window selection, close gating, modal lifetime, and injected device creation failure during re-pick and Apply. Core tests exercise presenter recovery and resource release without a GPU. Presentation's hosted StructuralPreview3DTests covers fit-as-Home through the renderer. Revit-hosted FramingAdjustmentEndToEndTests uses gm_test_model.rvt and transient host floors with real beam and column instances. It covers seed viability, target extraction, calculation, offset writes, tags, and DataStorage inside rolled-back transaction groups. A Revit 2027 case checks legacy-schema cleanup on 2027/Regression/realtest_model.rvt without saving the model. Linked-target behavior requires a Revit-hosted check with a loaded linked floor or roof. ./build.sh BuildSelectedLocalTests --TestProjects DBTools.ERFT.Local.Tests -y 2026 ./test.sh test --tool ERFT --scope local -y 2026 --fixture FramingAdjustmentEndToEndTests Limitations Unsupported member profiles omit those members from the preview. With no successful profiles, the preview contains only the target. Graphics failure requires a new window to initialize another presenter; calculation and Apply remain available in the existing window.

developer-guide/tools/experimental/recor.title: Record Set technical specification | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/experimental/recor.summary: Record Set technical specification Overview Record Set builds a package from selected RVT host files and their file-based external references. It copies files, optionally processes DWG Xrefs, and rewrites references in copied RVT files through TransmissionData. The source is src/Tools/Experimental/RecordSet/. Record Set describes application composition and window interactions. Architecture Domain values describe files and plans. Planning constructs ordered work; Execution dispatches filesystem, CAD, and Revit operations. Record Set architecture lists composition and presentation owners. Data and contracts Data contracts Features/Domain owns these values: Type Contents SourceFile Read-only Name, Path, LinkType, and nullable 64-bit LinkId. Mutable Discipline, Building, CadHandlingMode, BindType. Manual child list HostModel HostFile and read-only Links collection ExternalReferenceKey NormalizedPath plus typed LinkType PlanOptions Nullable AutoDiscoverCadXrefs and AllowCadRepath PlanContext TargetFolder, SelectedHosts, Options, and computed CommonLinkKeys ExecutionPlan Ordered Items, TotalBytes, PredictedOutputBytes, Summary, Fingerprint PlanSummary Hosts, UniqueLinks, CopyBytes, PredictedOutputBytes, Items PlanMessage Info, Warning, or Block severity and text SourceFile.CreateHost, CreateDiscoveredLink, and CreateManualCadXref construct source values. Discipline defaults to empty. Building defaults to -. Blank building input normalizes to -. CAD mode defaults to Inherit and bind type defaults to Bind. Destination paths belong to immutable PreviewDestination projections, rather than mutable source-file properties. Enum Values LinkType Rvt = 0, Dwg = 1, Other = 2 CadHandlingMode Inherit = 0, AddXrefs = 1, BindAll = 2 BindType Bind = 0, Insert = 1 ExecutionStatus Ok, Cancelled Inherit resolves to AddXrefs during planning. A null PlanOptions flag follows Core Console availability independently for each preview. The UI initially shows unchecked flags, publishes their effective values after preview, and preserves explicit user choices for the window lifetime. These options are not persisted. Destination rules PlanningService.BuildContext counts normalized source-path/type occurrences. Keys appearing at least twice become common links. Identity uses the complete normalized path and type, not just a filename. The count includes repeated references within one host. TargetPathRules computes intended paths: File Destination Host with building {target}/{building}/{discipline}/{name} Host without building {target}/{discipline}/{name} Noncommon link with building {target}/{building}/{discipline}/Linked Files/{name} Noncommon link without building {target}/{discipline}/Linked Files/{name} Common link {target}/Common Linked Files/{name} Blank or - building omits that segment. Empty discipline adds no directory segment. The destination allocator compares normalized paths. Reusing the same source/destination needs no extra copy. A different source colliding with a destination receives name (2).ext, then (3), and so on, with a warning. Allocation fails when the counter exceeds 10,000. Mappings and preview projections use the allocated destination. Safety policy PolicyReader loads the embedded resource DBTools.ToolConfigs.RecordSet.recordset_policy.json from Policies/recordset_policy.json. It does not load a user-side policy file. JSON member Shipped value or rule allowed_target_roots Nonempty required list. Shipped root is \\fileserver\Projects verify_after_copy Required Boolean, shipped false min_free_bytes Required nonnegative number, shipped 10,737,418,240 denied_extensions .dwl, .dwl2, .tmp, .bak, .lnk, .exe allowed_extensions Optional deny_globs Required list, shipped *backup*.rvt, *.old, ~$* paths.enable_long_paths Required Boolean in required paths object, shipped false delete_mode Defaults to quarantine. No plan action consumes it require_sentinel_for_delete Defaults true. No delete action consumes it Configured string entries must be nonblank. Roots must be absolute Windows drive-letter paths or complete UNC server/share paths. Relative, drive-relative, root-relative, and incomplete UNC roots fail admission. Malformed or incompatible policy throws. It is not normalized into valid data. Preview checks the target against admitted roots. Execution reloads policy and checks it again. The containment predicate admits equality with the root and descendants. Before acquiring the lock, execution checks every output-bearing plan path: directories, copy destinations, CAD repath hosts/roots, bind hosts, Revit hosts, and mapping destinations. Copy sources, mapping keys, and Revit source hosts remain source paths. Execution requires free space minus max(TotalBytes, PredictedOutputBytes) to meet MinFreeBytes. Safe filesystem operations resolve existing file and directory redirects before checking containment. Recursive copies carry destination checks into every nested operation. Lock, sentinel, and manifest mutations repeat containment checks. Copies overwrite existing destination files and preserve the source file's UTC creation, last-access, and last-write timestamps. Optional verification compares SHA-256 hashes, including every allowed file in a copied directory. It verifies copied bytes before later CAD/Revit mutations. Workflows Host import and reference reading FileSelectionWorkflow owns OS pickers. HostImporter normalizes picks, rejects existing or repeated hosts, and calls PlanningService.ScanHost with empty discipline and building -. A RevitOperationException or scan warning rejects that host and returns an ordered issue. Owner-token cancellation propagates. The application displays issues and adds only accepted hosts. RevitOperations implements IExternalReferenceReader and ITransmissionWriter. It strips long-path prefixes before passing paths to Revit. Missing TransmissionData or external-reference collections fail with operation and host context. Reference reading uses desired data when IsTransmitted is true and last-saved data otherwise. Library references (PathType.Content, including library-located keynote or assembly-code tables) are omitted. Absolute references retain their stored path. Relative references resolve against the source host folder. For a workshared local, the base is the file-system central folder from BasicFileInfo.CentralPath. Without a usable file-system central path, resolution uses the reference's saved absolute path. A moved package with intact relative structure therefore resolves its own files. The scan creates discovered links using their resolved paths and host metadata. It classifies RVT, DWG, and Other external references. It does not recursively scan linked RVT models. Plan construction and limits Features/Planning/Preview/PreviewPlanBuilder.BuildPlanAsync performs these stages: Find Core Console and resolve nullable CAD flags. Plan hosts and non-CAD links under the file policy. Plan each distinct DWG destination once, using its first occurrence's CAD options. Append Revit repath operations for copied hosts with allowed mappings. Check sources, count bytes, estimate bound output, enforce limits, and compute the fingerprint. Denied hosts or links produce warnings. Missing planned source paths produce Block messages. Directory copies count only policy-allowed files. TotalBytes counts each distinct source/destination copy pair, including repeated copies of one source to different destinations. PlanSummary.UniqueLinks is the number of distinct copy-source paths, including host paths. Hosts is the selected-host count. Items includes directory and message items. Limit Value Result when exceeded PlanningLimits.MaxTotalBytes 80 × 1024³ bytes Block PlanningLimits.MaxTotalItems 10,000 Block PredictedOutputBytes starts at TotalBytes. For Bind All, the estimate adds allowed discovered Xref sizes beyond the copied host DWG size. Estimate failure produces a warning and retains the existing estimate. These are preview limits, not guarantees of final package size. Plan items and progress Plan items are typed records. PlanAction supplies their dispatch identity. Record Data Fingerprint action Fingerprint keys Weight FsCreateDirItem Path fs_create_dir path 1 FsCopyItem Source, Destination fs_copy src, dst 3 CadCopyItem Source, Destination cad_copy src, dst 3 CadRepathItem Host, NewRoot cad_repath host, new_root 2 CadBindAllItem Host, BindType cad_bind_all host, bindtype as invariant numeric enum text 4 RevitRepathItem Host, SourceHost, Mapping revit_repath host, source_host, map:{source} per mapping 2 UIWarnItem Message ui_warn msg 0 UIInfoItem Message ui_info msg 0 Progress increases after an item completes, using its weight divided by the total weight, with a minimum denominator of 1. It is an operation estimate, not byte progress. Each item emits an action string and ordinally sorted key=value fields separated by |. Revit mappings use map:{source} keys. Fingerprinting hashes successive UTF-8 item segments with SHA-256, without an extra separator between segments, and keeps the first 16 lowercase hexadecimal characters. It records plan identity for the audit output. Execution does not use it as a content checksum. CAD planning For AddXrefs, the planner copies the DWG and allowed manual Xrefs beside it. With discovery enabled and Core Console available, it scans the tree and copies unique referenced paths beside the destination DWG, allocating collision suffixes when necessary. When repath is enabled, it appends CadRepathItem using the destination DWG directory as NewRoot. Discovery failure logs a warning and uses heuristic copying. Disabled discovery or unavailable Core Console also uses heuristic copying: copy existing sibling directories named xrefs, xref, refs, ref, external, dwg, or cad. Each source/destination directory pair is copied once. Heuristic copying does not rewrite Xrefs. The planner emits Info messages Auto-discover CAD Xrefs disabled. when discovery is disabled with Core Console present, or AutoCAD Core Console not found. DWG Xrefs copied by heuristic only. when Core Console is absent. Explicitly enabling both discovery and repath without Core Console produces Block. BindAll requires Core Console. Without it, preview produces Block and schedules no bind operation. With it, the plan copies the DWG and appends bind work, without manual or discovered Xref copy work. Selecting BindAll clears manual children. Bind and Insert select AutoCAD BINDTYPE 0 and 1 respectively. Bind preserves Xref-prefixed names. Insert merges names and can produce naming conflicts. Core Console boundary CoreConsoleRuntime.FindCoreConsole searches: An existing path from ACCORECONSOLE. accoreconsole.exe in PATH order. AutoCAD 2026, 2025, and 2024 under C:\Program Files\Autodesk. DWG TrueView 2025 under the same directory. Each run extracts an embedded DBTools.ToolCad.RecordSet.* script to a unique temporary .lsp file and attempts deletion in finally. Deletion failures log a Warning. CoreConsoleRunner starts both redirected reads immediately and returns immutable standard output, standard error, and exit code. It creates a temporary .scr file that loads and invokes the extracted LISP script: accoreconsole.exe /i "<input.dwg>" /s "<temporary.scr>" Cancellation terminates the owned process tree and observes terminal stream completion. The runner attempts .scr cleanup on every exit and logs deletion failures. Execution rechecks Core Console availability for each CAD repath or bind item. If it is missing, the executor logs the affected DWG path and throws InvalidOperationException rather than using heuristic copying. Script and function Argument Behavior rs_list_xrefs.lsp, rs-list-xrefs Host DWG path Enumerates Xref blocks and emits nested JSON rs_repath_xrefs.lsp, rs-repath-xrefs host.dwg\|new_root Strips matching root prefixes from Xref paths and saves rs_bind_all_xrefs.lsp, rs-bind-all-xrefs host.dwg\|BIND or host.dwg\|INSERT Sets BINDTYPE, binds *, purges three times, quick-saves Discovery requires a zero exit code and parseable JSON between the first { and last } in output. The root requires an xrefs array. Every node requires a non-null children array with non-null nodes. Host, node name, and node path can be blank. Blank paths do not expand into copy work. The JSON fields are host, xrefs, name, path, overlay, and children. The shipped scanner emits overlay: false rather than detecting overlay state. See Limitations for the scanner failure and the paths repath cannot resolve. The repath script receives a root rather than the planner's source-to-copy mapping and strips a case-insensitive matching root prefix. CadExecutor checks only the repath process exit code. Bind requires both a zero exit code and an output marker containing "ok":true. Revit repath RevitRepathItem.SourceHost preserves the source reference base while Host names the copied RVT. Mapping keys are normalized source paths and values are allocated output paths. The writer reads effective references, skips Content references, and matches against the source base. It sets desired paths while preserving effective loaded/unloaded state. TransmissionWriteResult.UpdatedCount is zero for no matching changes. The writer leaves the copied RVT untouched in that case. A positive count causes TransmissionData to be written with IsTransmitted = true. A rewritten workshared copy opens detached and cannot create new locals while transmitted. Reference failures preserve operation, host, reference ID, old/new path context, and original causes through RevitOperationException. Owner cancellation remains cancellation. Execution, cancellation, and audit files ExecutionPlanExecutor.ExecuteAsync validates preconditions, creates runtime metadata, acquires the lock, writes the sentinel, executes items in order, and writes an outcome manifest. It always attempts lock release after successful acquisition. The UI passes CancellationToken.None and shows a non-cancelable overlay. Lower owners honor supplied cancellation at work boundaries. Execution is not dispatched to a worker thread. Outcome Result Successful execution ExecutionStatus.Ok, ok manifest Owner cancellation before lock acquisition Cancelled, empty run ID and manifest path Owner cancellation after acquisition Cancelled, cancelled manifest, lock release Unexpected fault or foreign cancellation Attempt failed manifest, release lock, propagate failure Manifest-write, diagnostic, or lock-release failures remain visible with the primary failure. A cancellation-manifest failure preserves both cancellation and write exceptions. Preflight failures fault the returned task and create no manifest. The UI displays (none) when no manifest exists and preserves known sentinel state for pre-lock cancellation. Runtime paths are: {target}/.recordset.lock {target}/.recordset_sentinel {target}/_recordset_manifests/{run_id}.json Run IDs use UTC yyyyMMdd-HHmmss plus four random lowercase hex characters. The lock uses FileMode.CreateNew, FileShare.None, and UTF-8 contents: run_id={run_id} fingerprint={fingerprint} Acquisition invokes no external log callback after creation. A write/dispose failure attempts partial-lock deletion before propagating. After acquisition, logging and all later work are inside the release boundary. The sentinel is opened or created and remains after completion. There is no package deletion or quarantine plan action. SafeOperationRuntime.TrashRoot names _RS_TRASH/{run_id} but execution does not use it. The manifest has this shape: { "run_id": "20260113-154200-a1b2", "fingerprint": "0123456789abcdef", "target_root": "C:\\Output", "utc": "2026-01-13T15:42:00Z", "summary": { "hosts": 1, "unique_links": 3, "copy_bytes": 1000000, "predicted_output_bytes": 1500000, "items": 8 }, "status": "ok" } SafeWriteManifestRequest carries only the five summary scalars and Status. Execution projects these from PlanSummary. Operations does not depend on the planning aggregate. The manifest records summary and status. The lock prevents concurrent Record Set executions at one target. Inspect the log and manifest before cleaning output or retrying a failed run. Remove a stale lock only after establishing that its execution is no longer active. Manage Items The Options menu opens discipline or building catalogs through ManageDisciplinesCommand and ManageBuildingsCommand. ManageItemsWindowViewModel exposes AddCommand, RenameCommand, and DeleteCommand. Add trims NewName and requires nonblank input. It ignores case-insensitive duplicates and clears NewName after adding. Rename requires a selected item and nonblank RenameTo, trims the replacement, and rejects case-insensitive duplicates. It replaces the item in place, invokes the rename callback, selects the replacement, and clears RenameTo. Delete requires a selection, removes the item, invokes the delete callback, and clears selection and RenameTo. MetadataCatalogWorkflow returns the ordered catalog edits for the App view model to apply to host/link metadata. The dialog's default Close button closes without accepting a separate result payload. UI contracts PreviewWorkflowState requires a current preview, allowed target, and no Block messages before Process can run. Async Add Hosts, Sync Preview, and Execute commands use nonthrowing safe execution and restore busy state. Debounced preview handles expected owner cancellation separately. For Ok and Cancelled results, the production overlay reports completion and an alert shows status and manifest path. An execution failure shows no completion alert. RecordSetWindowViewModel runs Execute through RunWithoutThrowingAsync with SafeExecutionOptions.ErrorBanner and a null notifier, so the failure is logged and the logger window is surfaced, but no banner appears and the exception does not propagate. Execution progress appears in the main window overlay. Testing See Record Set testing for fixture boundaries and window lifetime requirements. Limitations The scanner calls the undefined AutoLISP function vl-file-syst-exists-p before opening an Xref. DWGs with Xref paths therefore fail discovery and use heuristic copying. CAD repath cannot repair relocated or collision-renamed Xrefs. Execution leaves completed file mutations in place after a failure; its manifest is not a rollback journal. Containment checks and filesystem writes are separate operations, so concurrent path replacement can race validation.

developer-guide/tools/experimental/recor.title: Record Set | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/experimental/recor.summary: Record Set Overview Record Set copies Revit host files and external references into a target directory and rewrites copied references. It previews an ordered plan before executing filesystem, CAD, and Revit TransmissionData operations. Execution copies files and rewrites references in plan order. See the technical specification for formats, ordering, safety checks, and CAD limitations, and the user guide page for the window. Architecture Source ownership Source and manifest: src/Tools/Experimental/RecordSet/. The manifest places Record Set on the Testing panel with InlineUi, order 60, and icon key recordset. Command and availability use DBTools.RecordSet.App.Composition.RecordSetCommand. The module is DBTools.RecordSet.App.Composition.RecordSetToolModule. Owner Responsibility App/Composition Module, command, registration, AppLauncher, and AppLaunchDependencies App/Views Main raw view and RecordSetWindowSession App/ViewModels Binding state, RecordSetWindowServices, debounce, and interaction sequencing App/DesignTime Designer binding surface and DesignTimeSampleFactory Features/Domain Files, hosts, plan options, plan items, summaries, and messages Features/Planning Host import, plan context, destination rules, preview Features/Execution Progress workflow, preflight, item dispatch, outcome handling Features/Operations Filesystem, Windows paths, Revit and CAD ports/adapters, safe-operation requests Features/Policy Embedded policy loading and file filtering Features/Metadata Catalog editing and neutral CatalogEdit results Features/ManageItems Catalog editor view, view model, and modal session AppLauncher constructs RecordSetWindowServices beside its consumer, RecordSetWindowViewModel. MetadataCatalogWorkflow returns ordered edits. The App view model applies them to host rows and linked-file metadata. Feature workflows do not import App row types. Stable controls and the byte converter live in src/DBTools.Presentation/Tools/RecordSet/. Raw views merge the versioned Presentation theme and contain stable WPF types. Designer sample construction reuses PreviewTreeBuilder and locates the selected DWG by file identity at any depth. Presentation and lifetime The main modal shell loads DBTools.ToolViews.RecordSet.RecordSetWindow.xaml through ToolWindowFactory. It uses title Record Set, size 1240 × 780, minimum 980 × 640, CenterScreen placement, and a taskbar entry. Manage Items loads DBTools.ToolViews.RecordSet.ManageItemsWindow.xaml with a bound title, size 520 × 420, minimum 420 × 300, CenterOwner placement, and a taskbar entry. Its Close button is the default button, so Enter closes the dialog. Both Close buttons use ButtonCommandCloseBehavior.ExecuteAndClose and honor the session close gate. User close returns false. With Debug Mode on, the logger window opens after the main dialog closes. Tree containers bind IsSelected and IsExpanded two-way. The stable selected-item behavior reports view selection through a OneWayToSource binding to SelectedTreeNode. A rebuilt preview reselects the same SourceFile and expands only its ancestor chain. Explicit selection changes or a missing file cancel pending reselection. Right-click selects and focuses a row or tree item. Right-clicking a Hosts row other than the current item makes it the sole selection, including when it already belongs to a multi-selection. Rows allow logical focus but remain outside Tab navigation. Options opens below its button. CAD actions require a selected DWG leaf. Manage Disciplines, Manage Buildings, Auto-discover CAD Xrefs, and Allow CAD repath remain disabled until hosts exist. Metadata Add new choices defer the prompt, preserve the prior value on cancellation, and never store the sentinel as metadata. Plan-message bindings use OneTime. CAD bind commands accept the view's string values Bind and Insert. Retirement releases the preview timer and deferred prompts synchronously. Active preview or execution work produces a Dev Mode retirement failure. Idle retirement disposes the view model and services without a dispatcher frame. Data and contracts The technical specification defines file identity, destination allocation, plan items, policy, and output manifests. Workflows Use Choose an allowed target folder. Add host RVT files. Assign discipline and building metadata in the Hosts grid. Review the destination tree and Info, Warning, or Block messages. Configure DWG actions through the selected DWG's context menu. Run Process when the preview is current and has no blocking messages. Duplicate host picks produce issues and are skipped. A host with a failed reference scan is rejected. It does not become an empty row. Canceling a file or folder picker preserves the current state. Target, host, metadata, and CAD changes invalidate the preview immediately. RecordSetPreviewSyncCoordinator debounces automatic refresh by 350 ms at DispatcherPriority.Normal. Preview planning runs through Task.Run and publishes on the UI context. Execution remains on its caller context and uses a non-cancelable progress overlay. Busy state disables editing, CAD actions, options, and ordinary window close. The footer reports Root, Free, ACAD, and Sentinel status. Root is Pending, Allowed, or Blocked; Sentinel is Pending, Present, or Missing. ACAD shows the Core Console path or Unavailable. Testing The Pure project references the normal desktop tool project, which owns its source and resource mapping. Pure fixtures cover domain, planning, preview, execution, filesystem policy, CAD process handling, view models, and catalog editing. Revit-hosted tests under Tests/Integration/Revit/ cover TransmissionData and WPF application behavior. WPF fixtures share WindowRuntimeScope, which releases only runtime state it installs. The hosted bootstrap supplies the Revit owner. Modal tests use ToolWindowDialog.Show with synchronous callbacks and a ten-second watchdog. The watchdog cannot interrupt native code or callbacks that do not pump the dispatcher. The CAD selection test uses a modeless test session to await preview/edit cycles outside a modal callback. It checks the selected node, ancestor expansion, CAD state, and manual Xrefs after rebuilds. Production remains modal. The execution fixture checks real copied bytes, the manifest, and lock release. Filesystem tests cover destination junctions and redirected manifest paths. Limitations Execution has no UI cancellation action and can leave partial output on failure. Inspect the log and outcome manifest before retrying or removing output. CAD discovery and repath limitations are specified in the technical specification.

developer-guide/tools/experimental/vtc-s.title: View Template Comparer (VTC) specification | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/experimental/vtc-s.summary: View Template Comparer (VTC) specification Overview This page specifies the data contract of View Template Comparer (VTC): what it reads from a view template, how it keys and compares settings, and how it applies, copies and stores them. The VTC developer guide describes the architecture. Architecture TemplateExtractor and RevitLinkSettingsAdapter read snapshots. TemplateDifferenceEvaluator compares them; TemplateApplier applies selected changes. TemplateStorage owns cached JSON. See VTC architecture for composition and views. Data and contracts Scope VTC compares two view templates of the current document. Category edits stay staged locally until Process. Imported categories are ordinary category rows on their own tab. Revit-link settings are limited to settings that the public Revit API can both read and write. VTC reads and writes a setting through the public API or does not handle it. Tabs The tree follows the Visibility/Graphics dialog. SettingTab values: ModelCategories AnnotationCategories AnalyticalModelCategories ImportedCategories Filters RevitLinks Worksets DesignOptions CategoryTabClassifier sends a model category with a positive ID (an imported DWG, SAT or similar category) to ImportedCategories. Internal categories, which the dialog does not show, are classified as model categories. Other category types keep their native tab. Imported categories Extraction emits imported parents and their layers and subcategories as CategoryGraphicsData. Layers and subcategories inherit the imported parent's tab. Imported rows keep SettingType=CategoryOverride and use the same compare pipeline as every other category. There is no import-specific apply path. Inline edit, Inspector edit, Preview, pending overrides, batch apply, merged save and snapshot apply all use the standard category path. A selection whose side is missing resets visibility and graphics as for any other category row. Revit links Data TemplateSnapshot.RevitLinks is a list of RevitLinkSetting records: public sealed record RevitLinkSetting( long LinkElementId, RevitLinkTargetKind TargetKind, // RevitLinkType or RevitLinkInstance string LinkName, string LinkDisplayName, RevitLinkSettingKind SettingKind, RevitLinkSettingValue Value); Each row is one target and one native setting. VTC extracts both RevitLinkType and RevitLinkInstance targets; they are keyed, labeled and copied separately. Setting kinds RevitLinkSettingKind has 11 values, all members of RevitLinkGraphicsSettings: Kind Kind LinkVisibilityType ColorFill LinkedViewId ViewRange ViewFilterType Phase NestedLinks PhaseFilter ObjectStyles ViewDetailLevel Discipline The adapter binds all 11 kinds directly to typed public API members for Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) and Revit 2027. Extraction RevitLinkSettingsAdapter.Extract enumerates link targets, reads View.GetLinkOverrides(...) (a new RevitLinkGraphicsSettings when there are none) and emits one row per setting kind. Simple settings use the native LinkVisibility or ElementId value. Phase, Phase Filter, Detail Level and Discipline use their public getter and setter and are stored as one row each. Linked element names are read from the linked document when it is loaded. These names identify Linked View, Phase and Phase Filter across models. Keys and comparison RevitLinkDiffEvaluator keys each row as link.{type|instance}.name.{LinkName}.{SettingKind}, for example link.type.name.ARCH_Model.rvt.LinkVisibilityType. LinkName is the only cross-model key. Compare, save, load and apply all use it; there is no element-ID key. If a key is ambiguous within a target kind, compare throws InvalidOperationException ("Revit link key '...' is ambiguous. ..."). TemplateDifferenceEvaluator compares typed SettingValue cases. DiffTreeBuilder groups the rows under Revit Links by LinkDisplayName, with one leaf per setting kind. Library storage TemplateStorage stores saved templates as JSON in the VTC cache directory (AppPaths.GetToolCacheDir("VTC")). It is the only code that derives cache file paths. Callers use logical template names. A rooted name, or a name with a path separator, is rejected before any path is derived. SavedTemplateInfo exposes only the name and modification time. Load and save accept only one complete TemplateSnapshot shape: required top-level members and collections must be present, explicit nulls and invalid nested elements are rejected, and the same validation runs before an in-memory snapshot is saved. There is no normalization and no recovery of other formats; incompatible data raises TemplateStorageException. Saved Revit-link rows must have a non-blank LinkName and LinkDisplayName, defined TargetKind and SettingKind values and a value valid for the kind: a visibility mode from 0 to 2, no mode for linked-view IDs, a detail level from 0 to 3, a defined discipline, and no enum value for other kinds. GetSavedTemplates returns an empty list when the cache directory does not exist, without creating it. Other enumeration failures raise TemplateStorageException (operation enumerate). TemplateExists returns false for a missing file or directory. Other probe failures raise TemplateStorageException (operation probe), so the save is refused instead of overwriting. Only SaveTemplate creates the directory. An existing name is replaced only after the user answers Replace; otherwise the file is written with overwrite disabled, so a template that another process saved under the name after the probe is kept and the save fails with TemplateStorageException. MergedTemplateBuilder writes RevitLinks rows like any other diff rows. Revit-link rows take part in Preview, Process, Create Merged and merged save. Sources: src/Tools/Experimental/VTC/Domain/Template/TemplateSnapshot.cs, src/Tools/Experimental/VTC/Features/Library/Operations/TemplateStorage.cs, src/Tools/Experimental/VTC/Features/RevitLinks/. Workflows Apply and copy Apply Applying a Revit-link row reads the current link overrides, changes only the selected setting and writes the settings back with View.SetLinkOverrides(...). Targets are resolved by LinkName only. Linked View, Phase and Phase Filter are remapped by linked-element name. Dependent rows first set the required top-level visibility mode. A selection whose side is missing resets only that setting to its host default. Applying from the Revit-link modal uses BatchApply in one VTC Process Apply transaction, with one sub-transaction per setting and one Undo entry. A missing comparison key is an ElementNotFound conflict; an unexpected fault rolls back the whole apply. Copy The context menu of a concrete link group or leaf row (not the Revit Links tab root) has Open Revit Link Settings... and Copy Revit Link Settings To.... Opening the modal from a leaf row shows the full group of that link target, so the modal always shows all 11 kinds. A successful modal apply refreshes the main comparison. The modal and the copy command work on one template side. RevitLinkActionSourceResolver selects the only side with a value, or a viable selected side, and reports "no Revit-link value" or a real two-sided ambiguity without showing UI. On ambiguity App asks which template to use; it never defaults to Left. Copy uses TemplateRuntime.GetRevitLinkTargets() and CopyRevitLinkSettings(...) and always copies all 11 kinds. Each target is copied in its own transaction; the transactions run in the Copy Revit Link Settings transaction group (started through RevitTransactionGroups.Begin) and are assimilated into one Undo entry. An expected failure skips only that target and is logged; an unexpected fault rolls back every target. Linked View, Phase and Phase Filter are copied by finding the source linked-element name in the target linked model; raw linked-document IDs are not copied across models. If the source linked document is unloaded and the name is not available, the raw ID is reused only when source and target reference the same linked model. Otherwise copy fails. Testing See VTC testing for Pure and Revit-hosted fixture inventories. Limitations A Revit-link key must be unique within its target kind. Cross-model Linked View, Phase, and Phase Filter remapping requires the linked-element name. When the source link is unloaded, raw IDs are reused only for the same linked model; copying to a different linked model fails.

developer-guide/tools/experimental/vtc.h.title: View Template Comparer (VTC) | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/experimental/vtc.h.summary: View Template Comparer (VTC) Overview View Template Comparer (VTC) compares two Revit view templates of the current document, stages category edits locally, and applies the selected differences and eligible pending overrides through one command, ApplySelectedChangesCommand (button label "Process"). It can also create a merged template and save templates to a local library. The data contract (tabs, imported categories, Revit-link settings, keys, apply and copy rules, library storage) is in the VTC specification. Architecture Source: src/Tools/Experimental/VTC/. The manifest registers DBTools.VTC on the Testing ribbon panel with InlineUi, order 50, and icon key vtc. Command and composition VtcCommand is the Revit entry point. It validates the command context and calls App/Composition/VtcWindowLauncher. VtcWindowLauncher owns the modal launch: it resolves the document's templates, shows an alert when there are none, has VtcWindowCompositionFactory build the collaborators, and creates VtcWindowSession through Core's ToolWindowFactory. After the dialog closes it opens the logger window when Debug Mode is on. It always retires the comparer and linked-file windows; a dialog failure is reported before any retirement failure. VtcWindowCompositionFactory creates one graph per document: TemplateExtractor, RevitLinkSettingsAdapter, TemplateDifferenceEvaluator, TemplateApplier, TemplateMaterializer, TemplateStorage (cache directory AppPaths.GetToolCacheDir("VTC")) and the one document facade, TemplateRuntime. TemplateRuntime (Revit/Template) resolves template IDs and exposes compare, extract, batch apply, create merged, apply model, Revit-link targets and copy, and line and fill pattern queries. App batch-session code depends on the App/Sessions/ITemplateSessionRuntime port, which TemplateRuntime implements. VtcWindowSession owns the modal window session. ToolWindowFactory supplies the stable shell for the raw VTC view. Comparison owns the workspace, Inspector and Preview views; Library owns its workspace view; the Revit-link modal reuses the Comparison diff control. AlertPresenter is the only alert boundary in App. Composition gives the alert service only to the presenter; view models and workflows use the presenter for standard alerts, custom requests and selections. VtcWindowBatchWorkflow handles App session reactions for Process and Library work. The App view model owns Revit-link prompts, modal hosting, refresh and result presentation. TemplateRuntime passes Revit-link batch apply and copy, and the classification of expected conflicts, to Template Apply. VtcWindowCommandRuntime reports a refused operation through SafeExecutionRefusalReporter as VTC {operation}. Sources: src/Tools/Experimental/VTC/Revit/Template/TemplateRuntime.cs, src/Tools/Experimental/VTC/Features/TemplateApply/Execution/TemplateApplier.Operations.cs, src/Tools/Experimental/VTC/App/Composition/VtcWindowCompositionFactory.cs. Source layout VTC has several features under Features/, each with its own domain, planning, state, Revit and UI code: Path Content Features/Comparison Diff tree (DiffTreeBuilder, DiffTreeIndex, DiffTreeNode, DiffTreeProjector), preview projection, window comparison state (VtcWindowComparisonCoordinator), category tab classification and RevitLinkActionSourceResolver Features/Library TemplateStorage, SavedTemplateInfo, TemplateStorageException Features/RevitLinks RevitLinkDiffEvaluator, RevitLinkSettingsAdapter, RevitLinkTargetResolver, the Revit-link settings window Features/TemplateApply TemplateApplier partials, pending overrides (PendingOverrideState), apply results and conflicts, MergedTemplateBuilder, SnapshotSelectionPolicy, pattern rendering and override editors Features/TemplateComparison.cs, Features/TemplateDifferenceEvaluator.cs Host-neutral comparison result and evaluator Domain/ Tool-wide vocabulary: TemplateSnapshot, SettingDifference, SettingValue, SettingTab, RevitLinkSetting, RevitLinkSettingKind, RevitLinkSettingValue, RevitLinkTarget, RevitLinkTargetKind and the graphics data types Revit/Template TemplateExtractor, TemplateMaterializer, TemplateRuntime App/ Composition, sessions, view models, views and design-time data TemplateDifferenceEvaluator is host-neutral. TemplateExtractor and RevitLinkSettingsAdapter own the Revit mechanics behind TemplateRuntime. SettingDifference.LeftValue and RightValue hold typed SettingValue cases. Compare, apply and App code pattern-match these cases. Display settings use VTC enums (DetailLevel, DisplayStyle, PartsVisibility, ViewDiscipline, ShowHiddenLinesMode); conversion to Revit enums happens only at the Revit API boundary. SettingPreviewItem and DiffTreeProjector.ViewFilter are Comparison contracts, so feature projections do not import App view models. DiffTreeNode holds comparison and display state only. PendingOverrideState holds pending override DTOs with no tree or UI dependency. TemplateApplyResult is the only apply outcome; the App view model (TemplateApplyOutcomeProjection) projects it onto setting keys for row feedback and filters and stores no outcome on comparison nodes. DiffTreeBuilder only builds a tree from differences. DiffTreeIndex keeps the rebuilt roots and owns key lookup, canonical node paths, selection collection in tree order and Revit-link subtree queries for the coordinator, the preview projection and the Revit-link modal. MergedTemplateBuilder (Features/TemplateApply/Planning/MergedTemplate) builds the merged TemplateSnapshot from the comparison result, the selections, the base side and the name. View-model operations only orchestrate effects. App composes outcome templates into Comparison views at runtime; Comparison raises only selected-node, override-edit and preview-setting requests for App to coordinate across panes and modals. Views VTC views are raw XAML EmbeddedResource items with explicit logical names: DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.VtcWindow.xaml (main view) DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.AlertBodyTemplates.xaml DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.ComparisonWorkspaceView.xaml DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.ComparisonInspectorView.xaml DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.ComparisonPreviewView.xaml DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.DiffViewControl.xaml DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.LibraryView.xaml DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.RevitLinkSettingsWindow.xaml VtcWindowSession loads the main resource through ToolWindowFactory and owns the one-time owner attachment and cleanup. VTC has no custom close gate and no native pick loop. Shared resource dictionaries are in DBTools.Presentation/Tools/VTC/: VtcDiffViewStyles.xaml and VtcComparisonViewStyles.xaml. The namespace DBTools.Presentation.Tools.VTC holds the converters VtcConflictConverter and VtcRawViewConverter. VtcResourceTemplateSelector resolves App outcome templates and returns an empty template in a standalone view. Alert bodies use full type-name string keys with TypeNameTemplateSelector. Every content and item slot has an explicit template; immutable record values bind OneTime and mutable view-model state uses INotifyPropertyChanged. Each raw view merges Theme once, before the VTC dictionaries; the shared dictionaries do not merge Theme. Vtc.TreeView is based on the implicit TreeView style with VTC overrides; each tree sets its own scrolling and virtualization. Named item selectors set TextSearch.TextPath for prefix typing and automation names on their template text. SavedTemplateInfo, ViewFilterOption, LinePattern, FillPatternData and TemplateOption return their display label from ToString(), so automation peers and text fallbacks show the label. Preview navigation is available only for navigable setting keys. Double-click override editing responds to the left mouse button only, on eligible rows. Keyboard focus moves to the comparison row after the Inspector tab loads. Pending focus and close requests are canceled on retirement. The linked dialog's context-menu selection commands bind to its own view model. The raw linked view has the automation name "Linked file override differences". The main window initializer uses the log prefix VtcWindow. Data and contracts The specification defines tabs, typed setting values, imported categories, Revit-link identity, and library storage. Workflows Process and merged templates ApplySelectedChangesCommand applies the selections and eligible pending category overrides in one VTC Process Apply transaction, with one SubTransaction per setting so an expected conflict rolls back only that setting. An apply failure becomes a per-setting conflict only after its sub-transaction confirms RolledBack. If the rollback throws or reports another status, the batch stops with a BatchApplyException that contains the apply failure and then the rollback failure. An unconfirmed rollback never publishes a pending-override conflict key. Create Merged (TemplateRuntime.CreateMergedTemplate) runs template creation and the pending-override batch in one transaction group, Create Merged View Template, started through RevitTransactionGroups.Begin and assimilated into one Undo entry. Expected per-setting conflicts are reported and the new template is kept. Any other fault rolls the group back and leaves no template, so a retry with the same name works. TemplateMaterializer copies the Left template with ElementTransformUtils.CopyElements and a duplicate-type handler that keeps destination types, so Revit shows no dialog. It catches no copy failure: a fault rolls back the group and reaches RunOrReport as an Error alert. VtcWindowBatchWorkflow.SavedTemplates treats template extraction or merge and the cache save or delete as the change. After that change, the list refresh has its own error boundary: a refresh failure is logged with the template name and shows one warning that the cache operation succeeded; success is shown only after the refresh succeeds. Both save commands ask Replace saved template 'X'? through AlertPresenter before they overwrite an existing name; Cancel writes nothing. Testing DBTools.VTC.Pure.Tests (no Revit host): DiffTreeBuilderTests, DiffTreeIndexTests, DiffTreeNode*Tests, DiffTreeProjectorTests: grouping, selection state and change notification, including imported-category tabs and Revit-link grouping by link name. PendingOverrideStateTests, PendingCategoryOverrideTests: staging, eligibility, restore, clear, merge-save application and failed-pending collection. TemplateApplyOutcomeProjectionTests: keyed conflict and success projection for row feedback and result filters. TemplateStorageTests: the real storage service with a temporary cache directory, including imported-category data and RevitLinks rows. The project references the VTC product assembly directly, not DBTools.App. TemplateDiffEvaluatorTests, RevitLinkDiffEvaluatorTests: snapshot comparison over SettingDifference rows. RevitLinkActionSourceResolverTests: sole-side, selected-side, ambiguous-side and no-value resolution. AlertBodyTemplateProviderTests: the provider and its raw DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.AlertBodyTemplates.xaml resource (WPF only). VtcRawXamlParseTests: the linked-file view's accessible name and its view model passed to the composed diff view. Raw comparison view tests use the registered ToolWindowFactory session and the stable behavior bindings. Revit-hosted tests (the local scope) in DBTools.VTC.Local.Tests open the GM and SGT test models, create temporary templates and roll back every change after each run: VtcWindowViewModelTests: Process, Create and link flows around real template extraction, apply and creation, alert orchestration and the Revit-link modal and copy. RevitLinkBaselineTests: extract and apply round trips of LinkVisibilityType and LinkedViewId on RevitLinkType and RevitLinkInstance targets in sgt_test_model.rvt. RevitLinkExtendedTests: the other RevitLinkGraphicsSettings members on the SGT linked model. RevitLinkSnapshotRemapTests: snapshot compare and apply with deliberately mismatched target and linked-element IDs, LinkName pairing and linked-element-name remap failures. ImportedCategoryRoundTripTests: imports a shared CAD file inside the rollback scope and checks that imported categories use the normal category compare and apply path. SgtModelExtractionTests, GmModelExtractionTests: extraction from existing views and presence of link targets in the open models. Limitations Comparison requires two view templates in the same document. Revit-link settings are restricted to the public API; linked-element remapping requires a resolvable name or the same-model ID condition in the specification.

developer-guide/tools/structural/analyti.title: Analytical Snap To Level | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/structural/analyti.summary: Analytical Snap To Level Overview Analytical Snap To Level moves selected analytical members to a chosen level elevation. Beams move both endpoints. Columns move the endpoint nearest the target elevation and retain the other endpoint. X and Y coordinates remain unchanged. A column tie moves the start endpoint. Related tool: Framing Joins. Architecture Registration manifest.yml registers DBTools.AnalyticalSnapToLevel with the command and availability type DBTools.AnalyticalSnapToLevel.App.Composition.AnalyticalSnapToLevelCommand. The button uses InlineUi, icon key analytical_snap, and order 20 on the Structural panel. The assembly is DBTools.AnalyticalSnapToLevel. Data and contracts Snapper API The public snapper boundary is: public AnalyticalSnapper(ITransactionRunner tx, Document doc, ILogger logger); public (int ProcessedCount, IReadOnlyList<(ElementId ElementId, string Reason)> Skipped) Run(ICollection<ElementId> selectedIds, Level targetLevel); AnalyticalSnapper.Run(ICollection<ElementId>, Level) returns ProcessedCount and an ordered list of (ElementId, Reason) skips. AnalyticalSegment.SnapTo owns the pure endpoint rule. AnalyticalSnapper resolves the typed Revit structural role, constructs the adjusted line, and calls SetCurve. A processed member counts even when its endpoint elevations already match the target. Skips and diagnostics Reason Constant on AnalyticalSnapper Condition not an analytical member NotAnalyticalMember Missing element, wrong category, or wrong runtime type role not supported RoleNotSupported Structural role is neither Beam nor Column not straight NotStraight Curve is not a Line would collapse WouldCollapse Adjusted length is less than Application.ShortCurveTolerance The completion alert groups skips in first-seen reason order. Each group shows its count and at most ten element IDs, followed by and N more when needed. The non-analytical group shows only its count. Debug logs include the target level, per-element skip or success, and final totals. Workflows Use Select analytical members. Run Analytical Snap To Level on the Structural panel. Choose a level from the elevation-sorted level picker. Read the processed and skipped counts in the completion alert. The ribbon accepts any nonempty selection through CommandAvailability.HasSelection. Processing requires OST_AnalyticalMember and an AnalyticalMember instance. See Limitations for supported roles and curves. The tool has no persistent settings. Execution Source: src/Tools/Structural/AnalyticalSnapToLevel/. App/Composition/AnalyticalSnapToLevelCommand resolves Features/AnalyticalSnapToLevelWorkflow. The workflow uses IAlertService for the level picker and completion alert, ITransactionRunner for changes, a window-owner provider, and a typed logger. It ensures the logger window through ILoggerWindowHost after successful completion when Debug Mode is enabled. All members run in one DB Tools - Snap Analytical Elements to Level transaction. Unexpected failures, including a SetCurve refusal, propagate to safe execution and roll back the entire run. An empty selection or a missing level choice produces SafeExecutionRefusedException. The level picker returns no choice when the document contains no levels. Testing Pure tests cover endpoint geometry through AnalyticalSegmentTests and AnalyticalSegmentEdgeCaseTests. Revit-hosted workflow tests cover skip-summary behavior. Revit integration tests live under Tests/Integration/Revit/ and exercise the command, workflow, and analytical curve changes. Limitations Only straight analytical members with role Beam or Column are processed. The tool preserves X and Y and does not change unsupported roles or curved members.

developer-guide/tools/structural/foundat.title: Combined Foundation Tags | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/structural/foundat.summary: Combined Foundation Tags Overview Combined Foundation Tags updates pier/footing association parameters and moves combined tags to footing corners. Source: src/Tools/Structural/FoundationTags/. The assembly and tool ID are DBTools.FoundationTags. Architecture Ownership App/Composition/FoundationTagsToolModule binds settings, registers the pack, and delegates feature registration to ServiceCollectionExtensions.AddFoundationTagsFeatures. Features/UpdateCombinedFoundationTagsWorkflow and Features/Move/MoveCombinedFoundationTagsWorkflow own manual execution and completion reporting. Queued result-selection gates receive the workflow logger. Pure geometry types are Point2D, FoundationTagsPoint, FootingCornerPoints, and NearestPointResult. FoundationTagsGeometry owns SelectCornerByViewOrientation, FindNearestPoint2D, and IsValidCornerName. Commands Ribbon command Identity Split-button order Update Combined Foundation Tags DBTools.UpdateCombinedFoundationTags 0 Move Combined Tags DBTools.MoveCombinedFoundationTags 1 Both use InlineUi on the Structural panel in split group foundation_tags. Their command and availability classes are UpdateCombinedFoundationTagsCommand and MoveCombinedFoundationTagsCommand under App/Composition. Icon keys are update_combined and move_combined. Organize Foundation Types occupies order 2 in the same group. Data and contracts Settings Configuration section: Tools.FoundationTags. Pack: structural.foundation_tags, titled Combined Foundation Tags. AutoUpdateEnabled defaults to true. Pattern lists default empty and resolve to: Property Default pattern TagFamilyPatterns ^DB Pier and Foundation Combined Tag(?: No Elevations)?$ PierFamilyPatterns ^Foundation Pier(?: - Round)?$ FootingFamilyPatterns ^(?:Footing\|Pile Cap)-Rectangular$ The UI allows three patterns per group through Core RegexPatternListContext. It validates syntax and tracks pending changes. FamilyNameClassifier compiles the configured patterns for both workflows. Workflows Update Features/CombinedFoundationTagsUpdater collects visible FamilyInstance elements from the active view. Configured family patterns classify piers and footings. Updates affect host-document instances. Compute each pier's top as Top Level elevation plus Top Offset. Write Foundation Pier Top by GUID. Find the nearest pier to each footing using XY location points, within two feet inclusive. Write that pier's type mark to Associated Pier and its top to Associated Pier Elevation. Publish current-run result IDs and timestamped selection sets. A missing or invalid Top Level records a pier failure. Missing Top Offset uses zero. Piers without LocationPoint cannot participate in nearest-point matching. Equal-distance ties retain the first candidate. Without a pier, the updater clears the association text to an empty string. It keeps a stored elevation and reports failure because these length parameters cannot be cleared. Parameter.ClearValue requires HideWhenNoValue, which the shipped definitions do not set. An elevation without a stored value needs no clearing. Double writes compare values rounded to two decimal places in internal feet. String comparison is ordinal. UpdateParameterWriter returns failures for missing, read-only, wrong-storage, or rejected parameter writes. The updater records these failures and continues. A footing can appear in both Modified and Failed sets when one parameter changes and another fails. Unexpected exceptions escape the parameter transaction and roll back the run. Parameter writes and selection-set publication use separate transactions inside one transaction group. The group assimilates to one Undo entry. A selection-set failure preserves committed parameter writes, then propagates after assimilation. Other failures attempt group rollback and preserve concurrent cleanup faults. UpdateRunResult contains UpdatedCount, FailedCount, and read-only snapshots of Modified and Failed IDs. The manual workflow offers Select Modified and Select Skipped when updates exist. Those banner actions check that the source document is still active before selecting IDs. With no updates, it shows an Info or Warning toast without selection actions. Selection sets use DB Tools - FoundationTags - Modified Elements (...) and DB Tools - FoundationTags - Skipped Elements (...) names with Eastern-time timestamps. Repeated names receive suffixes starting at (2). Pruning retains five sets across both kinds, ordered by descending element ID. Move Features/Move/MoveCombinedFoundationTagsRunner collects visible IndependentTag instances, resolves a tagged host or linked structural foundation, and filters tag family/type names by the configured patterns. Only the host tag moves. Linked footing geometry transforms into host coordinates. The desired name is the trimmed tag name, or its type name when the tag name is blank. Supported values are case-insensitive Top Right, Top Left, Bottom Right, and Bottom Left. The runner tessellates fine-detail footing geometry, including nonvisible objects, in the instance's local frame. Local XY extents define four rectangular corners. FoundationTagsGeometry.SelectCornerByViewOrientation labels them against the view's RightDirection and UpDirection. The edge most aligned with view-right becomes horizontal. A tie uses the second declared edge. The tag retains its current Z. Unsupported names, missing point locations, and geometry without usable corners are skips. All candidate moves share DB Tools - Move Combined Foundation Tags. Unexpected transform, geometry, tessellation, or tag-write errors log the tag ID and propagate, rolling back every move. MoveRunResult separates moved, skipped, candidate, total-view-tag, structural-foundation, and pattern-rejection counts, with rejected-name samples for diagnostics. Prerequisites and repair Manual commands and automatic updates validate shared parameters without modifying them. The required definitions are owned by Features/Prerequisite/PrerequisiteRequiredParameters: Parameter GUID Type Instance category Initial group Associated Pier 7f6c2c2a-46ab-4e78-9bf6-9b9c2ef8f7d1 Text Structural Foundation Identity Data Associated Pier Elevation 6d9b0f7f-4f7a-44a4-9c5c-0c0f4bf0da21 Length Structural Foundation Identity Data Foundation Pier Top 93de44b8-bb7c-4e58-a7e0-9a3a1c8e4d70 Length Structural Columns Constraints Invalid prerequisites activate core.structural.combined_tags and refuse manual commands with SafeExecutionRefusedException. Safe execution shows a Warning banner and logs a Warning without a stack. Unexpected validation faults remain errors and do not assert invalid prerequisites. Use Settings → Combined Foundation Tags → Refresh to inspect the active document. Use Fix (Install/Repair) or Install/Repair Required Parameters to repair it. Construction of the settings context is passive and shows a Refresh prompt. SettingsRuntime receives the settings host's UIApplication explicitly. Refresh replaces immutable RequiredParameters status rows. Their six column bindings use OneTime. HasWarning belongs to the session context and is not persisted in FoundationTagsSettings. Install/Repair uses embedded definitions in group DBTools.Structural.FoundationTags. It creates a temporary shared-parameter file, restores Revit's original shared-parameter path, and attempts temporary-file deletion. The embedded definitions supply the required parameters. Repair deletes conflicting definitions with the same required name and a different GUID, including duplicate-name collisions. It preserves other categories and the existing group when extending a binding. An instance binding already containing the required category remains unchanged. A type binding becomes an instance binding with its existing categories plus the required category. Revit drops the type values and the installer logs a Warning naming the parameter.
