The updater accesses these parameters by GUID. The warning disables Update, Move, and Organize Foundation Types. Its title is Combined Foundation Tags Disabled. Clear it after resolving the prerequisite issue. Automatic updates and monitoring CombinedFoundationTagsAutoUpdateTask runs Update in FloorPlan and CeilingPlan views when enabled and no warning blocks it. Invalid prerequisites set the warning and show a banner once per document session through PrerequisiteBannerLedger. NotApplicable and TransientNotReady evaluations skip execution. An unexpected runtime fault sets no prerequisite warning. Core's ViewActivationHook suppresses the failed task for that document session. PrerequisiteMonitorTask checks prerequisite state and schedules an Idling retry for transient initialization states. PrerequisiteRetryCoordinator retains each original event source and detach callback. Evaluation faults log and can be checked again on the next view activation. The monitor disposes its own retry coordinator at synchronous App shutdown. An injected coordinator remains caller-owned. Disposed lifetimes reject scheduling. Failed-detach entries retain cleanup state without retry work. A late Idling event can retry detachment. Testing Pure tests cover geometry, rotated views, corner names, regex classification, prerequisite lifecycle, and write results. Revit-hosted tests under Tests/Integration/Revit/ cover commands, modules, updates, moves, monitoring, repair, and settings. ./test.sh test --tool FoundationTags --scope local -y 2026 Limitations Association updates use host-document pier and footing instances. Move supports host tags referencing host or linked foundations and only the four listed corner names. Length values cannot be cleared with the shipped shared-parameter definitions.

developer-guide/tools/structural/framing.title: Framing Joins | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/structural/framing.summary: Framing Joins Overview Framing Joins allows or disallows joins at both ends of selected structural framing instances. The tool has no persistent settings. Architecture Source The implementation and manifest are under src/Tools/Structural/FramingJoins/. The project references Core and the Revit API. Data and contracts Commands Command Manifest identity Operation Allow Join DBTools.AllowJoinSelected Calls StructuralFramingUtils.AllowJoinAtEnd for ends 0 and 1 Disallow Join DBTools.DisallowJoinSelected Calls StructuralFramingUtils.DisallowJoinAtEnd for ends 0 and 1 Both commands use InlineUi and the Structural panel's framing_joins split button. Their manifest order is 0 and 1, respectively. The icon keys are allow_join and disallow_join. Availability uses CommandAvailability.HasStructuralFramingSelection. Workflows Use Select structural framing elements. Run Allow Join or Disallow Join. Read the completion banner for the processed instance count. Execution App/Composition/AllowJoinSelectedCommand and DisallowJoinSelectedCommand resolve Features/FramingJoinsWorkflow through their CommandService registration. The workflow receives ITransactionRunner, ILoggerWindowHost, a window-owner provider, and a typed logger through dependency injection. The workflow reads the current selection, filters by OST_StructuralFraming, removes duplicate IDs, and retains only elements that resolve to FamilyInstance. An empty selection or a selection without usable framing instances produces SafeExecutionRefusedException. FramingJoinTargetBuilder owns the category filter. FramingJoinsWorkflow.ExecuteCore owns the endpoint loop. All targets run in one transaction named DB Tools - Allow Join Selected or DB Tools - Disallow Join Selected. The count increases after both endpoint calls succeed. It counts processed instances, including instances whose join state already matches the request. An endpoint failure logs the exception and element ID, then throws InvalidOperationException with the original cause. The transaction rolls back the complete batch. A successful batch shows a six-second completion toast and ensures the logger window when Debug Mode is enabled. Testing Pure fixtures FramingJoinTargetBuilderTests and FramingJoinsWorkflowTests cover filtering and endpoint execution. Revit-hosted fixtures FramingJoinsCommandTests and FramingJoinsWorkflowRevitTests cover command and Revit integration. Limitations The tool processes FamilyInstance elements in Structural Framing. It does not alter joins for other selected elements.

developer-guide/tools/structural/joist-g.title: Joist Girder Weights | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/structural/joist-g.summary: Joist Girder Weights Overview Joist Girder Weights estimates pounds per linear foot and writes the result to a writable Double parameter named Wt. It scans structural framing in the active document. The ribbon command runs manually. A view-activation task runs automatically when enabled. Architecture Ownership and registration Source: src/Tools/Structural/JoistGirderWeight/. Owner Responsibility App/Composition/JoistGirderWeightToolModule Module, settings pack, hooks, and warning registration App/Composition/ServiceCollectionExtensions Dependency registration App/Composition/UpdateJoistGirderWeightsCommand Manual command Features/Workflow/WeightUpdateWorkflow Settings retrieval, update, completion/configuration banners Features/AutoUpdate/AutoUpdateTask View-activation execution Features/JoistGirder/JoistGirderClassifier Family and load-name classification Features/JoistGirder/JoistGirderWeightUpdater Revit collection, validation, and writes Features/Load/Operations/ElementLoadReader Parameter and unit resolution Features/Load/LoadParser Text parsing Features/Load/LoadResolutionEvaluator Load group ambiguity and precedence Features/JoistGirder/JoistGirderWeightEvaluator Pure formula Features/JoistGirder/Settings/Views/JoistGirderWeightSettingsView.xaml Settings view manifest.yml registers assembly DBTools.JoistGirderWeight and module DBTools.JoistGirderWeight.App.Composition.JoistGirderWeightToolModule. The command uses InlineUi, icon key joist_girder, and ribbon order 30. The asset is Assets/joist_girder_icon.png. Data and contracts Inputs The configured regex tests the family name. It tests the type name only when the family name is blank. The default family pattern is: ^(?:(?:[BV]?G)|Vulcraft) Joist Girder$ It matches G Joist Girder, BG Joist Girder, VG Joist Girder, and Vulcraft Joist Girder. Input Resolution Constraint Number of joists Number of Joists, SpaceNum, Number of Equal Spaces Greater than 1 Span Cut Length, Length Positive internal feet Depth Depth Positive internal feet Load Total/point load, or dead plus live load Nonnegative kips Output Wt Writable Double on the instance or type Numeric aliases are checked in the listed order, with instance then type lookup for each name. Load resolution prefers instance parameters over same-named type parameters. It rejects multiple populated matches in any Total, Dead, or Live group, even when a Total value exists. One Total value takes precedence over Dead plus Live. Without Total, exactly one Dead and one Live are required. Force-typed Double values convert from Revit internal units to kips. Unitless numeric values are kips. Text uses invariant numeric parsing and accepts these units: Units Conversion to kips Omitted, k, kip, kips Unchanged lb, lbs, lbf, pound, pounds Divide by 1000 kN, case-insensitive Multiply by 0.2248089431 Examples are 10, 10 kips, 10000 lb, and 45 kN. Blank, negative, malformed, or unsupported-unit text produces an input issue. Formula Features/JoistGirder/JoistGirderWeightEvaluator.EstimateWeight(n, load, lengthFeet, depthFeet) returns lb/ft. The calculation converts length and depth to inches. panelSpacing = lengthInches / n numberOfPanels = n - 1 totalReaction = loadKips * numberOfPanels / 2 maxMoment = totalReaction * lengthInches / 2 For even n, subtract loadKips * panelSpacing * i for integer steps starting at 1 while i < numberOfPanels / 2. For odd n, subtract loadKips * (panelSpacing / 2 + panelSpacing * j) starting at 0 while j < numberOfPanels / 2. effectiveDepth = depthInches * 0.95 chordForce = maxMoment / effectiveDepth requiredArea = chordForce / (50.0 * 0.6) topChordWeight = requiredArea * lengthInches * 0.28356 * 1.06 bottomChordWeight = topChordWeight * 1.13 webWeight = topChordWeight * 0.7 weightPoundsPerFoot = (topChordWeight + bottomChordWeight + webWeight) / lengthFeet 50.0 is the stress constant in ksi. 0.28356 is steel density in lb/in³. The remaining constants are depth, connection, and member multipliers. Settings Configuration section: Tools.JoistGirderWeight. Pack key: structural.joist_girder_weight, titled Joist Girder Weights. Property Persisted default Effective default AutoUpdateEnabled true true FamilyNamePattern Empty string Family pattern above DeadLoadPattern Empty string (?:^DL$\|Dead\s*Load) LiveLoadPattern Empty string (?:^LL$\|Live\s*Load) TotalLoadPattern Empty string (?:Point\s*Load\|Total\s*Load) For example, the Total pattern matches Point Load, Panel Point Load, Total Load, and Total Load - User Defined. Features/DefaultPatterns owns defaults. Settings/SettingsPackContext derives from SettingsPackAutoUpdateContext<JoistGirderWeightSettings> and owns pattern editing, empty-value defaulting, regex validation, snapshots, and baseline comparison. The Core base owns the toggle, warning, pending-change, and notification state. Workflows Update and failure behavior JoistGirderWeightUpdater validates candidates and computes weights before opening a transaction. Invalid candidates become skipped items. Valid candidates share Auto Update Joist Girder Weights. An unexpected transaction or setter exception propagates and rolls back that transaction. Updated increments after each setter call returns. See Limitations for count semantics. The returned summary contains Candidates, Updated, Skipped, and up to five sample issues. Zero candidates returns an empty summary. All-invalid candidates return skipped counts. The manual workflow displays an Info toast when nothing updates, Warning for mixed updated/skipped results, and Success when all candidates update. Configuration exceptions produce a ten-second Warning toast. Automatic execution catches configuration exceptions, sets the configured warning, and shows a banner. Other runtime faults propagate to Core's view-activation handling. Warning core.structural.joist_girder disables DBTools.UpdateJoistGirderWeights and automatic updates. Testing Pure tests cover the evaluator, classifier, patterns, load parsing and resolution, and settings context. Revit-hosted updater and workflow tests use real Revit parameters and roll back model changes. The workflow fixture supplies a WPF owner for banners and closes its own windows after each test. ./test.sh test --tool JoistGirderWeight --scope local -y 2026 Limitations The formula estimates weight; it does not select manufacturer sections or validate SJI load tables. Updated counts reflect attempted writes whose setters did not throw, including a false Parameter.Set result that leaves the value unchanged.

developer-guide/tools/structural/organiz.title: Organize Foundation Types | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/structural/organiz.summary: Organize Foundation Types Overview Organize Foundation Types renames foundation family types, assigns type marks, and merges types with equal dimensions. It processes all matching types in the active document. It does not use the current selection or persistent settings. Architecture Registration and ownership Source: src/Tools/Structural/OrganizeFoundationTypes/. Owner Responsibility App/Composition/OrganizeFoundationTypesCommand Manifest command, active-document availability Features/FoundationType/OrganizeFoundationTypesWorkflow Confirmation, organizer invocation, completion alert, Debug logger window Features/FoundationType/FoundationTypeOrganizer Collection, dimension comparison, rename, merge, deletion Features/TypeMark/TypeMarkGenerator Mark generation and pure formatting helper Features/TypeMark/TypeMarkPolicy Preserve or overwrite mode manifest.yml registers DBTools.OrganizeFoundationTypes as an InlineUi split-button item in foundation_tags, order 2, icon key organize_types. Update Combined Foundation Tags and Move Combined Tags occupy orders 0 and 1. The structural.foundation_tags pack's core.structural.combined_tags warning disables all three commands. A typical documentation workflow runs this organizer, then Update Combined Foundation Tags, then Move Combined Tags. Data and contracts Families and parameters The family-name comparison uses StringComparison.Ordinal. Family Category Dimensions Prefix Sort order Foundation Pier Structural Columns b, h P b * h Foundation Pier - Round Structural Columns d RP Diameter Footing-Rectangular Structural Foundation Width, Length, Foundation Thickness F Width, length, thickness Pile Cap-Rectangular Structural Foundation Width, Length, Foundation Thickness CAP Width, length, thickness All sorts are ascending. Dimensions use Double parameters. Type marks use the String parameter Type Mark. Dimension text uses Revit's feet-and-fractional-inches formatter. Missing dimension parameters display ?. Duplicate keys use the nullable raw dimension values. Marks and names Family group Mark format Name format Example Rectangular pier P-{n}, starting at 1 {b}x{h} ({mark}) 2'-6"x2'-6" (P-1) Round pier RP-{n}, starting at 1 {d} DIA. ({mark}) 2'-0" DIA. (RP-1) Footing or pile cap {prefix}-{widthFeet}.{n}, starting at 0 {width}x{length}x{thickness} ({mark}) 3'-0"x3'-0"x1'-0" (F-3.0) widthFeet is the floor of the width in internal feet. Each family group maintains its own ordinal set of marks encountered during processing. Generation searches from the starting counter for an unused mark in that set. It does not reserve marks on types that have not yet been processed. The confirmation asks whether to overwrite existing marks. Yes selects TypeMarkPolicy.OverwriteExistingTypeMarks. No selects PreserveExistingTypeMarks. Preserve mode generates marks only for blank values, but still renames types and merges duplicates. SetParam leaves a missing, non-String, or read-only Type Mark unchanged, so a generated name does not guarantee a mark write. Workflows Processing and transactions Collect and sort the four family groups. Compare each type's dimension tuple with retained types in its group. For a duplicate, reassign its instances to the retained type. For a retained type, assign its mark when permitted and rename it. Delete successfully merged source types after processing the group. The first successfully retained type for a dimension tuple becomes the merge target. Dimension comparison is exact. Each rename/mark operation and duplicate reassignment runs through a nested transaction-runner call. A failed reassignment rolls back that type's changes and records a skip. The organizer deletes a duplicate only after all its instances change type. All groups share the outer DB Tools - Organize Foundation Types transaction. A deletion error logs at Error and propagates, rolling back the complete operation. Per-type failures log at Debug and increment the skip count. The final warning and completion alert include skipped totals and up to five type id: reason samples. The alert also reports renamed and merged counts. Testing Pure TypeMarkGeneratorTests covers sequential numbering, gaps, width groups, prefixes, and invalid arguments. Revit-hosted OrganizeFoundationTypesTests covers confirmation, completion reporting, duplicate merges, and document changes inside a rolled-back fixture transaction group. Limitations Family names must match the four listed names exactly. Dimension equality is exact, including missing values; missing dimensions can therefore cause types to merge.

developer-guide/tools/structural/sgt-spe.title: Super Girt Tool (SGT) specification | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/structural/sgt-spe.summary: Super Girt Tool (SGT) specification Overview This page defines the Super Girt Tool (SGT) data, execution, persistence, and presentation contracts. Orientation analysis and resolved members Resolved member contracts Preview (Elevation, Section and 3D) and placement read the same resolved data. ResolvedMemberContractResolver builds one ResolvedMemberContract per member: identity (role, type, opening key and edge), orientation (warm-state key, canonical and probe rotation, Flip, Y and Z justification), the world line and frame, and the normalized section geometry from the exact warmed state. Preview does not compute transforms, signs or depths of its own. Opening members are listed once as OpeningMemberSegmentContract values (OpeningMemberContractCatalog); preview meshes, hit testing and placement enumerate that list, so segment order and index are the same in every preview mode and in the placed members. The resolver also derives the secondary section axis from the role and wall frame, so girts, headers and sills face the same way in the preview as when placed, also on mirrored or rotated walls. Warmed profile states Profile warming (ProfileWarmStateProbe) places temporary instances and captures one exact state per key of quarter-turn rotation, Flip state, raw Y and Z justification and horizontal or vertical axis mode (MemberProfile.ExactStatesByKey). Each probe applies the parameters in a fixed order: cross-section rotation (plus the wall compensation below), then Flip Facing, then Y justification and Z justification, then zero offsets, then one regeneration. Placement applies a resolved orientation in the same order. Rotated walls WallRotationCompensationEvaluator takes the wall's along-axis azimuth, finds the nearest right angle and returns the negated residual as compensation. Vertical roles (jambs) are probed at each canonical quarter turn plus that compensation; horizontal roles (girts, headers, sills) are probed at the canonical quarter turns only. Rows keep the canonical quarter-turn values (0, 90, 180, 270). Placement adds the compensation to the cross-section rotation of vertical members only. Opening frame direction When the wall frame is swapped relative to the linked wall (IsFrameSwapped), live openings are mirrored along the wall: start and end become length − end and length − start. Preview and placement use the resulting along-wall distances; there is no separate branch for mirrored links. Seating rules Orientation analysis (FamilyOrientationAnalyzer) tries each Y and Z justification pair on a probe instance, regenerates once per pair and measures web and flange seating. Web seating mode (WebSeatingMode): open sections (Channel, Zee, Angle) in horizontal roles use EdgeContact; HSS sections and jamb roles use FaceCoplanar. Zee and Angle types are not offered for opening roles. Seating planes: a girt's web seats on the elevation plane. Head, sill and jamb web seating planes use the structural target origin, including layer and wall offsets, not the raw wall-frame origin. Mirrored links: the flange must seat on the negative side of the depth axis for a mirrored link and on the positive side otherwise. Square HSS: every non-end-cap face is a candidate web and flange face, and either seating side is accepted. Rectangular HSS: calibration records deep and shallow face IDs (HssDeepFaceIds, HssShallowFaceIds). Horizontal roles seat a deep face on the exterior plane; jamb roles seat a deep face on the opening-edge plane. Without that metadata, the larger of the web and flange face sets counts as deep. Angles: for girts, the short leg is the web face and the long leg is the flange face (AngleShortLegFaceId, AngleLongLegFaceId). Faces are resolved again after each regeneration, because Revit geometry objects are not stable across regenerations. Non-finite distances or dot products reject a candidate pair. Temporary probe transactions report Revit blocking failures as type warnings or failures in the analysis result (TemporaryTransactionRunner). Plan admission and synchronization PlanStore.Initialize prepares and validates a candidate before it replaces the live plan or advances its revision. A rejected initialization keeps the accepted plan and sends no event; a successful one publishes one initialized event after the lock is released. Plan admission rejects duplicate member keys. Undo of a segment deletion relies on unique keys to match surviving group rows. Every Plan and PlanBaselineSnapshot has a required WallTarget. Host wall, linked wall and link-instance IDs are 64-bit through persistence, Revit lookup, hashing, opening identity, placement and preview. Opening element IDs and compound-wall material IDs are also 64-bit; manual-opening surrogate IDs and layer indexes are int. Plan.Clone() detaches each mutable collection that UI projection uses: editable girt and opening rows, runtime member and opening definitions, baseline lists, type options, layer snapshots, orientation and profile maps, grid collections and the execution context. Shared leaf values are immutable. PlanStore owns a detached accepted plan. Initialization copies its input before it prepares or stamps it. Reads and notifications return detached snapshots. Update is the write boundary. Rejected changes and mutator exceptions keep content and version; a no-op update publishes no event. An accepted update advances the version once and detaches the candidate before storage, so a retained reference cannot change accepted state. Notifications run outside the write lock. Shared wall-layer collections are read-only. Member segment replacement materializes and filters candidates before it replaces the segments. Empty or all-short input, and enumeration failure, keep the previous segments. Replacement from the member's own segment view is valid. Plan-change admission uses one lock and one latest-pending slot: Enqueue clones the accepted plan and assigns a monotonic request revision. An arrival while a dispatcher callback is scheduled replaces the pending snapshot; the scheduled callback applies the latest revision. The apply turn clears the pending slot and marks itself applying before it projects. An arrival during apply fills the pending slot without recursion; completion schedules exactly one later Dispatcher.BeginInvoke turn. The coordinator does not pump frames and does not drop an arrival. The request revision identifies the refresh; Plan.Version is plan data and diagnostic context. If applying one snapshot fails while a newer one is pending, the pending dispatch is still attempted. If both fail, the first failure is reported first, and the failed dispatch resets admission so a later change schedules normally. PlanSynchronizationCoordinator.TryApplyPartialEdit owns every UI-originated partial plan write: the opening parent-row commit, the girt and opening segment flyouts, the PreviewEditingWorkflow entry points (snap, typed gap, segment delete, merge) and jamb segment add and delete. Each such write, and SyncPlanFromUI (the UI-edit preview pass, Place and Update, Change Review), refreshes every pane from the written plan before it returns. It applies the refresh its own write queued (ApplyPendingPlanRefreshOnUI, in the same ApplyPlanRefresh batch as every other plan refresh), so no queued pass or later write projects stale rows over the edit, and a field typed after the write keeps its text. Before it projects, the coordinator applies a refresh still queued by a plan written outside it (Undo or Redo of a preview-only edit, PlanStore.Initialize). It then projects the whole UI (TryProjectPlanFromUI) and writes the edit on top of that projection as one plan version, so unsaved valid drafts are written with it. Examples: a wall offset pushed on LostFocus whose Background sync has not run when a Send-priority opening commit arrives, or an edit made while a 3D scene builds. While any field is invalid it writes nothing, records no Undo entry and shows the blocked-sync status (Fix invalid fields, Fix invalid rows or Preview blocked). Only a write outside the coordinator still refreshes at Background priority; a field typed between that write and its refresh takes the refreshed value. Each writer builds its change from a detached copy of the projection. A PreviewEditOutcome is a pair of plan changes that PreviewEditingWorkflow writes once through the coordinator and then records, so Undo and Redo replay only that change and the drafts written with it stay. A rejected opening segment edit aborts the write. Deleting girt rows is a grid draft without a plan write and is never refused. GirtProjectionMapper.ApplyProjectedRowsToPlan normalizes every segment group in the projection with SegmentGroupRenumberer, so the next sync leaves no gap in the order, no parent key of a deleted row and no group of one row. Accepted typed gap edits enter the same history; Undo and Redo restore the previous raw override, and each accepted typed edit clears the redo branch. The 2D gap editor (PreviewView2DGapEditor) survives redraws: PreviewView2DState.ClearCanvas is the only canvas clear and keeps an open editor, its anchor is placed again under the current pan and zoom, and keys typed in it go to the editor. Undo and Redo bypass admission: they replace the plan and so every pane's fields. A refused type change (girt segment flyout, or an unavailable type in the girt grid) reports through GirtPaneViewModel.ShowRefusedTypeChange and sets no blocker. Only a girt row that keeps a rejected type, or an extent validation fault, sets the girt-pane blocker; the next girt row edit, row add or delete, bulk repair of that row or plan refresh clears it. EndpointAssociationOpeningEdgeSide is the only opening-edge type across extents, member gaps, preview editing and persistence. Domain/Extents/OpeningEdge owns the closed OpeningEdgeExtent, DualOpeningEdgeExtent and OpeningEdgeEndpoint family: named wall, fixed-distance, grid and neighbor-opening variants keep the persisted extent fields. Strings are used only where a UI label or a serialized composite key requires text. Preview girt segmentation carries MemberSpanEndpointKind from endpoint selection through ordinary and opening-edge gap resolution. Girt segment boundaries Domain/Girt/SegmentBoundary/GirtSegmentBoundarySet decides where a girt can start, end and split. For a girt at elevation z, an opening blocks it when the opening spans z (inclusive, 1e-6 ft tolerance), is framed, is not bypassed by the row, is not the row's interior opening, and has a nonzero width after its span is clamped to the wall. Start-capable boundaries: the wall start and the higher edge of each blocking opening. End-capable boundaries: the lower edge of each blocking opening and the wall end. The row's interior opening adds its lower edge as start-capable and its higher edge as end-capable. GirtSegmentBoundarySet.Split is the only girt segment computation. It omits every span shorter than MemberRules.MinimumLength (0.5 ft). Its callers: plan-row segmentation (GirtSegmentationReconciler), preview (PreviewGirtSegmentBuilder), placement (MemberSegmentResolver.ResolveGirtSegments), the usable-span check (MemberResolutionExtentsProjection.HasUsableGirtSpan) and the snap offer (GirtExtentSnapPlanEditor.ResolveBoundaryEdges). MemberSegmentResolver is an internal, girt-only resolver; WallHydrator resolves every member through it and rejects a non-girt member with MemberSegment/RoleUnsupported. GirtSegmentBoundarySource supplies the wall length, openings, grid positions and the framing predicate. FromOpenings has the only production predicate, which frames every opening. FromPlan builds the source from plan rows (segmentation, the resolver, the snap editor); MemberResolutionExtentsProjection.GirtBoundaries builds it from runtime opening definitions (preview, placement, usable-span check). TryResolveT clamps an opening edge to the wall like the boundary set. GirtSegmentationReconciler splits each segment group from its first sibling's start to its last sibling's end (clamped to the wall) and reuses row identities by overlap. The first and last child keep the group's outer anchors and endpoint gaps, also when Split omits an outer pier shorter than the minimum length; only ends between two children become opening-edge anchors. A group with one span becomes one row. A group with no span keeps its rows as authored, and placement reports them. An interior row leaves its segment group, and SegmentGroupRenumberer.RenumberSegmentGroup normalizes the remaining rows (a group of one row dissolves). Girt endpoint anchors Domain/Girt/EndpointAnchor/GirtEndpointAnchor is the stored anchor of one girt endpoint and the only reader of stored girt anchors. Its kinds: Kind Stored as Meaning Wall ExtentKind.FullLength Wall end Grid ExtentKind.Grid Grid line OpeningEdge ExtentKind.OpeningEdge, opening key + Left or Right Lower-T (Left) or higher-T (Right) edge of an opening Girt endpoints never use ExtentKind.MemberEdge; that kind is only for opening-member (jamb, header, sill) segments. Gaps: An opening-edge endpoint stores a user gap only in OpeningEdgeGapOverridesFeet["<key>:<Left|Right>"]. Otherwise the gap is derived from the jamb at that edge and elevation (GirtGapResolver.GetDefaultOpeningEdgeGapFeet), and is 0 when there is no jamb. GirtGapResolver.GetOpeningEdgeGapFeet is that rule; preview, the gap editor and placement all call it. StartGapOverrideFeet and EndGapOverrideFeet apply only to Wall and Grid anchors. Their rule is GirtGapResolver.GetEndpointGapFeet, called by preview (MemberGapResolver.GetEffectiveEndpointGapFeet), the gap editor and placement (GirtEndpointGapEvaluator.ComputeEndpointCutbackFeet): the override when set; otherwise, when the end lies within 1e-4 T of an edge that can bound it (a start on a higher edge, an end on a lower edge of a boundary opening in the girt's own boundary set), the gap derived from that edge's jamb; otherwise 0. When the plan cannot resolve a gap handle (for example the edge of an opening deleted before the preview redraws), PreviewEditingWorkflow.TryGetMemberGapFeet shows a Gap edit failed banner and no gap editor opens. Anchor writes: GirtPlanRow.SetAnchor clears the endpoint gap when it writes an opening edge. GirtPlanRow.ReplaceAnchor (snap edits, merges) also clears the gap entries of the old and new edges. GirtPlanRow.Reanchor (the resolver) clears the endpoint gap and the lost edge's entry and keeps the entry of the edge it moves to. GirtPlanRow.AbsorbPayload takes in a merged row's payload: bypass lists are united and gap entries are added; on a key conflict the receiving row's entry wins. The resolver merge (the survivor receives), the preview segment merge (the kept row receives) and the segmentation group proxy (the first sibling receives) use it. Interior intent is derived, not stored: a row whose start is the lower edge and whose end is the higher edge of one opening that it does not bypass spans that opening (GirtEndpointAnchor.FindInteriorOpeningKey, exposed as GirtPlanRow.InteriorOpeningKey). Re-anchoring GirtEndpointAnchorResolver.Resolve is the only re-anchoring rule. MemberSegmentationReconciler.Recompute runs it after opening-role normalization and before opening and girt segmentation. Recompute runs on each UI-edit or plan-mutation preview refresh, after committed opening edits, and in PreparePlacementPlan before Place or Update preflight; a render-only preview draws the plan as stored. An endpoint is lost when its grid is gone (GridRemoved), its opening is gone (OpeningRemoved), or its opening edge is not capable for that end in the row's boundary set (OpeningNotBoundary; for example the opening no longer spans the girt, lies outside a shortened wall or is bypassed by the row). A lost end uses the row's other end as reference: a start moves to the nearest start-capable boundary at or before reference − minimum length, an end to the nearest end-capable boundary at or after reference + minimum length. The wall ends are the fallback. When both ends are lost, the start moves to the wall start and the end to the first end-capable boundary at or after the minimum length. The re-anchored end loses its endpoint gap and the gap entry of its lost edge; the edge it moves to keeps its entry. Bypass keys and gap entries of openings no longer in the plan are removed. Siblings of one segment group that now overlap merge into the earlier sibling. The survivor keeps its member key; each side keeps the outermost anchor that was not re-anchored (with its gap); bypass lists and gap entries are united with GirtPlanRow.AbsorbPayload; opening-member targets that named an absorbed row are rewritten to the survivor; and the group is normalized with SegmentGroupRenumberer. Segmentation then splits the plan again and reuses identities by overlap. PlanSynchronizationCoordinator.NotifySegmentedStateRecompute reports MemberSegmentationSummary.ReanchoredGirtEndpoints ("Re-anchored N girt end(s) to the nearest opening or wall edge.") and MergedGirtRows ("Merged N overlapping girt segment(s) into their neighbors."). Snap edits GirtExtentSnapPlanEditor.Create accepts an opening edge for a girt's start or end only when IsBoundaryCapable finds it capable for that end in the boundary set of the edited row; otherwise it fails with GirtSnap/BoundaryInvalid. The snap removes that opening from the row's bypass list; a start on the lower edge of the opening whose higher edge is the end makes that opening interior. An edit that leaves no span of the minimum length fails with GirtSnap/NoUsableSpan. Create and ResolveBoundaryEdges apply the same test (IsBoundaryCapable, then HasUsableSpanAfterEdit over GirtSegmentBoundarySource.FromPlan), so ResolveBoundaryEdges offers exactly the edges Create accepts; an edit whose other end does not resolve fails with GirtSnap/NoUsableSpan. PreviewEditingWorkflow.ResolveGirtSnapEdges gives a handle on the row's own start or end that end's accepted set; any other segment handle is unrestricted. The snap index has no free-along target. Positions and progress Runtime resolution reports an opening-member split-label position more than 0.01 ft outside the wall through RuntimeHorizontalPositionResolution.OutOfRangeResult: a clamped T for rendering, OutOfRange = true and the reason SplitOutOfRange. Non-finite split text is invalid (MemberEdgeInvalid). A header or sill split label outside the wall fails placement with Extents/PositionResolutionFailed; preview can draw the clamped member. Grid positions are clamped to the wall. Stored girt endpoints accept only Wall, Grid or OpeningEdge; runtime AlongExtent still represents a resolved Wall-to-Grid span. Wall-analysis progress uses (string message, double? progress01) throughout. Non-null values are normalized to [0,1]; null means indeterminate. Framing orientation analysis returns one FramingTypeOrientationAnalysisResult value and passes no orientation records through progress. Profile warm-state extraction uses the caller's logger. Workflows Window session Lifecycle App/Sessions/WindowSession/WindowSessionLifecycle.cs owns the lifecycle states, close intent, startup outcome and finalization result. The modal driver is synchronous and always returns a completed task, because both Revit command callers block immediately. A relink hides the window, runs the synchronous picker, then calls ShowDialog again in the same command frame. One owned ContextIdle callback resumes target analysis after the window is visible. The driver rejects a modal return before the pick or shown handshake completes, and never posts the modal re-entry. WindowSessionOperationObserver observes the current initial-analysis or target-analysis task on the owning dispatcher. A completed task delivers inline; a pending task delivers through one owned dispatcher operation while the modal frame is active. Closing during analysis cancels the analysis and keeps the window and transaction group alive until the outcome arrives. Retirement revokes the callbacks and aborts the operation. Forced retirement clears commit intent, releases payload resources and publishes cancellation. If the synchronous picker is still on the stack, cancellation and transaction rollback wait until it returns; no target analysis or banner runs afterward. An ordinary Closed cleanup is a separate state and keeps an accepted commit. Native window and dispatcher references are captured before registration retirement. Transaction operations complete through the inline Revit call gate, before the command returns. App/Sessions/WindowSession/Revit/SgtWindowSession.cs supplies Revit picking and startup, window resource effects and error-boundary integration. RunModalFlowAsync is the production entry point. Launch uses a closed WindowSessionLaunchRequest: New requires a concrete WallTarget; Edit requires a non-default SystemId. WindowSessionBuilder requires an inline Revit call gate and rolls back construction failures with ordered cleanup. The command consumes only completed lifecycle tasks. Close and the transaction group The session owns one transaction group, Super Girt Tool. SGT refuses a document that is already modifiable at launch. Native X and Alt+F4 reuse the WPF close already in progress. An active analysis delays close until its outcome settles. An accepted Closed releases the mandatory preview and window resources, then finalizes the group inline. A successful close intent with a healthy, successful session assimilates the group; Cancel, errors and forced retirement roll it back. A programmatic close that throws, or returns without Closed, rolls back once and leaves a close-only retry for X, Alt+F4 and Cancel. The retry does not finalize again. No transaction is committed outside the session group. Model commit requires an explicit successful startup and model outcome and a healthy group. Failures of mandatory preview or window cleanup select rollback before assimilation. Synchronous transaction, cleanup and finalization failures propagate. App/Sessions/WindowSession/WindowSessionUIStatePersistence.cs saves only cosmetic state: expanded panels, column widths and bulk-edit defaults. It is best-effort and never gates or delays the model commit. Neither OK nor Cancel waits for the disk write. A successful commit with a pending save logs that preferences are saved in the background, without a banner. An already-failed save shows a warning through the Revit default-owner notifier after the close. A finally block always attaches the disk-task observer, also when finalization throws. The observer logs a later disk failure and does not touch the retired window. Cancel releases the transaction and window first, then observes the save without changing the Cancelled outcome. A failed cosmetic save does not change a completed model commit. Error boundary WindowInitializer attaches the Core error boundary of the window. WindowErrorBoundaryRegistry owns the dispatcher subscription and routes DB Tools failures to the most recently attached active window, or the most recently attached window when none is active. A DB Tools failure is thrown from, or passes through, an assembly named DBTools or starting with DBTools.; this includes DBTools.HandyControl and the Helix code merged into DBTools.Presentation, but not another add-in's HandyControl or Helix copy. WindowErrorBoundary classifies, presents and records the handled state. SgtWindowSession subscribes to its own boundary; a missing host fails session construction. When Core handles a failure on the SGT window, the session records the original exception and any presentation failure, requests a rollback close while it keeps the modal frame, completes its cleanup, unsubscribes, and propagates the original failure, ahead of cleanup or modal-assertion failures, through the command's safe-execution boundary. SGT does not attach its own dispatcher exception handler; Core neither handles nor signals other add-ins' exceptions. A ShowDialog failure before ContentRendered cannot have started analysis, so rollback, resource release and finalization run synchronously on the Revit UI thread, and only the cosmetic save can remain. Broken modal-continuation invariants are collected as finalization failures and do not skip rollback or cleanup. When the modal frame is already gone, the session records that invariant, does not await incomplete dispatcher work, downgrades finalization to rollback and continues every safe cleanup step. The safe-execution boundary owns user-facing reporting. View model The view model owns queued plan, preview and render dispatcher operations. Disposal stops both refresh coordinators, drops the pending plan snapshot and aborts queued callbacks before it cancels analysis. Late preview results cannot publish to a retired view. Girt and opening projection publishes validation flags, but those notifications do not queue another UI edit; segment group display refresh is suppressed the same way. Invalid rows and refreshed group labels therefore cannot start a preview loop. Each analysis run owns its cancellation source until its finally completes. A newer run or disposal cancels the active run without disposing its source early. An idle source is canceled and disposed immediately when replaced. Canceled or superseded results cannot publish a plan or change preview mode after an await. A disposed view model creates no new idle source. Features Placement Path Content Features/Placement/Domain Command state, preflight and readiness rules, gaps, validation and placement projections Features/Placement/ViewModels/PlacementCommandStateProjector.cs Adapts girt and opening view models into those inputs and applies their validation state Features/Placement/Planning Placement projections from the domain plan Features/Placement/Operations/ModelWrite The writer port, write context, contract catalog and opening target Features/Placement/Revit/ModelWrite Model changes Persistence/ElementTagSchema.cs Element-tag schema constants App/Sessions/Workflow/AnalysisSessionWorkflow orchestrates analysis for the command. Revit wall analysis and plan construction are in Features/WallAnalysis/{Domain,Revit/Planning}. WallAnalysis can use the Placement planning and model-write contracts it needs to build a plan; Placement does not reference WallAnalysis. App depends on both. Recoverable plan rejections are SpecFailure results at the opening-segment, preview girt-snap, member-segment hydration and placement-projection boundaries; the UI shows the typed rejection and publishes no plan or preview change. Argument defects, cancellation and unexpected faults are exceptions and propagate through the safe-execution boundary. Revit transaction and model-write code can throw SpecFailureException when unwinding must roll back; unrelated faults propagate as exceptions. TemporaryTransactionRunner retains operation, accessor, and rollback failures before diagnostics. Snapshot and rollback logging failures follow in attempt order; a single operation failure preserves its original exception. Plan admission rejects an invalid update with SpecFailureException carrying PlanValidationFailed and the validation details. Opening persistence and segment mutation translate only that code into their failure results. A rejection keeps the committed plan and version; parent edits stay suppressed until a successful retry or cancellation. A rejected segment add, delete or property change shows the failure in the banner and the preview status without a refresh request. UI-to-plan synchronization reads the committed layer directly when there is no UI selection. It builds the girt projection where it uses it and lets opening persistence own the opening projection. Segment lookup and deletion use canonical opening rows through the row resolver. PlacementElementTagStore admits elements for contextual selection, update, removal and deconstruction. An owned element has the Structural Framing category, a valid SGT schema entity, the exact SGT marker and a non-blank system ID. An update collects admitted instances once per transaction and indexes them by role and identity; each target consumes its entry, and unmatched admitted instances are deleted after all walls are processed. An element with another marker is never owned, even when its stored system ID matches. PlacementWorkflow keeps the command's SafeExecutionResult and returns one placement or removal outcome. A successful command requests a successful close; a failed or canceled model write requests a rollback close. Declining the removal confirmation leaves the window open, because no write began. Revit/CommittedWrite/CommittedWrite maps Revit refusals and non-committed transaction status to Transaction/NotCommitted and keeps the original cause. Each command uses ordinary transactions inside the session group. GirtView raises typed row requests with the selected GirtRowViewModel, visual anchor, and input event. App routes these requests to the bulk-edit and segment flyouts. Girt column widths are not persisted. The dialog ports IDangerConfirmationDialog and IUpdateSummaryDialog are in Features/Placement/Workflow; App/Sessions/WindowSession/WindowSessionDialogs.cs implements them. Change Review Features/ChangeReview owns the detached review candidate, row decisions, target precedence, the decision ledger, relink pairing and the dialog. The dialog is an embedded raw XAML view with no x:Class or code-behind. Accept, Keep and Ignore are the only decision terms in the UI and the code. Opening labels use the source name and the along-wall range; the opening key is internal. ChangeReviewWorkflow synchronizes the accepted plan before it captures its revision, reads one live snapshot and analyzes a confirmed candidate before it publishes it. Confirm writes only the detached plan and ledger state. A later Place or Update command writes the model and sets Placed from the write result, so several model commands can follow one review while the session group stays open. The lifecycle owns the review child and any relink picker. It retires the child in finally, closes the child before it hides the parent for a pick and resumes the same modal driver after the picker returns. Cancel, native close, command failure and forced retirement roll back the session group; only a successful close assimilates it, as one Undo entry named Super Girt Tool. ChangeReviewPlanBuilder decides: it resolves each item's decision once and derives both the candidate plan and the ledger that Confirm saves; rows show the resolved decision. AllowedDecisions is the matrix of allowed decisions and ProposeDecision the default rule. The dialog offers the matrix's decisions (SetInvalidated removes Ignore for a released user-created opening unless Ignore is already selected) and preselects an allowed proposal. The builder applies a proposal to an undecided item that needs no attention only when the matrix allows it. An explicit Ignore returns a Placed opening to its Placed framing configuration, held, also when the draft has a local edit. An opening that was never placed stays unframed; a later Keep frames a never-placed manual opening again. Without a live observation a row offers only Keep and Ignore. The live snapshot carries the grid crossings along the Placed wall and the observed wall; girt grid anchors resolve against the grids of the wall the review adopts. Rows show the opening source name (or Manual opening for an unnamed manual row), source, status and decision; effects appear in the details pane of the selected row. Placement validation messages include the along-wall range where it matters. The canonical key is never shown. Preview Features/Preview/Domain owns the preview scene, palette, wall, girt, opening, grid and segment-assignment state. Features/Preview/Rendering/Scene3D builds plain SGT mesh values. Features/Preview/Views/Rendering/Scene3D/StructuralPreviewSceneAdapter maps them to the snapshot DTOs of IStructuralPreview3D. WPF renderers and canvas layout are under Features/Preview/Views. The Presentation viewport owns Helix, camera navigation, fit and reset, hit testing, hover and selection materials. SGT code has no Helix reference. PreviewPresenterBehavior (App) draws the 2D elevation and section and owns handles, snapping, context menus and row selection; it forwards 3D scene and emphasis updates through the stable API. SgtWindow composes PreviewView.xaml into the host and retires the presenter before transaction finalization. Placement view models store no Preview domain objects. Preview edits change the domain plan and request a FromPlan projection. PreviewServiceCollectionExtensions.cs registers the feature; the window-session builder binds it into the modal runtime. Edit workflows are under Features/Preview/Editing/MemberResolution/Segmentation; reusable plan-edit calculations are under Domain/PlanEditing. StructuralPreviewSceneAdapter is the only conversion from scene metadata to Presentation DTOs. Mesh IDs keep the source row, role and segment identity, so click selection, hover tooltips, sibling dimming, segment emphasis and wall-context materials are deterministic. SGT turns off the viewport's own tooltip popup; the PreviewView overlay is the only tooltip. Viewport pointer events still drive it, including wall-only click tooltips and clearing on wall hover. Wall meshes are pickable context hits but never select rows; a member hit wins when both are present. The adapter adds a transparent floor plane and sets a minimum overlay thickness. Scene bounds and the exterior normal set the home camera orientation; the presenter owns orbit, pan, zoom, fit and camera persistence while the view is hosted. Refresh: Features/Preview/Refresh/PreviewProjectionService projects a given Plan without changing the plan or its store. App reconciles segmentation for PreviewRefreshMode.UIEdit and PlanMutation. A changed plan refreshes the UI and queues RenderOnly before any preview publication. RenderOnly reads the committed plan without reconciliation. PreviewRenderingService owns scene construction and its cache, not plan state. PlanSynchronizationWallSetupProjection projects the Layer selector items from the accepted plan. PreviewRefreshCoordinator keeps monotonic request, completion and success sequences. The work returns a PreviewUpdateOutcome: only Applied advances success; Blocked completes without success; Deferred completes without success and queues one RenderOnly successor, which readiness waits for. A disabled preview, a rejected UI synchronization, a missing plan and a canceled or failed build cannot satisfy readiness. A rejected UI dispatch fails that sequence and keeps any newer request for dispatch. Publication: The presenter acknowledges a scene only after the viewport applied the scene, the emphasis or reset, and the selection highlight. A missing subscriber, an unavailable presenter or a contained rendering failure returns Blocked; a failure clears the scene cache so a later refresh can retry. When the presenter attaches after the view entered 3D mode, it invalidates the last publication key and requests one render-only refresh. A reused view model therefore delivers its cached scene again to the new presenter. App records a scene cache key only after publication succeeds. A matching cache hit can satisfy readiness without another publication; a cached but unpublished scene forces a new build. Clearing the cache and a failed publication invalidate the key. Analysis switches to elevation only after preview readiness succeeds. Features/Preview owns preview state, projection, rendering, editing workflows and refresh scheduling and coalescing (PreviewRefreshCoordinator). App runs the refresh: SgtWindowViewModel.UpdatePreviewAsync synchronizes every pane through PlanSynchronizationCoordinator inside the window's analysis lifetime. App also owns PreviewPresenterBehavior, because it routes into the girt and opening grids through WindowSessionSurfaceCoordinator. The Func<PreviewRefreshMode, int, Task<PreviewUpdateOutcome>> that App passes to PreviewRefreshCoordinator injects work into the scheduler. Viewport and input: The stable SGT preview input behavior owns the raw 2D canvas and the zoom and reset buttons; the payload keeps elevation, section, snapping, handle editing and context-menu decisions. Unwiring releases the stable behaviors before the presenter and scene adapter retire. The 3D viewport installs at ContextIdle after Loaded, so the shell paints first. Entering 3D restores the home camera; scene updates keep a user-adjusted camera. The raw preview has the role palette legend, a DirectX failure panel and a Sandbox fallback panel. Unavailable status shows only in 3D mode. Each raw fragment resolves static theme resources through one dispatcher-owned SgtThemeResourceExtension. Grids and flyouts Opening parent-row edits are a DataGrid transaction. SgtDataGridRowEditGateBehavior defers row completion at Send priority while the payload validates and commits or cancels the Opening edit. Add Opening uses the parent-edit helper after the view loads; the same helper saves and restores named Opening column widths around UI-state persistence. The gate aborts pending dispatcher completions before release; the window owns deferred parent-edit and width-restore callbacks through the session, and stale rows are ignored after a replacement or retirement. Completion requires a canonical GUID opening key and valid geometry, also when every framing role is off. Invalid input keeps the row in edit mode and does not raise ParentRowCommitted. SgtWindowInteractionBehavior (Presentation) caches the two DataGrids and flyout roots after the view loads. Its logical and visual traversal skips duplicate nodes and walks ContentElement parents, including PopupRoot to Popup for dropdown scrollbars. Bulk and segment flyout positioning keeps its Render and ContextIdle operations in the releasable behavior, clamps open cards after a window resize and resets the segment card to its 680-pixel default before population. Drag, resize and zero-distance behavior are kept. ComboBox, text, button, toggle and DataGrid input never dismisses by click-away; outside dismissal requires an active bulk edit. The modal scrim is the element named FlyoutModalScrim. The root PreviewMouseDown tunnel dismisses an active bulk edit when the source is outside the bulk card and the excluded controls. The scrim's MouseLeftButtonDown then closes the segment flyout if it is open, otherwise the bulk flyout, and marks the event handled only when it closed one. A right click can take the tunnel path but does not run the scrim handler. The scrim covers the whole client area, including the 16-DIP band outside the main content grid; the floating cards keep their inset. On native non-client mouse-down messages (title bar, resize frame, system areas) the shell dismisses only an open segment flyout. Bulk edit and its flyout stay, so dragging the window keeps the bulk selection. The behavior attaches a session-owned HwndSourceHook, leaves the message unhandled and detaches with the window, so move, resize, system menu and close stay native. The behavior handles the Girt Flip-cell gesture at the root before DataGrid selection runs. Left-click checkbox toggling and row selection are kept, including Shift bypass, Ctrl toggle and deselecting a selected row. Segment expander double-clicks do not activate bulk rows. The opening segment TreeView uses SgtTreeViewSelectedItemBehavior. It forwards only the TreeView's own SelectedItemChanged value, so input in an embedded ComboBox or editor cannot change the selection. It is retired with the shell. The Sandbox sample implements the same interaction surface, so sample rows and flyout drag and resize use the shared behavior. Openings, Orientation, WallAnalysis and BulkEdit Opening keys are canonical GUID-N strings and stay the same when the source changes. OpeningLiveReference and WallTargetReference carry owning-document UniqueIds and, where needed, the UniqueId of the host link instance. OpeningRuntimeIdIndex assigns ordinal IDs 1..n per projection; it never derives them from key bits or element IDs. Opening rows store along-wall start and end distances in feet. OpeningGeometryResolver derives the normalized frame from those distances and the current wall length, so a manual opening does not stretch with the wall. A local geometry edit converts a Live opening to Manual and keeps its live reference and source name. Held and Unframed rows are read-only and show (awaiting review) or (not framed). Only Unframed removes an opening from girt boundaries and opening members; an opening with all roles off still splits girts. OpeningRoleRules.ApplySeedDefaultsForEnabledRoles is the shared seeding rule: a geometry change removes roles that no longer apply, seeds roles that now apply and keeps applicable overrides and user-disabled roles. GeometryFingerprint.Compare owns the wall and opening change tolerances (0.01 ft and 1 inch), including type, layer material and function, frame, reflection and framing-mode changes. Live geometry takes material names from the owning document; WallGeometryContext stores no wall identity. Openings owns Revit opening queries, editable-row mutation, synchronization and projection, and the opening pane view models. Opening identities, ranges, contracts and feet geometry are in Domain/Openings, beside EditableOpeningRow. Opening bounds accept only complete, finite source candidates. Complete cut-face bounds replace every fallback. Otherwise solid bounds seed the result, the width replaces the solid's horizontal bounds before the profile union, and the vertical order of precedence is profile, parameters, solid. Missing geometry, solids, cut generators or profile loops fall through to the next source; traversal, symbol-geometry, triangulation, transform and non-finite-vertex faults keep their original exception and stack. If any supported insert exhausts every source, the query returns one typed OpeningQuery/Incomplete failure and no partial list. Wall-context failures stay typed, and opening-row recovery matches the code UI/PlanMissing, not message text. Orientation: Orientation/Revit/Analysis owns the family-orientation analyzer and solver inputs; Orientation/Analysis has the portable rotation math and solver results; shared orientation values are in Domain/Orientation. WallAnalysis owns the plan-builder contract and Revit geometry extraction, calibration, profile warming, seeding and plan construction under WallAnalysis/{Domain,Revit/{Geometry,Planning}}. WallContextResolver accepts only a closed WallTarget and produces a ResolvedWallContext, the only host or link input to WallGeometryBuilder. Calibration checks cancellation before argument validation and cache access. Argument defects throw; typed SpecFailureException failures become calibration results; only successes are cached. Family calibration runs per family: it logs a failed family and continues, and each type of that family then carries the typed failure, with family and type names, as a per-role orientation failure. The orientation analyzer throws SpecFailureException for expected family incompatibilities, and WallAnalysisFramingTypeAnalyzer converts them per role. Host and linked frame construction share one typed frame-failure boundary in WallGeometryBuilder. Cancellation, rollback failures and invariant defects propagate. When every profile fails, ProfileLoopsAllFailed keeps up to five type IDs and their causes in numeric order and reports how many it omitted. Per-type logs and partial-success warnings stay available. New and edit analysis both pass PlanAdmissionValidator before they return success. Edit analysis keeps the stored configuration and analyzes the current geometry of the selected wall. PlanSeedingStep is the only initial seeding owner. App reports the projected girt and opening counts without adding rows or writing UI values into the plan. A non-foundation plan keeps the no-openings notice. BulkEdit owns the bulk-edit flyout, centered on BulkEditFlyoutViewModel. A failed apply tries to restore every captured girt and opening-role snapshot in request order, then propagates the apply failure followed by every restoration failure. Placement owns GirtTypeItem, GirtTypeCatalog and GirtPaneViewModel.GirtTypeDisplay for the girt grid. Opening, bulk and preview selectors use immutable FramingTypeOption values. The shared combo-box item style, also used by the girt grid, binds IsSelectable and shows ProfileWarningText; selection setters refuse unavailable types. Placement preflight checks opening member profiles before placement. SmartDefaultsResolver, SmartDefaultsInput, TypeDrivenDefaultsInput and FamilyResolutionInput are pure contracts. Girt and opening rows apply resolved values through their own methods; Domain never references feature view models. Features/BulkEdit owns the bulk-edit flyout, centered on BulkEditFlyoutViewModel. Bulk apply changes girt and opening rows with both reactive-sync suppressions active. After a successful commit, the girt owner refreshes the Flip capability and option lists of the selected rows while still suppressed, and clears an earlier type-change blocker only when its own row now has a valid orientation. Opening-only edits and failed applies keep that blocker. One UI-edit preview refresh then writes the committed rows to the plan. A failed apply restores its row snapshots and reports one bulk error without projecting the transient edits. Testing Projects DBTools.SGT.csproj has a desktop and a portable target. The shared portable rules select inward code by layer, turn off content identity and merging, and exclude desktop resources. Project References Content Tests/DBTools.SGT.Portable.Pure.Tests.csproj portable SGT Domain and features, plan store, persistence, review workflow, preview status Tests/DBTools.SGT.Pure.Tests.csproj desktop SGT WPF and session behavior Tests/DBTools.SGT.Local.Tests.csproj owning projects; stages the desktop product Revit fixtures Review cancellation and relink stay in IChangeReviewOperation; desktop lifecycle composition binds App/Views/IChangeReviewDialogHost to the dialog constructor. The presenter maps Presentation status to portable readiness values. Raw XAML and the Windows test project require WPF. Test helpers are under Tests/Support. Fixture boundaries Fixtures mirror production owners under Tests/: Each Pure fixture folder and namespace mirrors the directory of the code it tests. Test-only helpers are under Tests/Support. Fixture names name the current subject, for example OrientationConverterTests, PlanProjectionMapperTests, OpeningProjectorTests and MemberSegmentationReconcilerTests. Preview scene-key tests mirror the domain cache-key owner. DBTools.SGT.csproj has a desktop and a portable target. build/MSBuild/Portable.targets removes App, Revit, Views, DesignTime and XAML inputs from the portable target. DBTools.SGT.Portable.Pure.Tests references portable SGT and covers domain and features, the plan store, persistence, the review workflow and preview status. DBTools.SGT.Pure.Tests references desktop SGT for WPF and session cases, including OpeningSynchronizationControllerTests, PreviewRefreshCoordinatorTests, BulkEditFlyoutViewModelTests and OpeningMemberExtentSnapTargetResolverTests, which need no Revit host. Windows Pure WindowSessionLifecycleTests uses the real modal host and watchdog; it covers re-entry after a pick without another ContentRendered and pending picks after HideForPick (the runner re-enters after each pick, before target analysis finishes). Raw embedded XAML is a desktop resource, because the window host composes it. The presenter maps Presentation status to portable readiness values; the desktop review callback binds IChangeReviewDialogHost to the dialog constructor with its cancellation and relink port. DBTools.SGT.Local.Tests holds the [RevitLocal] fixtures and modeless Revit integration tests; real modal execution is tested in Windows Pure. Revit-hosted window tests use modeless Window.Show() with a bounded DispatcherDrain. StartupAnalysisWorkflowTests covers startup target resolution. Tests/Integration/Revit/App/Views/SgtWindowHostedTests.cs builds the raw SgtWindow through ToolWindowFactory and checks the shell dimensions, root composition and the named Girt, Openings and Preview hosts before it releases the session. SgtWindowSessionTests drives the real run scope through RunWindowFlowAsync and checks transaction rollback, plan target, preview, DataContext, overlay cleanup, failure order and startup tasks without opening a modal dialog. The SGT test model, linked document and wall IDs, opening and geometry baselines, plan-build outcomes and preview projections are fixed repository data. Missing or unexpected state fails with the requested baseline, the observed result, the model path and the Revit year. Per-case rollback and cleanup of the fixture document, UIDocument and logging are part of each assertion. The launch smoke test treats startup-analysis completion, the UI-state save, preview and viewport cleanup, group rollback, window close, handler and view-model release and run-scope disposal as ordered cleanup that can fail. The active Revit document belongs to the daemon. The WPF construction smoke test releases the view model it attaches; production window and session disposal has one owner. PreviewPlacementParityTests.Persisted_system_edit_plan_preserves_configuration_and_reanalyzes_desired_geometry round-trips nested girt, left-jamb, opening-key and offset selections through the registered repository, moves the linked wall after it saves the baseline, then calls the registered edit-plan builder. It requires the live wall elevation to differ from storage and checks that the edit plan uses the current geometry and keeps the stored configuration. The transaction group rolls back the storage write and the link move afterward. Run the tests: ./test.sh test --tool SGT --scope pure ./test.sh test --tool SGT --scope local -y <year> Revit-hosted submissions normally omit --machine; the daemon selects an eligible worker. --machine forces a worker for diagnosis. See Test Pipeline. Placement and review fixtures Revit-hosted fixtures use the local scope: Contract Test Place creates members, tags and storage WallSystemWriterTests.PlaceAsync_RealProjection_PersistsTagsCountsAndProgressInOneTransaction Delete System removes owned members and storage and keeps a copied foreign tag PreviewPlacementParityTests.DeleteSystem_DeletesStorageAndPlacedElements Deconstruct removes SGT associations and keeps the framing PreviewPlacementParityTests.DeconstructSystem_DeletesStorageAndTags_PreservesPlacedElements Update keeps held opening members and does not adopt a copied identity WallSystemWriter.Updates_HeldOpeningLeavesFramingUntouchedAndNeverAdoptsCopiedIdentity Update keeps matches and deletes unmatched tagged instances WallSystemWriter.Updates_UpdateAsync_PreservesMatchesAndDeletesUnmatchedTaggedInstance A persisted configuration is reloaded and the current wall geometry is analyzed again PreviewPlacementParityTests.Persisted_system_edit_plan_preserves_configuration_and_reanalyzes_desired_geometry Purge keeps the current system and member tags inside the session group WallSystemWriterTests.PurgeUnsupportedAsync_preserves_persisted_v2_system_and_member_tags_inside_the_session_group Removing an opening re-anchors girt ends, and placement matches the preview PreviewPlacementParityTests.Removing_an_opening_reanchors_girt_ends_and_placement_matches_preview The review ledger and an inner Update commit or roll back with session OK or Cancel SgtWindowSessionTests.Real_change_review_confirm_and_inner_update_follow_session_close The Confirm test replaces only the child dialog; the workflow, repository, analysis, placement executor, elements, tags and session group are real. It writes the ledger from Confirm and runs a physical Update before it requests Cancel or OK. See Limitations for the manual Undo check. Input fixtures Pure and Revit-hosted flyout fixtures supply a complete ISgtWindowDragInput (coordinates, capture owner, capture and release), because raising routed mouse events does not take native mouse capture and Revit-hosted jobs run on a hidden desktop that receives no input. SgtWindowDragInput delegates to WPF in production. The Revit-hosted preview gesture test uses the same interface through PreviewPresenterBehavior.SetDragInputSource; the presenter keeps that source across disable and enable. The tests assert capture through the supplied input and keep the production handler, cursor, selection, rendering and zoom assertions. Revit-hosted input tests use layout hit testing and directly raised routed events: the Flip-cell test raises the preview tunnel on the realized grid, the scrim test raises the preview and left-button routes from the same hit, and the Ctrl test sets and restores the thread's keyboard state without injecting input. Limitations Domain storage accepts only format version 3 and does not migrate other formats. Girt endpoint anchors accept only wall, grid, and opening-edge anchors; MemberEdge is reserved for opening-member segments. Zee and Angle types are unavailable for opening roles. The Revit API does not expose the Undo stack. Check the single Super Girt Tool Undo entry in Revit after a successful close.

developer-guide/tools/structural/sgt.htm.title: Super Girt Tool (SGT) | DB Tools
developer-guide/tools/structural/sgt.htm.summary: Super Girt Tool (SGT) Overview Super Girt Tool (SGT) analyzes one wall, edits girts and opening members in a modal window with 2D and 3D previews, and places tagged structural framing. It supports new systems and contextual editing of stored systems. The SGT specification defines the data and execution contract. This page is the developer overview. The user guide describes window controls and user procedures. Architecture Source: src/Tools/Structural/SGT/. The assembly and tool ID are DBTools.SGT. manifest.yml registers SgtToolModule and SgtCommand under DBTools.SGT.App.Composition. Owner Responsibility App Composition, startup, modal sessions, UI-to-plan synchronization, window hosting, and cosmetic UI persistence Domain Plan, plan store, baseline snapshots, geometry, member rules, and plan editing Features/BulkEdit Bulk row editing Features/ChangeReview Live comparison, decisions, relink pairing, and review dialog Features/Openings Opening queries, mutation, synchronization, and row UI Features/Orientation Family orientation analysis and portable solver math Features/Placement Readiness, projection, model writes, update, and removal Features/Preview Projection, rendering, editing, hit testing, snapping, and refresh scheduling Features/WallAnalysis Wall geometry, calibration, profile warming, and plan construction Persistence Storage mapper, schema, repository contract, and Revit implementation Revit Cross-feature Revit adapters Domain is independent of App, Features, Persistence, and WPF. Features do not depend on App; App composes their ports. Presentation owns stable WPF controls and the 3D viewport. The payload embeds raw XAML; ToolWindowFactory supplies its modal shell. Sandbox uses the same raw fragments and composition callback. See the specification's owner tree, composition, and application boundary for source locations and lifetime owners. Data and contracts PlanStore owns detached accepted plans. UI edits pass through PlanSynchronizationCoordinator; preview and placement consume the same resolved member contracts. PreviewRefreshMode.UIEdit synchronizes UI values before reconciliation, PlanMutation reconciles the plan, and RenderOnly renders accepted state. Stored systems contain Placed geometry and element identities, baseline settings, and a decision ledger. ISystemRepository provides per-system Save, Load, Exists, Delete, ledger-save, and purge operations. SettingsData.PlacementMode stores the framing mode. The specification defines resolved geometry, storage, and plan admission and synchronization. Workflows Launch a new system with a concrete wall target, or edit a stored system with its SystemId. Analyze the wall, calibrate eligible framing families, warm profiles, and build an admitted plan. Edit girt and opening rows or preview handles. Invalid fields block synchronization and placement. Use Change Review to compare the accepted configuration with live geometry. Confirm publishes the analyzed candidate and saves its decision ledger; Place or Update writes framing. Finish the session. A successful close assimilates its Super Girt Tool transaction group; Cancel, errors, failed close, and forced retirement roll it back. Target re-pick hides and reopens the same modal session within one synchronous Revit command frame. Cosmetic UI-state writes run separately from model finalization. See window session and feature workflows. Testing Tests mirror production owners under Tests/; shared fixture support lives in Tests/Support. Project Execution boundary DBTools.SGT.Portable.Pure.Tests Portable domain, plan store, persistence, review, and preview logic DBTools.SGT.Pure.Tests Windows Pure WPF and modal-session behavior DBTools.SGT.Local.Tests Revit-hosted tests (the local scope), model writes, and Revit integration The specification owns the fixture inventory and commands, including physical placement and review fixtures and hidden-desktop input adapters. Limitations SGT requires a document that is not modifiable at launch and an inline Revit call gate for its modal session. Stored formats other than version 3 are purged within the session group. See the specification limitations for member-role restrictions and the manual Undo check.

developer-guide/troubleshooting.html.title: Troubleshooting | DB Tools
developer-guide/troubleshooting.html.summary: Troubleshooting This page lists common build, runtime and tool errors, and how to read the DB Tools logs. For a reported failure, read the logs in %APPDATA%\DBTools\Logs\ first. Build Choosing a build command Build one project or test project with plain MSBuild: dotnet build path/to/project.csproj -c Release This computes content versions, restores only the selected year and stages the project's runtime inputs. It does not validate or publish a distribution. ./build.sh BuildAll builds, validates and publishes the complete distribution for every supported year, including the Dev Mode preflight and manifest checks. BuildAll compiles no tests; use ./build.sh BuildTests or a selected-test target. See Build Pipeline. Python 3.10 or later is required Python 3.10 or later is required. Install it with: sudo apt-get install python3 On Linux and WSL, build/DotNet/sdk.sh uses Python to verify and install the pinned SDK when the private SDK root is incomplete; test.sh also uses it for test discovery. Install Python and rerun the command: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y python3 bash build/DotNet/sdk.sh On Windows, build.ps1 installs and verifies the SDK without Python. DbToolsDaemon.Protocol package missing or mismatched BuildAll requires the DbToolsDaemon.Protocol package version pinned in build/Distribution/protocol-package-lock.json, with the SHA-256 recorded there. The Validation Runner loads the package after the build tasks verify it. If the package is missing or its bytes differ from the lock, obtain the pinned package and update the lock. sourceKind is github-release for a published release, or local-candidate for an approved local candidate with its candidate-<version> tag, daemon commit, and copies of the bundle README and SHA256SUMS. Do not point the build at a daemon checkout or bypass the check. BuildAll does not need the daemon CLI or an installed Revit. The DIST suite and Revit-hosted tests use the daemon CLI. Dev Mode preflight fails ValidateDistributionCandidate runs the Dev Mode policy on each year and prints: Revit <year> Dev Mode preflight: <n> failures, <m> warnings; outcome=<x> Both years must pass. A CollectibleThreadStatic warning counts as a failure. A failed policy, boundary, graph, identity or candidate-byte check needs a source fix and a new build. HandyControl output missing A missing vendor import, resource or DBTools.HandyControl output means the vendor/HandyControl submodule is not initialized. build.sh and build.ps1 initialize it automatically, which requires a Git checkout and network access: git submodule update --init --recursive vendor/HandyControl ./build.sh BuildAll The output is .artifacts/vendor/<Configuration>/handycontrol/net10.0-windows/DBTools.HandyControl.dll. Unsupported Revit year The supported desktop years are Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) and Revit 2027; the distribution and reference metadata use the year keys 2026 and 2027. A build or candidate for any other year is rejected; there is no fallback framework. Revit backup files in test models Revit writes backup copies (*.0001.rvt, *.00001.rvt) when it saves a model. Under testing/RevitTestModels/ these files are ignored by Git. The build does not delete them; remove them by hand when you no longer need them. Runtime Tool assembly fails to load InvalidOperationException: Failed to load tool assembly 'DBTools.GM' from the declared Tools path '<path>' in ALC rooted at 'DBTools'. Related errors from ToolAssemblyResolver: Tool assembly '<name>' was not found at the declared Tools path '<path>'. Tool assembly path '<path>' declares simple name '<x>', expected '<name>'. Tool assembly '<name>' is already loaded from '<path>', but the declared Tools path is '<path>'. App loads each tool from Tools/<name>.dll beside DBTools.dll. Check that the year directory has the complete product tree (see Assembly Loading Contract) and that the manifest's assembly name matches the file. Rebuild with ./build.sh BuildAll. "Assembly already loaded" during Dev Mode reload Revit shows a popup about an assembly that is already loaded during or after BuildAll, while the dbtools-daemon Dev Mode driver watches the distribution. Causes: The driver watches the multi-year root .artifacts/dist/Release instead of one year directory. A reload starts while promotion replaces the files. DB Tools code loaded or resolved a DBTools.* assembly or type outside the driver's collectible AssemblyLoadContext (for example through an AppDomain-wide scan or Assembly.Load), so the context cannot unload. Point the driver directly at one year directory, .artifacts/dist/Release/2026 or .artifacts/dist/Release/2027, never at a copy, and publish with ./build.sh BuildAll. Promotion keeps each unchanged file as the same file (a hard link), so Windows Defender does not scan it again. A copied directory is a set of new files that Defender scans again, which can add tens of seconds to each Dev Mode inspection. Theme validation Startup validates the theme with ThemeValidator.ValidateOrThrow; a failure stops startup. In a Revit-hosted test run, read the daemon job's startup failure output instead of waiting for a dialog. Theme dictionary merge failed InvalidOperationException: Theme dictionary merge failed at '/DBTools.Presentation;V<PresentationVersion>;component/Resources/Brushes.xaml'. A resource dictionary did not load: a missing assembly reference, a broken StaticResource chain or invalid XAML. Rebuild with ./build.sh BuildAll and check that the year directory contains DBTools.Presentation.dll and DBTools.HandyControl.dll from the same build. Theme resource freeze failed InvalidOperationException: Theme resource freeze failed for key '<key>' in '<source>'. A Freezable resource (brush, geometry) cannot be frozen, usually because it has a binding or a dynamic reference. Make its values static. Theme merged dictionary contract mismatch InvalidOperationException: Theme merged dictionary contract mismatch: expected 9 dictionaries but found 8 in '<root>'.
