InvalidOperationException: Theme merged dictionary contract mismatch at index <i>: expected '<uri>' but found '<uri>'. Resources/Theme.xaml must merge these dictionaries in this order: HandyControl Themes/SkinDark.xaml, HandyControl Themes/Theme.xaml, then Tokens.xaml, Brushes.xaml, Converters.xaml, Controls.xaml, DataGrid.xaml, Menus.xaml and Components.xaml. See Theme System. Revit API context errors ContextUnavailableException: No UIApplication in current gate scope. InvalidOperationException: ActiveUIDocument is null. Code used the Revit API outside a valid API context, for example from a modeless window without the call gate, after the document closed, or during shutdown. Run Revit API work through IRevitCallGate.RunAsync, check that a document is open, and handle cancellation when a document closes. WPF Dispatcher errors InvalidOperationException: No WPF Dispatcher is available (Application.Current is null and no Revit window dispatcher could be resolved). InvalidOperationException: WPF Dispatcher is shutting down. UI work ran during early startup or late shutdown, when no dispatcher is available. Check for a dispatcher and for Dispatcher.HasShutdownStarted before UI work, and use BeginInvoke where the caller need not wait. Unhandled UI exception from a window command A WPF command that calls ISafeExecutor.RunAsync and lets the exception propagate into an AsyncRelayCommand raises a Dispatcher unhandled exception, which the Dev Mode driver host can also show. In window commands, use ISafeExecutor.RunWithoutThrowingAsync: it logs and notifies but does not rethrow. Use RunAsync where the caller must receive the exception. XamlParseException on a read-only binding System.Windows.Markup.XamlParseException: A TwoWay or OneWayToSource binding cannot work on the read-only property '<name>' ... Run.Text binds TwoWay by default. Binding it to a get-only property fails when the window loads. Set Mode=OneWay (or OneTime for an immutable value), or bind a TextBlock.Text instead. Contextual ribbon layout changes A contextual ribbon injector that modifies Revit's contextual tabs eagerly (for example the Multi-Select tab) or inserts at index 0 shifts the native buttons. Inject only when the selection contains matching elements, append panels and buttons with Add, and remove them when the selection no longer matches. Core's ContextualRibbonInjector follows these rules. Other startup and manifest errors Message Cause AppRuntime not initialized. Code ran before App startup completed or after shutdown Manifest '<id>' is missing required 'panel' field. (and other missing required messages) Invalid manifest.yml Tool module type '<type>' not found in assembly '<assembly>'. The manifest module type or assembly name is wrong Tools Transfer Drafting Views (TDV) TransferException carries a TransferErrorCode: Code Meaning Action DestinationTypeMissing The destination has no matching drafting view type Create the view type in the destination SourceTypeNameUnavailable The source view type name cannot be read Check that the source is a valid drafting view CreateViewFailed The destination view could not be created Check write access and view limits CopyElementsFailed The view elements could not be copied Check the elements and the target view OverridesFailed The view overrides could not be copied Some overrides cannot be transferred View Template Comparer (VTC): raw XAML resource not found System.IO.FileNotFoundException: Embedded tool XAML resource 'DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.AlertBodyTemplates.xaml' was not found. The VTC alert body templates are an EmbeddedResource with the logical name DBTools.ToolViews.VTC.AlertBodyTemplates.xaml, read with ToolWindowXaml.ReadEmbeddedResource. Check the item and its LogicalName in DBTools.VTC.csproj. The shared VTC dictionaries are in src/DBTools.Presentation/Tools/VTC. Logs Log files Logs are written to %APPDATA%\DBTools\Logs\. File names use Eastern time: dbtools-<RevitYear>-<InstanceId>-<Timestamp>-<Nonce>.log dbtools-<RevitYear>-<InstanceId>-<Timestamp>-<Nonce>-manual-<ManualTimestamp>.log The second form is written after Start New Log File in the logger window. Example: dbtools-2026-ABC123-20260124-143022345-a1b2c3d4.log. Startup cleans up old files: at most 50 files across all instances, at most 14 days old, and at most 100 MB in total while more than one file remains (the newest file is kept even if it alone is larger). Failures that occur before logging starts are written to %APPDATA%\DBTools\Logs\DBTools.Fallback.log. Debug mode Debug mode lowers the minimum log level from Information to Debug, shows the logger window and flushes the log buffer every 120 ms instead of 600 ms. It is off at every startup and is not saved. It turns on when: you enable it in the Settings window or open the logger window; an Error-level entry is logged and the logger window can be shown. An error logged before the Revit main window exists opens the window once deferred startup can show it. Closing the logger window turns debug mode off. Logger window The title is DB Tools Log - Revit <Year> [<InstanceId>]. The window is a modeless utility window. The logger host applies pin mode changes centrally: a change that keeps the owner mode only updates Topmost, and a change of owner mode closes and recreates the window. Code must not change the owner of the live window directly. The window provides: level filters for INFO, WARN, ERROR and DEBUG, and a text search; Copy All and Export, which save every retained entry in arrival order regardless of the filters. Export writes DBToolsLog_<yyyyMMdd_hhmmss><AM|PM>.txt; auto-scroll, which follows new entries. Scrolling up pauses it until you scroll back to the bottom or until a new entry arrives after 15 s idle; turning it off keeps it off; Start New Log File (in the danger menu), which starts a new file, clears the window and logs a confirmation with the same instance ID. If closing the previous file fails, the new file stays active and a warning is logged. Correlation IDs and execution phases ISafeExecutor gives every operation a GUID correlation ID and logs its phases: [Start] GM Apply starting (CorrelationId=...) [Complete] GM Apply completed in 1234ms (CorrelationId=...) Phase Level Meaning [Start] Information The operation started [Complete] Information The operation finished [Cancel] Warning The operation was canceled [Error] Error The operation failed Search for the correlation ID to find every entry of one operation and its duration. Reporting a problem Include: the log file from %APPDATA%\DBTools\Logs\, or a logger window export; the Revit version (year and build number); the DB Tools version; the correlation ID of the failed operation; the steps to reproduce; a screenshot of any error dialog.

index.html.title: DB Tools documentation | DB Tools
index.html.summary: DB Tools documentation DB Tools is a set of tools for Autodesk Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) and Revit 2027, mainly for structural engineering workflows. It runs on 64-bit Windows 10 or 11 and installs for the current user. Sections Section Audience Contents User guide Revit users Installation, getting started and one page per tool. Developer guide Contributors Architecture, creating a new tool and troubleshooting. API reference Contributors Reference generated from the XML documentation comments. Tools Tool Purpose Global Mapper Bulk replacement of families, types, styles and materials; duplicate detection; shared parameters. Super Girt Tool Girt, header, sill and jamb placement on walls. Combined Foundation Tags Data and positions for combined pier and footing tags. Transfer Drafting Views Copy of drafting views between a project and a library. View Template Comparer Comparison and merge of view templates. The user guide lists all tools. Requirements Item Requirement Revit Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) or Revit 2027, desktop Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit Account Standard user. The installer needs no administrator rights. Architecture DBTools.dll is the Revit entry point. It loads DBTools.Core (shared infrastructure and the tool registry), DBTools.Presentation (WPF resources and controls) and one assembly per tool from the Tools folder. The architecture overview describes the layers. Source: https://github.com/kirsch33/dbtools. Report problems on the issue tracker.

user-guide/getting-started.html.title: Getting started | DB Tools
user-guide/getting-started.html.summary: Getting started This page describes the DB Tools ribbon, the settings window and the conventions shared by all tools. For installation, see Installation. The ribbon DB Tools adds the DB Tools tab to the Revit ribbon. The tab has these panels: Panel Contents DB Tools Settings Settings DB Tools Common Global Mapper, Transfer Drafting Views (Export To Library and Import From Library), Align Elevation Tags DB Tools Structural Super Girt Tool, Combined Foundation Tags (Update Combined Foundation Tags and Move Combined Tags) and Organize Foundation Types in one split button, Analytical Snap To Level, Allow Join and Disallow Join in one split button, Update Joist Girder Weights DB Tools Testing View Template Comparer, Record Set, Extreme Roof Framing The pages of this guide refer to a panel by its last word, for example DB Tools > Common. The Testing panel holds tools that are still under development. A panel is hidden when its group is turned off in the settings. A tool whose prerequisites are not met is disabled, and a settings warning explains why (see Warnings). Settings Click Settings to open the settings window. It opens without a model. The General section has these options: Option Default Effect Enable Common Tools On Shows or hides the Common panel. Enable Structural Tools On Shows or hides the Structural panel. Enable Testing Tools On Shows or hides the Testing panel. Enable Services On Shows or hides background services in the ribbon. Enable Debug Mode Off Writes verbose logs and opens the logger window. Below General, each tool that has options contributes a settings pack: Elevation Tags, Combined Foundation Tags, Joist Girder Weights, Library Files (Transfer Drafting Views) and others. Each pack has a Reset button. Button Effect Validate Checks the settings and refreshes the warnings. Save Settings Saves all changes and closes the window. Reset All > Reset All Settings Resets every setting. Settings are stored per user and per Revit year in %APPDATA%\DBTools\settings.<year>.json. Several tools have an Auto-Update Enabled option. It makes the tool run when a view is activated. It does not update DB Tools itself. Warnings A tool can raise a settings warning when a prerequisite is missing, for example Combined Foundation Tags Disabled or Library Paths Invalid. The warning disables the commands that depend on the prerequisite. The settings pack of the tool shows a card with a fix action, or states what to correct. Logs and debug mode DB Tools writes a log file for each Revit session to %APPDATA%\DBTools\Logs\, named dbtools-<year>-...log. With Enable Debug Mode on, the logger window opens after a tool runs. The window can search and filter entries, copy them, and export them. Conventions A failure while a tool changes the model rolls back the run and leaves the model unchanged, except where a tool page says otherwise. Tools report their result in a banner at the screen corner or in a dialog. A banner closes by itself after a few seconds, except where a tool page says otherwise. A completed run is normally one undo entry. Press Ctrl+Z to undo it. Each tool page states exceptions. Tools that match elements by name take .NET regular expressions in their settings. Next Open the page of the tool you need. See the User guide for the list.

user-guide/index.html.title: User guide | DB Tools
user-guide/index.html.summary: User guide DB Tools is a set of tools for Autodesk Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) and Revit 2027. This guide describes how to install the add-in and how to use each tool. Installation: requirements, installing, uninstalling, files and troubleshooting. Getting started: the ribbon, the settings window, logs and shared conventions. Tools Common Tool Purpose Global Mapper Replaces families, types, styles and materials in bulk, finds duplicates, and adds shared parameters. Transfer Drafting Views Copies drafting views between the open project and a library project. Elevation Tags Aligns the labels of spot elevation tags in plan views. Structural Tool Purpose Super Girt Tool Places and manages wall girts, headers, sills and jambs. Combined Foundation Tags Updates the data of combined pier and footing tags and moves the tags to footing corners. Organize Foundation Types Renames foundation types by their dimensions, assigns type marks and merges duplicates. Analytical Snap To Level Moves analytical beam and column end points to a level. Allow Join and Disallow Join Allow or disallow joins at the ends of structural framing. Joist Girder Weights Estimates joist girder weight and writes it to the Wt parameter. Testing Tool Purpose View Template Comparer Compares two view templates and merges selected settings. Record Set Packages Revit host models together with their linked files. Extreme Roof Framing Tool Adjusts structural columns and beams to sloped roofs and floors. The Testing tools are under development. Help Each tool page lists the tool's limitations and the messages it shows. For a failure, read the newest log in %APPDATA%\DBTools\Logs\. See Getting started. To build or extend DB Tools, see the Developer guide.

user-guide/installation.html.title: Installation | DB Tools
user-guide/installation.html.summary: Installation DB Tools is a Revit add-in for Revit 2026 (2026.5 or later) and Revit 2027 on 64-bit Windows 10 or 11. The installer runs under a standard user account and needs no administrator rights. Requirements Item Requirement Revit 2026.5 or later, or 2027 (desktop) Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit Account Standard user Installing Download DBTools-Setup-<version>.exe from the GitHub releases page, or from the location your administrator provides. Close all running Revit sessions. Run the installer. On the Revit page, select the Revit years to install for. The installer checks %ProgramW6432%\Autodesk\Revit <year>\RevitAPI.dll. It enables only the years it detects, and it selects them by default. At least one year has to be selected. If DBTools.bundle is already installed, the installer asks An existing DBTools.bundle was found. Overwrite?. Answer Yes to replace it. Answer No to cancel the installation. Wait for the installer to finish. The installation log is shown on the progress page and on the finish page. The button Open install folder opens %APPDATA%\DBTools. Start Revit. The DB Tools tab appears on the ribbon. What the installer does The installer copies the release into a staging folder next to the active bundle, checks that the required files exist for each selected year, and rewrites PackageContents.xml so that the bundle registers only the selected years. It then renames the current bundle to a backup, moves the staging folder into place, and deletes the backup. If any of these steps fails, the installer restores the previous bundle and reports the error. Installing replaces the entire bundle. A new install removes the previous version folder and any other file in the old bundle. There is no in-app updater. To update, run the installer of the new release. Files and folders Path Contents %APPDATA%\Autodesk\ApplicationPlugins\DBTools.bundle\ The add-in, loaded by Revit as an Autodesk application plugin bundle. Contents\DBTools\<version>\<year>\ holds DBTools.addin, DBTools.dll, DBTools.Core.dll, DBTools.Presentation.dll, DBTools.HandyControl.dll and the Tools\ folder with one DBTools.<Tool>.dll per tool. %APPDATA%\DBTools\ The installer's data folder: the uninstaller, the icon and Families\ (Revit families that the tools use). %APPDATA%\DBTools\settings.<year>.json User settings, one file per Revit year. %APPDATA%\DBTools\Logs\ Log files, named dbtools-<year>-...log. %APPDATA%\DBTools\Cache\ Tool caches, for example VTC\ (saved templates) and TDV\ (temporary library copies). Each tool stores its own data under %APPDATA%\DBTools\ as its page describes. Uninstalling Open Settings > Apps > Installed apps, select DB Tools, and select Uninstall. The uninstaller deletes DBTools.bundle together with its .staging and .backup folders, and the Families folder. The uninstaller keeps your settings, logs and caches in %APPDATA%\DBTools\. To remove all DB Tools data, delete that folder. Silent installation The installer is an Inno Setup program and accepts the standard Inno Setup switches, for example: DBTools-Setup-<version>.exe /VERYSILENT /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES /NORESTART A silent installation installs for every detected Revit year. With /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES, the overwrite question takes its default answer, Yes. The installer has no switch for choosing Revit years or the install folder. Troubleshooting The DB Tools tab does not appear Close Revit and make sure %APPDATA%\Autodesk\ApplicationPlugins\DBTools.bundle\PackageContents.xml exists and lists your Revit year. Start Revit. Open the newest file in %APPDATA%\DBTools\Logs\ and search for ERROR or FATAL. If startup fails before logging starts, %APPDATA%\DBTools\Logs\DBTools.Fallback.log holds the failure. Reinstall DB Tools. DB Tools theme failed to load Revit shows this message when startup cannot load the DB Tools theme. The message is followed by the failure details. Check that the year folder in the bundle holds DBTools.dll, DBTools.Core.dll, DBTools.Presentation.dll, DBTools.HandyControl.dll and the Tools\ folder. If any file is missing, close Revit and reinstall DB Tools. The installer reports an error The installer reports Could not activate the staged DBTools bundle or a similar message when it cannot rename the bundle folder. Close Revit, close any program that holds a file in the bundle folder, and run the installer again. Antivirus software that locks files in %APPDATA% can cause this error. Revit years A Revit year that is not installed cannot be selected. To add a year later, install Revit for that year and run the installer again.

user-guide/tools/analytical-snap.html.title: Analytical Snap To Level | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/analytical-snap.html.summary: Analytical Snap To Level Analytical Snap To Level moves the end points of the selected analytical beams and columns to the elevation of a level you choose. It edits the analytical model only. The physical elements do not change. Synopsis Ribbon: DB Tools > Structural > Analytical Snap To Level. The button is enabled when at least one element is selected. Elements that are not supported analytical members are skipped and reported (see Result). Usage Select analytical members. Select the analytical members themselves, not the physical elements they represent. Click Analytical Snap To Level. In the Select Target Level dialog, select one level and confirm. Closing the dialog without a selection cancels the command with the message No target level selected. Read the Snap to Level Complete dialog. The level list is sorted by elevation, lowest first. Each entry reads <name> (Elev: <value>), where the value is the level elevation in feet with two decimals. The project has to contain at least one level. Snapping rules A member is snapped only when all of these hold: it is an analytical member (the Analytical Member category); its structural role is Beam or Column; its curve is a straight line. Role Rule Beam Both end points move to the level elevation. The member becomes horizontal. Its plan position is unchanged. Column Only the end point closer to the level elevation moves to it. The start point moves when both ends are equally close. The other end stays fixed. X and Y coordinates of every end point are unchanged. Result The whole run is one undo entry named DB Tools - Snap Analytical Elements to Level. If an unexpected error occurs, the run is rolled back and no member changes. The completion dialog shows the number of elements processed and skipped. Below that, it lists one line per skip reason with the count. Skip reason Meaning not an analytical member The element is not an analytical member (a physical element, an analytical wall or floor). Only the count is shown. role not supported The structural role is not Beam or Column (for example girder or brace). not straight The curve is not a line. The member is not changed. would collapse The snap would make the member shorter than Revit's short-curve tolerance. For each reason other than not an analytical member, the dialog lists up to 10 element IDs and and N more for the rest. Press Ctrl+Z to undo a completed run in one step. Limitations The tool snaps to levels. It does not accept a reference plane or an arbitrary elevation. To use another elevation, create a level at it. All selected members snap to the one level you choose. To snap different floors to different levels, run the tool once per floor. Braces, walls, floors and curved members are not supported.

user-guide/tools/elevation-tags.html.title: Elevation Tags | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/elevation-tags.html.summary: Elevation Tags Elevation Tags places the label of each matching spot elevation at a uniform position beside its leader end. The elevation text is re-measured and positioned from the tag type's font, text width and the view scale. The tool runs on demand from the ribbon and, optionally, each time you open a plan view. Synopsis Ribbon: DB Tools > Common > Align Elevation Tags. The button is enabled when a view is active. It processes the active view only. Supported views: floor plans, structural plans (engineering plans) and ceiling plans. In any other view type the command shows the warning banner Elevation Tags supports Floor Plans, Structural Plans, and Ceiling Plans only. Active view type: <type>. and changes nothing. Usage Open a floor, structural or ceiling plan. Click Align Elevation Tags. Read the banner. With Auto-Update Enabled on, the same alignment runs each time a supported plan view becomes active. Automatic runs show no banner. Failures go to the log. What is aligned A spot elevation is processed when all of these hold: one of its names matches a tag name pattern (see Settings); it has a leader; the elevation base of its type is not Relative. For each processed spot the tool computes the label position from the leader end, then applies the per-type offsets. It moves the label only when the new X or Y position differs from the current one after rounding both to two decimals (feet). Spots that already sit at the target position are not counted as updated. For a type whose elevation base is Project Base Point, the displayed elevation is measured from the project base point when the project base point and survey point are at different positions. Settings Open DB Tools > Settings and select the Elevation Tags pack. Setting Default Description Auto-Update Enabled On Align tags when a supported plan view is activated. Tag Name Patterns (Regex) ^DB Elevation Tag - (?:Concrete\|Steel\|Wall) Label$ Up to 3 regular expressions. A spot is processed when any pattern matches any of its names. Matching is case-insensitive. Along Leader 0 Moves the label away from the leader end (positive) or toward it (negative), along the horizontal direction of the label. Perpendicular 0 Moves the label away from the leader line (positive) or toward it (negative), vertically. A spot is tested against these names: the spot name, the spot dimension type name and its family name, and the name and family name of the type's marker symbol. Because spot elevations are a system family, the patterns match the type and marker symbol names, not only loaded family names. When the pattern list is empty, the default pattern is used. A pattern that is not a valid regular expression is skipped and logged. The two offsets are stored per spot elevation type. The settings pack has a type selector (previous and next buttons) and a live preview that shows the label, the tag origin and the leader end for the selected type with the current offsets. The offsets are in paper inches. The tool multiplies them by the view scale divided by 12 to get model units. Settings are stored per user and Revit year in %APPDATA%\DBTools\settings.<year>.json. They apply to every project. Result The command is one undo entry. The banner shows one of these messages: Message Kind Aligned N elevation tag(s). Success Aligned N elevation tag(s); M could not be updated. See the DB Tools log. Warning M elevation tag(s) could not be updated. See the DB Tools log. Warning No spot elevation tags were found in the active view. Info No spot elevation tags matched Tag Name Patterns. Check Elevation Tags settings. Info No matching elevation tags needed changes. Spot elevations without a leader are skipped. Info A failure on one tag does not stop the others. A spot whose names cannot be read counts as failed. Press Ctrl+Z to undo a manual run. Limitations Only the active view is processed. There is no multi-view command; auto-update covers each view as you open it. Linked models are not processed. Spots without a leader and spots on a Relative elevation base are skipped. The last info message does not say which of the two causes applies. The text width is measured with the Windows font engine and the tag type's font. Arial is used when the type defines no font.

user-guide/tools/erft.html.title: Extreme Roof Framing Tool | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/erft.html.summary: Extreme Roof Framing Tool The Extreme Roof Framing Tool (ERFT) adjusts structural columns and beams so their tops follow the underside of a sloped floor or roof. It changes the top offset of each column and the start and end offsets of each beam; it does not change level associations. You pick a target floor or roof and the members to adjust, check the calculated changes in a table and a 3D preview, then apply them as one undo entry. ERFT stores the result with the members, so you can edit the system later. ERFT is a Testing tool and is under development. Synopsis Ribbon: DB Tools > Testing > Extreme Roof Framing. To edit an existing system: select its members, then Modify tab > Edit ERFT. The command needs an open document. Usage Click Extreme Roof Framing. Select the target. The banner says Select a LINKED floor or roof target (press ESC to switch to HOST target selection). Click a floor or roof in a linked model, or press Esc to pick one in the host document. At the host prompt, Esc cancels. Select the source columns and beams to adjust, then click Finish. Check the target, the tolerance, the Columns and Beams tables and the preview. Click Apply. Source members ERFT accepts members of the host document only: structural columns placed at a point; structural framing with a straight location line that is not a brace. Members whose structural material name contains the word concrete (any case) are excluded, and a banner reports how many. The selection must contain a column, or a beam that connects to a column. Otherwise the launch stops with a message (see Messages). Window Target Target: shows the selected floor or roof. Pick hides the window, lets you select another target and recalculates the plan. Tolerance The tolerance is the rounding step for offset changes. Control Values Tolerance: 1/16", 1/8", 1/4" (default), 1/2", 1", or Custom Custom field Inches, at least 0.01; an invalid value shows a message and disables Apply Nearest, Up, Down Rounding direction. Up and Down are numeric: Down makes a negative change larger. The change is rounded to a multiple of the tolerance. Nearest rounds to the closest multiple, so a change smaller than half the tolerance becomes no change. Up rounds to the next multiple above the change, and Down to the next multiple below it. With a 1/4" tolerance, a +0.01" change becomes +1/4" with Up and 0 with Down; a -0.01" change becomes 0 with Up and -1/4" with Down. A row shows No Change when its rounded change is smaller than half the tolerance. Columns and Beams Table Columns Columns ID, Type, Top Offset, Delta, Status Beams ID, Type, Start Offset, End Offset, Status The status is Pending (will change), No Change or Error. Selecting a row selects the member in the preview, and clicking a member in the preview selects its row. Esc, or a click on an empty area of a table, clears the selection; Esc does not close the window. 3D Preview The preview shows the target as a transparent surface and the members at their adjusted positions, colored by status: green for Pending, gray for No Change, red for Error. Hover a member for a tooltip. Zoom to Fit fits the scene and keeps the view angle; Home returns to the default view angle. The target cannot be selected. If the graphics device fails, the preview is turned off for that window and asks you to update the graphics driver or enable GPU acceleration, then reopen the tool. Tolerance, Apply, Cancel and Pick still work. A member type whose section profile cannot be read is left out of the preview. Commands Button Action Cancel Close without changes. Apply Write the changes. Enabled when the tolerance is valid, at least one row is Pending and no row has an error. During Apply, Cancel, closing the window and a second Apply or Pick are blocked. How the changes are calculated ERFT processes columns first, then beams in dependency order. Column: the new top is the nearest point of the target's bottom surface to the column top. The change is rounded to the tolerance and added to the top offset. Beam end at a column (within 1/2"): the end follows the column's adjusted top. Beam end on another beam (within 1/2"): the end follows the adjusted supporting beam, interpolated along its plan position. Free beam end: the end goes to the nearest point of the target's bottom surface. The bottom surface is the set of faces of the target that face downward. "Nearest point" is the closest point in 3D, not a vertical projection, so a member outside the target's outline goes to its nearest edge. If the target has no downward faces, every row shows Error. Result Apply makes one undo entry, ERFT Apply Adjustments. Press Ctrl+Z to undo it. Apply: sets the column top offsets and the beam start and end offsets of the Pending rows; tags each changed member as an ERFT member of the system; saves the system (target, tolerance, rounding and offsets) in the model. If any offset, tag or stored-data write fails, Apply changes nothing. A success alert reports the number of modified columns and beams and the unchanged count, and the window closes. A failure shows an error alert and keeps the window open. Editing a system Select one or more ERFT members. On the Modify tab for Structural Columns, Structural Framing or a multi-category selection, click Edit ERFT. When the selection belongs to several systems, choose one. ERFT restores the stored target, tolerance and rounding, reads the current member geometry and offsets and calculates again. Applying again starts from the current offsets; it does not add the stored changes a second time. If some stored members no longer exist, a warning reports how many, and the others are edited. If no stored member exists, or the stored data is missing or invalid, the edit stops with a message (see Messages). Messages Alerts and banners are titled with the tool name. Some messages end with a diagnostic code in the form [SpecFail/<code>] <detail>; include it when you report a problem. Message Meaning Select a LINKED floor or roof target (press ESC to switch to HOST target selection). Target selection, first step. Select a HOST floor or roof target (press ESC to cancel ERFT launch). Target selection in the host document. Select source structural columns and beams to adjust, then click Finish. Source selection. Filtered out <n> concrete element(s) based on Structural Material name match: /\bconcrete\b/. Concrete members were removed from the selection. Could not extract geometry from the selected floor/roof. The target has no usable geometry. Select another floor or roof. Could not extract geometry from the stored target floor/roof. Edit mode: the stored target was deleted or changed. One or more selected source elements could not be analyzed. ERFT only supports point-based structural columns and straight structural framing members. A selected member is not supported. Adjust the selection. Select at least one column or beams that frame to columns. The selection has only beams, and none connects to a column. Custom tolerance must be a number of inches, at least 0.01. The custom tolerance is invalid. Apply is disabled. Applied adjustments: with the counts of modified columns, modified beams and unchanged elements Apply finished. Apply failed: followed by the reason Apply changed nothing. The window stays open. No plan to apply. Apply was clicked with no calculated plan. <n> element(s) from the original adjustment were not found and will be skipped. Edit mode: some stored members no longer exist. None of the previously adjusted elements could be found in the document. Edit mode: no stored member exists. Stored tolerance value '<value>' is invalid., Could not restore the stored rounding mode '<value>'. Edit mode: the stored data is invalid. Create a new adjustment. Cannot edit the selected ERFT system because stored plan data is missing or invalid. Edit mode: the stored data cannot be read. Limitations Only host-document members can be adjusted. The target can be in the host or in a loaded linked model. Concrete members are excluded. Brace framing and curved beams are not supported. ERFT changes offsets only, never the levels of members. See the developer page and the technical specification for the geometry, rounding and storage details.

user-guide/tools/foundation-tags.html.title: Combined Foundation Tags | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/foundation-tags.html.summary: Combined Foundation Tags Combined Foundation Tags prepares and positions the combined pier and footing tags (family DB Pier and Foundation Combined Tag). It has two commands: Update Combined Foundation Tags computes the data that the combined tag displays and writes it to shared parameters on piers and footings. Move Combined Tags moves combined tags to a corner of the footing they tag. The tool does not place tags. Place the tags with Revit's tag commands. Synopsis Ribbon: DB Tools > Structural > the foundation tags split button. The split button also contains Organize Foundation Types. Command Effect Update Combined Foundation Tags Writes Foundation Pier Top on piers, and Associated Pier and Associated Pier Elevation on footings, in the active view. Move Combined Tags Moves each matching tag in the active view to the corner of its footing that the tag's name specifies. Both commands are enabled when a view is active and process the active view only. Both are disabled while the shared-parameter prerequisites are not met (see Prerequisites). Prerequisites The update command needs three project parameters, bound as instance parameters and identified by GUID: Parameter Type Category Group Associated Pier Text Structural Foundations Identity Data Associated Pier Elevation Length Structural Foundations Identity Data Foundation Pier Top Length Structural Columns Constraints DB Tools checks the parameters when the active model changes and before each command. If a parameter is missing, has another GUID, has the wrong data type, is bound as a type parameter, or is bound to the wrong category, DB Tools raises the warning Combined Foundation Tags Disabled. The warning disables Update Combined Foundation Tags, Move Combined Tags and Organize Foundation Types. To repair the parameters: Open DB Tools > Settings and select the Combined Foundation Tags pack. Click Refresh to list the status of each required parameter. Click Install/Repair (or Fix on the warning card). Install/Repair needs an active Revit document. It loads the definitions from the embedded shared parameter file, binds them to the required categories as instance parameters, and clears the warning. It also resolves conflicts: it deletes parameters that have the same name with another GUID, or duplicate definitions with the same name, and reinstalls the DB Tools definitions. It keeps any other categories bound to these parameters and their values. If one of those bindings is a type parameter, Install/Repair changes it to an instance parameter and Revit drops its type values. Status values include MISSING, GUID_MISMATCH, DUPLICATE_NAME, WRONG_DATA_TYPE, UNBOUND, WRONG_BINDING_TYPE and WRONG_CATEGORY. Update Combined Foundation Tags Usage Open a plan view that shows the piers and footings. Run Update Combined Foundation Tags. Read the banner. With Auto-Update Enabled on (the default), the update also runs each time you activate a floor plan or ceiling plan. Automatic runs show no result banner. What it does The command considers the family instances visible in the active view. A family instance is a pier when its family name matches a pier pattern. It is a footing when its family name matches a footing pattern (see Settings). For each pier, it computes Foundation Pier Top = the Top Offset parameter (0 if absent) plus the elevation of the level in the Top Level parameter, and writes it to the pier. For each footing, it finds the pier nearest in plan (X and Y of the location points) and within 2 ft. It writes the pier's Type Mark to Associated Pier and the pier's Foundation Pier Top to Associated Pier Elevation. A footing with no pier within 2 ft gets an empty Associated Pier. A value is written only when it differs. Lengths are compared after rounding to two decimals. Revit cannot clear a length value. A footing with no pier in range keeps its previous Associated Pier Elevation and counts as skipped on every run until a pier is within 2 ft. Result The update, with its selection sets, is one undo entry. If a Revit write fails unexpectedly, the whole update is rolled back and the error is shown. A failure while creating the selection sets keeps the parameter writes and is reported. The banner reads Updated N element(s); M failed/skipped. or No elements modified. An element is counted as skipped when a pier lacks a valid Top Level, a footing or pier has no location point, a parameter is missing or read-only, or a length cannot be cleared. Outcome Banner At least one element modified Stays open. Has Select Modified, and Select Skipped when some elements were skipped. Nothing modified, some skipped Warning that closes after 10 seconds. No buttons. Nothing modified or skipped Info that closes after 6 seconds. The buttons select the elements of the run that just finished. They work only while the model that ran the update is active. Each run also creates selection sets named DB Tools - FoundationTags - Modified Elements (<timestamp>) and DB Tools - FoundationTags - Skipped Elements (<timestamp>) when the respective list is not empty. The timestamp is in Eastern time. A second run in the same second adds a suffix such as (2). The model keeps the 5 most recently created sets with the prefix DB Tools - FoundationTags - . If an automatic update fails, DB Tools shows the error and stops automatic updates for that model until you close and reopen it. After Save As, or the first save of a new model, it tries once more. The commands remain available. Move Combined Tags Usage Open a plan view with combined tags. Run Move Combined Tags. What it does The command examines the independent tags in the active view. It moves a tag when: the tag tags a Structural Foundations element (in the model or in a linked model); the tag's family or type name matches a tag family pattern; and the tag's name is a corner name. The corner name is the name of the tag, or the name of its type when the tag has no name: Top Right, Top Left, Bottom Right or Bottom Left (case-insensitive). The command computes the footing's bounding rectangle from its geometry in the footing's own X and Y axes. It selects the corner by the view's orientation, so Top Right is the corner at the top right of the view even in a rotated view. It sets the tag head position to that corner. The Z value of the tag head is unchanged. Linked footings are transformed into the host model's coordinates. The tag's leader is not changed. Result The banner reads Moved N; skipped M of K candidate tags. A candidate is skipped when the corner name is not valid, the tagged element is not a family instance with a location point, or it has no geometry. When no candidate exists, the banner says why: Message Cause No tags were found in the active view. No independent tags in the view. No tags in the active view are currently tagging structural foundation elements. The view's tags tag other categories. No tags matched the configured Tag Family Patterns. Check Combined Foundation Tags settings. Sample rejected tag families/types: <list> Tags tag foundations, but no tag family pattern matches. The move is one undo entry. If an unexpected Revit geometry or write error occurs, the whole move is canceled and no tag stays moved. Settings Open DB Tools > Settings and select the Combined Foundation Tags pack. Setting Default Used by Auto-Update Enabled On Update (runs on floor plan and ceiling plan activation) Tag Family Patterns ^DB Pier and Foundation Combined Tag(?: No Elevations)?$ Move Pier Family Patterns ^Foundation Pier(?: - Round)?$ Update Footing Family Patterns ^(?:Footing\|Pile Cap)-Rectangular$ Update Each pattern list holds up to 3 regular expressions. Matching is case-insensitive. An empty list uses the default. An invalid expression is skipped and logged. When no valid pier or footing pattern exists, the update does nothing. When no valid tag pattern exists, the move does nothing. Limitations Both commands work on the active view only. Only family instances that are visible in the active view are updated. The nearest-pier search is 2D and has a fixed 2 ft radius. Piers and footings are recognized by family name only. Families with other names need a matching pattern. The corner a tag moves to is taken from its name. A tag with another name is skipped.

user-guide/tools/framing-joins.html.title: Allow Join and Disallow Join | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/framing-joins.html.summary: Allow Join and Disallow Join The Allow Join and Disallow Join commands (the Framing Joins tool) allow or disallow joins at both ends of the selected structural framing elements. Revit joins a beam or brace to the column or framing it meets and cuts the geometry accordingly. The tool sets that behavior for many members in one operation. Synopsis Ribbon: DB Tools > Structural > the Allow Join / Disallow Join split button. Command Effect Allow Join Allows joins at both ends of each selected framing member. Disallow Join Disallows joins at both ends of each selected framing member. The top part of the split button runs the current command. The arrow lists both commands. Availability Both commands are enabled when the selection contains at least one element of the Structural Framing category. The commands are disabled when nothing is selected or when no selected element is structural framing. Usage Select the framing members. Use a selection box, Ctrl+click, or a Revit selection filter. Run Allow Join or Disallow Join. Read the confirmation banner. Selected elements that are not structural framing are ignored. Only family instances of the Structural Framing category (beams, braces and joists) are changed. Columns and other categories are not. Result The command is one undo entry named DB Tools - Allow Join Selected or DB Tools - Disallow Join Selected. It sets both ends (end 0 and end 1) of each member. A banner shows Allowed joins on N element(s). or Disallowed joins on N element(s). for 6 seconds. N counts the members processed, including members that already had the requested state. If Revit rejects the change on any member, the command stops, reports Failed to apply allow join operation for element <id>. (or disallow) and changes nothing. No member keeps a partial change. The banner No elements were modified. appears when no member was processed. Press Ctrl+Z to undo a run in a single step. Limitations The command sets both ends together. To set the ends differently, use the end-join controls in Revit. Structural columns are a separate category and are not changed.

user-guide/tools/gm.html.title: Global Mapper | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/gm.html.summary: Global Mapper Global Mapper (GM) replaces project content in bulk. You map a source (a family, a type, a line style, an object style, a material or a parameter) to a target, review the plan, and apply every mapping in one operation. GM also finds likely duplicates, ranks replacement candidates by name and property similarity, and adds shared parameters to families and categories. Synopsis Ribbon: DB Tools > Common > Global Mapper. GM opens as a modeless window and needs an open, active project. It works on the active document only. Linked files are not changed. Tab Purpose Duplicates Finds likely duplicate elements and lets you choose which one to keep. Families Maps families and their types, parameters, object styles and materials to other families. Line Styles Replaces line styles. Object Styles Replaces Detail Items object styles. Materials Replaces materials. Shared Parameters Adds shared parameters to families and categories, or maps existing parameters to them. The Shared Parameters tab needs a Revit shared parameter file with at least one group. Without one, GM disables the tab and explains why. Usage Open a tab. Choose the source rows to change and the target for each. A target can be chosen by hand or by the similarity ranking. Check Apply on each mapping to include in this run. Click Review Plan. GM opens Commit Review as a modal window and shows the plan. The model is not changed until you click Apply there. Click Apply. Then choose Keep + Continue, Keep + Close GM or Roll back (see Commit Review). Save the project before a bulk change. Header controls These controls apply to the current tab. Control Effect Search: Filters rows by name. Threshold: Slider from 0 to 100%. Sets the minimum similarity for automatic target selection. Sort mode (Similarity / A-Z) Orders target lists by similarity, with colored scores, or alphabetically with no scores. One setting covers the top-level and nested target lists. Hide Unused Hides elements with no instances in the project. Hide Unscanned Hides unscanned rows. Shown on the Families and Shared Parameters tabs only. Applied Only Shows rows with Apply on, including rows linked from other tabs. Not shown on Duplicates, which has its own status filter. Inspector Pane, Preview Panel, Views Panel, SP Authoring Pane Show or hide those panes. Clear... menu Clear Saved Mappings, Clear Saved UI State, Clear Deep Scan Cache (see Saved state). Mapping Conflicts Opens the conflict list. Shown when conflicts exist. Auto-Resolve All resolves them in the order: Duplicates, Tab Defaults, Family Overrides, Manual. The status line at the bottom left shows the loading state, the number of visible rows and the number of applied and conflicting rows of the current tab. A grid shows Loading... while data loads and a No ... message when a loaded result is empty. Similarity and threshold GM scores each target against its source. Scores are colored green (high), orange (medium) or red (low). At a threshold, an unchanged row selects the highest-scoring target at or above it. If no target qualifies, the row stays empty. A manual choice is never changed by the threshold. Opening a list and closing it without picking another entry is not a manual choice. <Do Not Map> is an explicit choice. On the Duplicates tab, the threshold controls which keep-target candidates appear for each source row. Duplicates tab The tab scans automatically when you open it. It groups elements that look like duplicates by name and property similarity. Styles and materials are matched on their previews. GM does not report two styles or materials as duplicates when it cannot read their previews. Line-style detection covers the whole line-style catalog, including styles with no family usage. Detect refreshes the catalog and the Usage rows and keeps your keep targets. Usage indexing decides which keep targets every restylable curve of a source can accept. While indexing runs, rows show line-style targets pending Usage indexing. A saved keep target stays visible, and Review Plan validates the targets after indexing. Steps Scope the rows. Category limits family rows and follows the category selected elsewhere in GM. Kind filters sources: All, Families, Materials, Line Styles, Object Styles or Shared Params. The status bar filters groups by All, Open, Resolved, Excluded or Conflicts. Group nodes show resolved counts, for example Families (133) · 45 resolved. For each source row, choose the Keep Target. A target must be in the same domain and category as the source. Check Apply for the rows that are ready to commit. Click Accept Applied to stage the rows that are ready. Click Review Plan. Columns Column Description Apply Commit flag for this session. It is off when the tab opens and is never restored from saved state. Source The element to replace, with its Kind, Suggestions and Highest Score. Keep Target The one element that remains. Save Off makes the choice apply to this run only. On saves the keep target for later sessions. Status Ready, Accepted, Mapped, or blank. A row is Ready when Apply is on, the keep target is not the source itself, the row is not excluded, and it has no validation or conflict flag. Choosing the source itself as the keep target marks the row as the keeper and turns Apply off. Accept Applied stages the rows that are Ready, not every row with Apply on. The inspector pane shows candidate details and a Metadata section with the Source ID and instance count. Its Accept split button saves the selection. The drop-down Accept Once keeps it for this session only. For a family row, Edit Type Mapping... in the context menu sets which source types map to which keep types. Shared-parameter duplicate rows can drive the selections on the Shared Parameters tab (Map From and Apply). Keep targets, the one-time-save choice, ignored candidates and exclusions are restored with the saved state. Exclusion badges (Saved, Session, Saved (Overridden)) show the exclusion time in a tooltip when it is known. Conflicts A blocking conflict prevents Review Plan. An advisory conflict (a restored saved choice that is not applied) shows in the conflict list only. The conflict button appears when any conflict exists. If one source is accepted to more than one target, GM raises a duplicate multi-target conflict and offers one-click cleanup. Choosing Keep Manual for a duplicate-versus-manual conflict clears the duplicate row's keep and apply state, so the same conflict does not return. Families tab The tab maps families in the selected category to replacement families. A family can be replaced only by a family of the same category. Columns Column Description Expand (+) Shows the row details. Quantity Instances of the family in the project. Apply Includes the mapping. Source The family. Target The replacement family. Choose the category first, then the target. Select the target with the dropdown; entries show their similarity score. Row details Expand a row to map its parts. The detail tabs are Types, Object Styles, Materials and Parameters. Object Styles and Materials are disabled when empty. The nested target lists use the same sort mode and threshold as the parent list. When you change the parent target, nested lists refill and keep the rows you changed by hand. Types: map each source type to a target type, or select <Do Not Map>. To create a type in the target family, check Create on the type row and enter New Type Name. Created types appear after the refresh that follows a commit. Parameters: map parameter names, with example values. Instance and type parameters are separate mappings, labeled (Instance) and (Type). A parameter maps only to a target of the same scope. GM copies parameter values only through these mappings, and they run with the type replacements. A red ! badge marks a conflict, such as a duplicate target parameter or a missing type-write policy. Resolve it before Review Plan. The Parameters tab shows Parameter scanning is unavailable; parameter mapping is disabled. when scanning is unavailable, and No mappable parameters detected for this family. when it finds none. Expanded rows restored from saved state refresh their Object Styles and Materials usage automatically once usage data is loaded. While a target list is open, the mouse wheel scrolls that list, not the grid behind it. Type-scope writes: if a type-scope mapping writes into a target type that already has instances, GM blocks the commit until you choose Keep target type values (skip type-scope copies) or Overwrite target type values (copy them). GM takes the decision from the model state before the replacement batch starts. Moving the target's instances away earlier in the batch does not cancel Keep target type values. When overwriting is allowed, each mapping copies the original source values, even if an earlier mapping changed that source type. Object Styles and Materials: usage found by walking one placed instance. Rows from a deep scan carry a DS badge. An instance cycler, with previous and next buttons and a zoom button, moves to the sampled instance, even when it is in another view. Badges Badge Meaning OS, MAT, OS+MAT The family Apply state is linked from the Object Styles or Materials tab. LK (OS/MAT) Marks the nested rows that currently drive that link. DS Row data came from a deep scan. A tooltip shows partial-scan warnings. A linked Apply marks the family row, but family-owned operations (type swaps, parameter maps, type creation) run only when you checked that family row yourself. A saved target that is no longer among the options is flagged as incompatible. Choose the target again. Line Styles tab The tab replaces one line style with another. Column Description Apply Includes the mapping. Source The current line style. Target The replacement. Qty The curves in this document that a commit can restyle from this style. Preview A swatch of the style. GM captures each source's curves before it applies any line-style mapping, so a swap A to B and B to A exchanges the two populations, and a chain A to B to C leaves A's curves on B and B's curves on C. The mappings commit one after another inside the single undo step of the apply. A failed mapping rolls back the whole apply. GM restyles a grouped curve only when its group, and every enclosing group, has exactly one placed instance of its group type. Curves in groups with more than one instance are not counted and not replaced, because Revit requires Edit Group mode for them. GM does not enter that mode and does not ungroup elements. Ordinary curves with the same style are counted normally. A target has to be usable by every restylable curve of the source. A saved target that is not usable stays in the saved intent, shows a warning and is left out of the plan until you choose a valid target or Do Not Map. On the Line Styles, Object Styles and Materials tabs, an unavailable saved or chosen target stays visible as a disabled entry with a reason. A refresh keeps it; choose another target to replace it. Object Styles tab The tab replaces object styles of Detail Items subcategories (styles that are not line styles). Selecting a style lists the families that use it. A preview pane shows the style. Checking Apply links the affected families on the Families tab. Unchecking it removes the link. A family keeps its Apply if you checked it or another source links it. A lock badge only tells where a mapping came from. To override a mapping that a duplicate seeded, edit its target. At commit, GM opens each affected family document and ensures the target style exists in it, creating the style when it is missing. It copies the core style appearance from the project target, rewrites the references to the source style, and reloads the family into the project. Before commit, GM leaves out a top-level mapping whose source style has no family usage and no deep-scanned family reference. A mapping found only by a deep scan is kept and appears in Commit Review. A nested mapping whose owner family no longer shows the source in the usage or deep-scan data is left out with a warning. Materials tab The tab replaces materials. Column Description Apply Includes the mapping. Source The material to replace. Target The replacement. Color Preview A swatch of the material color. Families Count Families that use the material. Families affected by a mapping are linked on the Families tab with the badge MAT or OS+MAT. In Families Using This Material, the Apply indicator shows the active link, so a linked family stays marked when a filter hides it from the Families list. At commit, GM updates material parameters in the project and in the affected family documents. When the target material is missing in a family document, GM creates it, copies its core properties and rewrites the references. It then reloads the family. A mapping whose source or target cannot be resolved in the project is ignored before commit and shown as a warning. Revit does not support formulas for parameters of the Material data type. GM migrates writable material defaults for each family type. It leaves formula-determined parameters outside the replacement. A replacement material takes over the appearance and the physical and thermal properties of the new material everywhere the old one was used. Shared Parameters tab The tab adds shared parameters to families and categories, or maps existing parameters to shared parameters. The left panel shows a tree of curated categories (Doors, Mechanical Equipment, Walls, Windows), then families, then types. Category labels show counts such as Mechanical Equipment (12), and empty categories show (0) and are dimmed. The right panel shows an authoring card for each shared parameter of the selected type. Select a group in SP Group. Expand a category and a family, and select a type. The panel shows the existing parameters with sampled values, and the shared parameters of the group. For each parameter to add, check Apply and choose the binding mode. Optionally choose Map From (or enter a formula) to fill the new parameter from an existing one. Click Review Plan. Binding mode Effect Host-level Adds the parameter to the category as a project parameter. If the parameter already has a binding, GM adds the category to it, keeps its group and refuses a change between instance and type. Embed-in-family Adds the parameter inside the family document, so it travels with the family. Plan validation checks that each selected type still belongs to its family and category. It rejects a mismatched or stale selection with an error before apply. Map From writes the value that the Examples column shows: Between two parameters of the same type (Length to Length, Text to Text, Yes/No to Yes/No), the stored value is copied exactly. Into a Text parameter, GM writes the source as shown, with the document's units (300 mm, Yes, or the name of a phase or level). Into a Length, Area or other measured parameter, GM reads the source as Revit reads typed input, in the document's units. In a millimeter project, 12 is 12 mm. Text read into a Number or Integer parameter uses the decimal separator of your Windows number format and no thousands separators. With a decimal point, 1.5 is 1.5, and 1,5 or 1,500 is not written. With a decimal comma, 1,5 is 1.5, and 1.5 or 1.500 is not written. An Integer parameter takes only whole numbers, so 2.5 is not written. A value that cannot be read this way is not written. Examples are a Yes/No into a Number, 300 mm into an Integer, or a level or phase name into another element parameter. Commit Review lists the operation as Failed, with the value, the parameter and the reason, and writes none of its values. The Formula preview reads values by the same rules, including a measured value in the unit it shows. When a value cannot be read as a number, the preview shows that it is unavailable. The first visit to the tab loads the shared parameter groups and the curated categories, with a loading overlay once. Later expanding and collapsing, searching, and conflict updates do not show the overlay. The instance navigator, between SP Group and the authoring pane, steps through sampled instances. Zoom to Instance goes to an instance even when it is not in the active view. Deep scan Some family details, such as embedded parameters and nested families, need a deep scan. A deep scan opens the family document. It is always started by you; GM does not scan when you expand a row. A deep scan is needed to: unlock the expanded details of a family with no instances (Scan required); read embedded definitions, such as nested family graphs, that a placed instance does not expose. For a family with instances, the Object Styles and Materials details come from walking one placed instance, so a deep scan is usually not needed. That walk records whether a source appears directly in the root family or only inside nested family content, and planning reuses that. Action Effect Scan Family (in the expanded details) Always runs a fresh deep scan. A complete result replaces the cache entry. An incomplete result removes the previous reusable entry. Deep Scan Unscanned (top-bar icon, Families tab) Scans all unscanned families with no instances in the current category, after a confirmation, with a progress overlay. Clear Deep Scan Cache Deletes the cached results and refreshes the display before it reports success. Results are cached across sessions. At startup GM restores cached results for eligible families with no instances. The restore is strict: if the cache entry does not resolve in the current document (for example a missing or ambiguous style or material), GM logs a warning and leaves the family unscanned. No banner appears. If you clear the cache while the restore runs, the cleared families stay unscanned until you scan them again. If Revit reports an error while GM reads a family parameter, GM keeps the names it read as diagnostics and marks parameter discovery incomplete. Those names are not offered as mapping choices and are not used for duplicate scoring. GM also removes the older reusable cache entry for that family. A separate successful read of the host can still fill the mapping choices. Otherwise, scan again after you fix the reported problem. If GM cannot fully resolve nested-family or material usage during a scan, it keeps the extracted details and warnings visible as a partial result, and does not cache or restore the family as complete. Scan again after you fix the reported references. A malformed or incomplete cache entry is deleted and needs a new scan. The cache is disposable and is not migrated between formats. Saved state GM saves your mappings and window state for each project, by its file path. Each unsaved document has its own state, so unsaved documents with the same title do not share state. On reopen, saved targets are restored as suggestions. Apply is left off, so nothing is enabled for commit. Menu item (Clear...) Effect Clear Saved Mappings Removes the mapping and duplicate selections for this document. The mappings do not return from an older saved file or from an open GM window. Clear Saved UI State Removes the tab, search, filter and scroll state. The next GM window for the document starts with default state. An open window does not write its older state back when it closes. Clear Deep Scan Cache Removes deep-scan data and the DS badges. If a deletion fails or is canceled, GM does not report success. If GM cannot write the saved mappings, it logs the failure and shows an error banner, and your mappings may not persist. If the saved-mappings file has a format that this GM version cannot read, GM shows a banner and continues without restoring it. A saved target, or a saved Shared Parameters Map From source, that no longer exists is flagged as incompatible and must be created again. A style target must belong to the scope of its source (Line Styles or Object Styles). Each of the Materials, Line Styles and Object Styles tabs lists only its own kind of element. Family-usage counts stay with the correct style after you reopen GM or refresh. Result Commit Review Review Plan opens Commit Review. Revit is blocked while it is open. The window shows: the planned operations, by section (Plan Overview, Planned Operations, Host Replacements, Family Changes, Nested Families, Shared Parameters, Validation Issues); sections that do not apply are hidden; after apply, Commit Results, Domain Summary (succeeded, failed and skipped counts per stage, with affected references, family and timing context) and Family Breakdown; an Operation Results table with a status for each operation (Pending, Succeeded, Failed, Skipped), its operation id, stage and timing. Failed operations are summarized per mapping rule, with the source and target display names rather than element ids. The status bar shows the apply phase before the commit and the Applied, Skipped and Failed counts after it. Right-click a report table for Copy Selected or Copy All. Copy Report copies the whole report. Failed in the rules summary counts failed mapping rules. One rule can run across many families. Use the Families line (Planned / Attempted / Failed) and the Failed Operations row, which adds up the per-family failures. Apply and keep Apply runs the plan as one operation. The changes stay provisional while Commit Review shows the results. The commit continues after a failed operation: failures are recorded and the remaining operations run. The overlay Cancel button requests cancellation at once. After the run, GM verifies that no references to a source remain. Outcome What you can do Every operation succeeded and verification found no remaining source Choose Keep + Continue, Keep + Close GM or Roll back. An operation failed, verification found a remaining source, or the apply was canceled GM rolls the attempt back. Nothing is kept. Inspect the errors and choose Retry Apply to run the reviewed plan against the current model. Succeeded with nonfatal warnings Labeled Completed with Warnings. The Operation Warnings section lists each distinct instance, parameter and reason. Review it before you keep the changes. Keep remains available when verification succeeds. Keep + Continue records the mappings and returns to GM. GM refreshes the mapped data in place and restores the expanded row context. Types created with Create appear in the refreshed rows. Deep Scan results stay for families the commit did not change. Scan a changed family again to restore its details. Keep + Close GM records the mappings and closes GM. Roll back restores the model and creates no undo entry. A kept apply is one undo entry named Global Mapper: Apply. Press Ctrl+Z to revert it. Do not leave Commit Review open after Apply. Choose Keep or Roll back first. Closing the window with the X: during apply, requests cancellation and cleanup, then closes. If the cleanup fails, the window stays open and shows the error; after apply, asks whether to keep or roll back, with Roll back as the default. After any apply, GM re-reads the affected rows and counts from the model, whether the apply was kept or rolled back. A banner reports the outcome. A successful apply with operation warnings shows a warning banner that ends with Operation warnings: <n>. Otherwise a green banner with the Applied, Failed and Skipped counts; a red banner that starts with the reason, for example Apply was rolled back: 1 operation(s) failed. No changes were kept. or Apply failed; no changes were kept.; or Apply was canceled. No changes were kept. If the apply fails, Commit Review stays open. If an apply seems to stall near 90%, Revit is still processing one operation. Click Cancel once and wait. GM cancels and cleans up when that operation ends. If it does not recover, report it with the newest DB Tools log. How replacement batches behave Line styles, host materials, family materials, family object styles, types, host symbols and nested-family replacements use each mapping's original source population. A swap A to B and B to A exchanges the populations. A chain A to B and B to C leaves the original A population on B and the original B population on C. References moved by an earlier mapping do not become a later mapping's source. A shared nested family can appear under several selected roots. GM combines its applicable mappings and changes each original reference once. Later family reloads keep the result. Equivalent duplicate mappings get a merged notice. Conflicting targets for the same family source need your attention. A source that is absent from a traversed family is zero work, not a failed mapping. When a family reload cannot complete, every family operation that ran in that traversal is shown as failed, including equivalent shared-family aliases. The report keeps the affected count for writes completed before the failure and shows the reason. GM rolls the whole apply back, and you can choose Retry Apply. A failed operation can report writes that succeeded before it failed. Those counts are diagnostics, and the rollback discards the writes. If one half of a swap fails, the successful half could leave both populations on one target. For that reason GM rolls back the whole apply. Unchanged shared children stay on the project version during another family's reload. Shared children that the current traversal changed are reloaded from the edited family document. The family-document counts in Commit Review include the examined root and nested family documents, including documents where a source has no references. A parent-only material mapping leaves a shared child's material defaults unchanged. Map the child itself, or include it in the traversal, to change those defaults. Messages GM reports results and problems in banners with the title Global Mapper. Message Meaning Apply completed. Applied: <n>, Failed: <n>, Skipped: <n>. Family documents attempted: <n>, family document failures: <n>. The apply finished. The banner adds Operation warnings: <n>. when operations reported warnings, and Verification warning: <text> when the reference check found a problem. Apply was rolled back: <n> operation(s) failed. No changes were kept. One or more operations failed. Inspect the errors in Commit Review and choose Retry Apply. Apply was rolled back: <reason> No changes were kept. The check after the apply found a remaining source reference. Apply failed; no changes were kept. The apply stopped with an error. Commit Review stays open. Apply was canceled. No changes were kept. You canceled the apply. Keep is unavailable: the last apply kept no changes. Retry Apply or close Commit Review. Keep was chosen after an apply that was rolled back. No conflicts to resolve. Auto-Resolve All found no conflicts. No auto-resolvable conflicts were found. The remaining conflicts need a manual choice. Queued creation of new type: '<name>'. You can rename before commit in Commit Review. A Create row was added on the Types detail tab. No unscanned (0-instance) families are eligible for deep scan. Deep Scan Unscanned has no family to scan in the current category. Deep scan cache cleared. Clear Deep Scan Cache finished. Cleared saved mappings for this document. Clear Saved Mappings finished. Cleared saved UI state. Next open will use defaults. Clear Saved UI State finished. No placed instances found to navigate to. The instance cycler has no instance to show. Saved mapping source parameter '<name>' is not available. Re-create the mapping. A saved Shared Parameters Map From source no longer exists. Configure a Revit shared parameter file that has at least one group to use this tab. The Shared Parameters tab is disabled. Set a shared parameter file in Revit. Inline texts: Deep scan to unlock details for families without instances (row tooltip): the family has no instances and no deep scan. Run Scan Family. Parameter scanning is unavailable; parameter mapping is disabled. and No mappable parameters detected for this family. (Parameters detail tab). line-style targets pending Usage indexing (Duplicates row): wait until indexing ends. When an action fails unexpectedly, GM shows an error banner titled with the action, for example GM Duplicate Type Mapping, GM Deep Scan or GM Clear Saved Mappings, followed by the error text. The action changes nothing. Retry it, and read the DB Tools log if it fails again. If Review Plan is disabled, no mapping is applied, or a blocking conflict exists. If the target list is empty, the category has no other family. If some instances were not replaced, open the family and check that every type is mapped. Limitations GM changes the active document only. A family can only be replaced by a family of the same category. Line style and object style scopes are limited as described above: curves in multi-instance groups are not restyled, and the Object Styles tab covers Detail Items subcategories only. Commit time grows with the number of elements and families. A few dozen changes finish at once; thousands can take minutes. The progress overlay shows the state. The Shared Parameters tab lists the curated categories only: Doors, Mechanical Equipment, Walls and Windows.

user-guide/tools/joist-girder-weight.htm.title: Joist Girder Weights | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/joist-girder-weight.htm.summary: Joist Girder Weights Joist Girder Weights estimates the weight per foot of joist girders from their span, depth, panel count and panel point load, and writes the result to the Wt parameter of each girder. The estimate is for preliminary design and takeoffs. It does not replace the manufacturer's tables. Synopsis Ribbon: DB Tools > Structural > Update Joist Girder Weights. The command processes the whole model. It does not depend on the selection or the active view. Usage Make sure each girder family provides the inputs listed under Family requirements. Click Update Joist Girder Weights. Read the banner. With Auto-Update Enabled on (the default), the same update runs each time you activate a view, with no banner. Disable it in the settings if view changes are slow in a large model. Which elements are processed The tool collects the elements of the Structural Framing category whose family name matches the Family/Type Name Pattern. It matches the type name only when the family name is unavailable. Default pattern: ^(?:(?:[BV]?G)|Vulcraft) Joist Girder$. It matches G Joist Girder, BG Joist Girder, VG Joist Girder and Vulcraft Joist Girder. Family requirements Each parameter is read from the instance first and then from the type. Names match case-insensitively where the parameter is looked up by alias. Input Parameter names Notes Number of joists (N) Number of Joists, SpaceNum, Number of Equal Spaces Must be greater than 1. Length Cut Length, then Length Must be greater than 0. Depth Depth Must be greater than 0. Panel point load Parameters matched by the load patterns See Load resolution. Output Wt A writable decimal-number parameter, such as a Number parameter, on the instance or the type. Numeric inputs may be decimal-number, integer or text parameters. A text value has to parse as a number. Load resolution Load parameters are found by matching their names against the three load patterns. Matching parameters are collected from the instance and the type. Pattern Default Matches, for example Dead Load (?:^DL$\|Dead\s*Load) Dead Load, DL Live Load (?:^LL$\|Live\s*Load) Live Load, LL Total Load (?:Point\s*Load\|Total\s*Load) Point Load, Panel Point Load, Total Load The load is resolved as follows: A negative value in any load parameter skips the girder as invalid. More than one parameter with a value in any one group (Total, Dead or Live) skips the girder as ambiguous. This check comes first: one Total Load value plus two Dead Load values skips the girder. If exactly one Total Load parameter has a value, it is the panel point load. Otherwise, if exactly one Dead Load and exactly one Live Load parameter have values, their sum is the panel point load. Otherwise the girder is skipped. A single Total Load value takes precedence over single Dead and Live values. Load values are converted to kips. A Force parameter is converted from its stored unit. A number with no unit is taken as kips. Text values accept a number followed by an optional unit: kip, kips, k, lb, lbs, lbf, pound, pounds or kN (for example 10 kips, 10000 lb, 45 kN). To use other parameter names, such as localized names, change the patterns in the settings. Settings Open DB Tools > Settings and select the Joist Girder Weights pack. Setting Default Auto-Update Enabled On Family/Type Name Pattern ^(?:(?:[BV]?G)\|Vulcraft) Joist Girder$ Dead Load Pattern (?:^DL$\|Dead\s*Load) Live Load Pattern (?:^LL$\|Live\s*Load) Total Load Pattern (?:Point\s*Load\|Total\s*Load) An empty pattern field uses the default. A pattern that is not a valid regular expression is reported as a configuration error. In that case the manual command shows the error as a warning banner for 10 seconds and changes nothing. Auto-update shows the same banner and raises the tool warning Joist Girder Weights Disabled, which disables the command until you clear the warning in the settings. Calculation The estimate uses N joists (N - 1 panels), panel point load P (kips), length L and depth D, in inches: panel spacing = L / N; maximum moment from the end reaction P(N - 1)/2, less the moments of the panel loads between the support and midspan; chord force = moment / (0.95 D); required chord area = chord force / (50 ksi x 0.6); top chord weight = area x L x 0.28356 lb/in^3 x 1.06; bottom chord weight = 1.13 x top chord weight; web weight = 0.7 x top chord weight; Wt = (top + bottom + web) / (L in feet), in lb/ft. The value is written to Wt as a number, without a unit conversion. Result The manual command writes all valid girders as one undo entry named Auto Update Joist Girder Weights. A girder that fails validation is skipped, and the rest are updated. The banner shows: Candidates: <n> Updated: <n> Skipped: <n> Sample skipped element(s): - Element <id>: <reason> The sample list holds up to 5 skipped girders. The banner is a success banner when nothing was skipped, a warning when some girders were skipped, and informational when none were updated. No joist girders were found. appears when no element matches the family pattern. Press Ctrl+Z to undo a manual run. Limitations The tool writes only Wt. It changes no other parameter. The calculation uses a fixed allowable stress and fixed efficiency factors. Check the results against manufacturer data for final design. Auto-update runs on every view activation and reads every matching girder. It adds delay in models with many girders.

user-guide/tools/organize-foundation.htm.title: Organize Foundation Types | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/organize-foundation.htm.summary: Organize Foundation Types Organize Foundation Types renames pier, footing and pile cap types by their dimensions, assigns sequential type marks, and merges types that have identical dimensions. It changes types. It does not move placed instances. Synopsis Ribbon: DB Tools > Structural > the foundation tags split button (with Update Combined Foundation Tags and Move Combined Tags). The command processes the whole model. It is disabled while the Combined Foundation Tags Disabled warning is active (see Combined Foundation Tags). Usage Save the model.
