Run Organize Foundation Types. Answer Do you want to overwrite existing type marks? Read the Organize Foundation Types result dialog. Answer Effect Yes Regenerates the type mark of every processed type. No Keeps existing type marks. Types with an empty type mark receive a new one. Processed types The tool processes types of these families (exact names, case-sensitive): Family Category Dimension parameters Mark prefix Foundation Pier Structural Columns b, h P Foundation Pier - Round Structural Columns d RP Footing-Rectangular Structural Foundations Width, Length, Foundation Thickness F Pile Cap-Rectangular Structural Foundations Width, Length, Foundation Thickness CAP Types of other families are not processed. Naming and marks Each type is renamed as <dimensions> (<mark>). Dimensions are formatted in feet and fractional inches. Family Name format Example Foundation Pier <b>x<h> (<mark>) 2'-6"x2'-6" (P-1) Foundation Pier - Round <d> DIA. (<mark>) 2'-0" DIA. (RP-1) Footing-Rectangular <width>x<length>x<thickness> (<mark>) 3'-0"x3'-0"x1'-0" (F-3.0) Pile Cap-Rectangular <width>x<length>x<thickness> (<mark>) 4'-0"x4'-0"x2'-0" (CAP-4.0) Types are processed in ascending order of size, and marks are assigned in that order: piers: section area b x h; round piers: diameter; footings and pile caps: width, then length, then thickness. Pier and round pier marks are P-1, P-2, ... and RP-1, RP-2, .... Footing and pile cap marks are <prefix>-<w>.<n>, where <w> is the width in whole feet (rounded down) and <n> counts from 0 within that width: F-3.0, F-3.1, CAP-4.0. Merging Types of one family with equal dimension values are duplicates. The tool keeps the first in the sort order, changes every instance of the other types to the kept type, and deletes the other types. Equality is exact on the stored values, so types that differ by a small amount are not merged. Instances stay where they are. Result The run is one undo entry. The result dialog shows the number of types renamed, duplicates merged and types skipped: Successfully organized pier and footing types. - N types renamed - N duplicates merged - N types skipped When types are skipped, the first line reads Organized pier and footing types with skipped types. and the dialog adds up to 5 lines <type id>: <reason>. A type is skipped when Revit rejects its change, for example when the new name already exists. The remaining types are still processed. If a merged type cannot be deleted, the command fails and changes nothing. Press Ctrl+Z to undo the whole run. Limitations With No, the tool does not compare new marks with preserved marks that come later in the sort order, so two types can end with the same mark. Use Yes for a consistent set. The tool changes only the type name and the Type Mark parameter, and the type of merged instances. The type mark is written only when the Type Mark parameter is a writable text parameter. Linked models are not processed. Types that Revit rejects are skipped, not retried.

user-guide/tools/recordset.html.title: Record Set | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/recordset.html.summary: Record Set Record Set packages Revit host models together with the files they reference. It copies the selected RVT host files and their file-based links (RVT, DWG and other external references) into a target folder with a fixed folder structure, optionally processes DWG Xrefs with AutoCAD Core Console, and rewrites the references in the copied RVT files so they point to the copies. Before it writes anything, Record Set shows the planned output tree and any problems. Record Set is a Testing tool and is under development. Synopsis Ribbon: DB Tools > Testing > Record Set. The command opens the modal Record Set window. It needs an open document. Usage Click Target Folder... and choose the output folder. The folder must be inside an allowed target root (see Safety checks). Change picks another folder. Click Add Revit File... (or Add host) and pick one or more host RVT files. In the Host Models grid, set Discipline and Building for each host. Read the Preview tree and the Preview Messages. For DWG files, set the CAD handling from the DWG's context menu in the preview tree. Click Execute when the preview is current and has no blocking message. Canceling a file or folder picker changes nothing. Window Target folder Shows the selected output folder. The footer reports: Field Values Root Pending, Allowed or Blocked: whether the target is inside an allowed root Free Free space on the target drive ACAD The AutoCAD Core Console path, or Unavailable Sentinel Pending, Present or Missing: the .recordset_sentinel file in the target Host Models Column Purpose Host File File name of the host RVT (read-only) Discipline Discipline folder of the host and its links. Empty adds no folder. Building Building folder. The default - adds no folder. The Discipline and Building lists have a < Add new… > choice that asks for a new value; canceling the prompt keeps the previous value. Right-click a row and choose Remove Host to remove it. When you add hosts, Record Set reads each host's external references. A host that is already in the list, or picked twice, is skipped with a message. A host whose references cannot be read is rejected and does not appear in the grid. Record Set does not read links of linked RVT models. Preview The tree shows the proposed output folder structure. It is rebuilt automatically 350 ms after the last change to the target, hosts, metadata or CAD settings. Options menu: Item Effect Manage Disciplines... Add, rename and delete discipline names. Renames and deletes apply to the hosts and links that use them. Manage Buildings... The same for building names. Auto-discover CAD Xrefs Read the Xrefs of each DWG with AutoCAD Core Console and copy them beside the DWG. Allow CAD repath Rewrite Xref paths in the copied DWG files. These items are disabled until a host exists. The two CAD options follow Core Console availability until you set them; your choice lasts until the window closes and is not saved. Right-click a DWG in the tree for its CAD actions: Item Effect CAD: Keep Xrefs Copy the DWG and its Xrefs (the default). CAD: Bind All Bind all Xrefs into the copied DWG with AutoCAD Core Console. Clears manually added Xrefs. Bind Type > Bind / Insert AutoCAD BINDTYPE 0 or 1. Bind keeps Xref-prefixed names; Insert merges names and can produce name conflicts. Add Xref... Add a DWG Xref by hand, copied beside the DWG. Preview Messages Messages have the severity Info, Warning or Block. Any Block message disables Execute. Examples: a file excluded by the safety policy (Warning); a planned source file that does not exist (Block); a destination name collision; the second file is renamed name (2).ext, name (3).ext and so on (Warning); Auto-discover CAD Xrefs disabled. or AutoCAD Core Console not found. DWG Xrefs copied by heuristic only. (Info); CAD: Bind All, or discovery together with repath, without Core Console (Block); a plan larger than 80 GiB or more than 10,000 items (Block). Manage Items The Manage Disciplines and Manage Buildings dialog has Add, Rename, Delete and Close. Names are trimmed and compared without case; a duplicate is ignored on Add and rejected on Rename. Close is the default button, so Enter closes the dialog. Output structure File Destination Host {target}\{building}\{discipline}\{host}.rvt Link used by one host {target}\{building}\{discipline}\Linked Files\{name} Link used by two or more hosts {target}\Common Linked Files\{name} A - building and an empty discipline add no folder. A link counts as common when the same full path and type appear at least twice, also twice in one host. DWG files Keep Xrefs with discovery and Core Console: the DWG's referenced files are copied beside the copied DWG. With Allow CAD repath, Record Set then strips the old root from the Xref paths in the copy. Keep Xrefs without discovery or without Core Console: Record Set copies sibling folders named xrefs, xref, refs, ref, external, dwg or cad next to the DWG. Xref paths are not rewritten, so references can break. Bind All: the DWG is copied and its Xrefs are bound into the copy. No Xref files are copied. Core Console is found through the ACCORECONSOLE environment variable, then accoreconsole.exe on PATH, then AutoCAD 2026, 2025 or 2024, then DWG TrueView 2025 under C:\Program Files\Autodesk. Revit references In each copied host, Record Set rewrites the external references that point to copied files and leaves the loaded or unloaded state unchanged. A host with at least one rewritten reference is saved as transmitted. A transmitted workshared copy opens detached and cannot create new local files. Library references (for example keynote and assembly-code tables in a content library) are not copied or changed. Safety checks The safety policy is built into Record Set and cannot be changed by the user. The target folder must be inside an allowed root. The shipped root is \\fileserver\Projects. Files with the extensions .dwl, .dwl2, .tmp, .bak, .lnk and .exe, and files matching *backup*.rvt, *.old and ~$*, are not copied. The target drive must keep at least 10 GiB (10,737,418,240 bytes) free after the copy. Execute checks the policy again and checks every output path, after resolving file and folder redirects, before it writes. Result Execute runs the plan in order under a progress overlay that cannot be canceled. Editing and closing the window are disabled while it runs. Record Set creates {target}\.recordset.lock (only one run per target at a time) and {target}\.recordset_sentinel. It creates folders, copies files (overwriting existing files and keeping their timestamps), runs the CAD operations and rewrites the Revit references. It writes {target}\_recordset_manifests\{run_id}.json with the run ID, plan fingerprint, target, UTC time, the summary counts and the status (ok, cancelled or failed). It removes the lock. An alert then shows Status: ok and the manifest path. A failure shows no alert and no banner: Record Set logs the error with its details and opens the logger window. With Debug Mode on, the logger window also opens when the Record Set window closes. Limitations A failed run is not rolled back: copied or rewritten files stay in the target. Read the log and the manifest before you clean the output or run again. If a run stops without removing .recordset.lock, the next run at that target fails. Delete the lock only when no run is active. There is no cancel action during Execute. The size and item limits are preview estimates, not limits on the final package size. CAD repath strips a matching root prefix only; it does not follow Xrefs that were renamed because of a collision. Linked RVT models are not scanned for their own links. The safety policy and its allowed root are fixed in the tool. See the developer page and the technical specification for the plan format, fingerprint and audit files.

user-guide/tools/sgt.html.title: Super Girt Tool | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/sgt.html.summary: Super Girt Tool The Super Girt Tool (SGT) places horizontal girts and opening framing (headers, sills and jambs) on one wall in one operation. You configure every girt row and opening of the wall in one window, check the result in a 2D and 3D preview, and place all members together. SGT stores the configuration with the members, so you can edit, update or remove the system later. Use SGT to: add girts to a host foundation wall or a wall in a linked model; frame doors, windows and penetrations with headers, sills and jambs; keep girt spacing and alignment consistent along a wall; edit or update a girt system placed earlier. Synopsis Ribbon: DB Tools > Structural > Super Girt Tool. To edit an existing system: select one of its members, then Modify | Structural Framing > Edit SGT Wall. The button appears only when SGT members are selected. SGT supports these structural framing shapes: C and MC channels, Z shapes, angles and HSS. Girts can use any of them. Opening members (headers, sills and jambs) use channels or HSS only. Types that analysis found unusable cannot be selected. Usage Click Super Girt Tool. Select a wall in a linked model, or a host foundation wall. SGT analyzes the wall and fills the window. Check the seeded girts. SGT seeds girt rows at a spacing of at most 5'-0". Change elevations and types as needed. Configure the openings. In linked mode, SGT detects the openings. In foundation mode, click Add Opening for each opening. Turn the framing roles on or off. Check the layout in the Elevation, Section and 3D previews. Click Place. SGT computes rotation, justification and position from the selected framing types and the wall. Wall setup Control Purpose Offset Distance from the selected layer plane along the wall depth. 0 places the girt's exterior flange on the layer face; positive values move girts outward, negative values inward. Layer The wall layer plane that girts align to, for compound walls. The default is the most-exterior structural layer; without one, the thickest non-finish layer, or the thickest layer when all layers are finishes. Ties prefer the exterior layer. The list shows the layers of the analyzed wall and follows the current plan, also when the preview cannot update. Girts Each row is one girt at one elevation. Column Purpose (chevron) Opens the segment flyout of a segmented girt Elevation Height above the plan base Girt Type Structural framing family and type, for example C Shapes : C10X15.3 Rotation Cross-section rotation: 0°, 90°, 180° or 270° Y Justification Lateral justification: Left, Center, Right or Origin. The Revit Y offset stays zero. Z Justification Vertical justification: Top, Middle, Bottom or Origin. The Revit Z offset stays zero. Flip Revit Flip Facing. Available only when the type supports facing flips, as found during analysis. To add a girt, type an elevation in the field next to Add Girt and click Add Girt. The row context menu has Move Up, Move Down, Add Row Below, Duplicate Selected and Delete Selected. Select several rows to edit them together. A girt is split at each opening it crosses, unless it bypasses the opening. A girt split in this way shows a chevron in the first column. Click it to open the segment flyout, where you edit Type, Rotation, Y, Z and Flip of each segment, or delete a segment. The selected segment is highlighted in the preview. The flyout opens to the right of the chevron, centered vertically in the window; resizing widens mainly the Type field. The background is dimmed lightly, so the preview stays visible. When opening edits merge the segments back into one, the chevron goes away. Rotation values: 0: default orientation (web vertical, flanges horizontal). 90: rotated 90°. 180: rotated 180° from the default. 270: rotated 270° (-90°). Channels used as horizontal girts usually use 0 or 180. Y justification: Left: member shifted toward the wall start. Center: member centered on the placement line. Right: member shifted toward the wall end. Origin: the family origin. Z justification: Top: top of the member at the elevation. Middle: center of the member at the elevation. Bottom: bottom of the member at the elevation. Origin: the family origin. Elevations and offsets Elevation and offset fields accept: decimal feet: 7.5; feet with an apostrophe: 7'; feet and quoted inches: 7'-6", 7'-6 1/2"; quoted inches: 18", 6.5", 6 1/2". Spaces are allowed around the marks, the hyphen and the fraction slash. One leading + or - applies to the whole value, for example -6 1/2". Unit names (ft, in, metric units), localized decimal commas, exponents, signs on components, unquoted fractions and trailing text are rejected. Openings In linked mode, SGT detects the openings of the linked wall; you can also add manual openings. In host foundation mode, SGT ignores the openings of the Revit wall, and the grid contains only openings you add with Add Opening. Column Purpose Opening Name of the opening Source Live (detected) or Manual Center Along Distance along the wall from the wall start Bottom Elevation Distance from the plan base to the bottom of the opening Width, Height Rough opening size Left Jamb, Right Jamb, Header, Sill Turn the framing member on or off Member Typical use Header Above most openings Sill Below windows; often off for doors at grade Left Jamb, Right Jamb Usually both on; turn one off when the opening is at a wall end The chevron of an opening row opens the segment flyout for its members: role-level Type, Rotation, Y, Z and Flip and, when a role is segmented, one child row per segment. It behaves like the girt segment flyout. Opening row edits are drafts. While you edit Center Along, Bottom Elevation, Width, Height or a role checkbox, the preview shows the last committed plan. Leave the row or press Enter to commit the row, which re-segments and refreshes the preview once. Esc cancels the draft (see Limitations). If you turn on a role and change its Type, Rotation, Y, Z or Flip before you leave the row, the commit keeps those settings. An invalid row stays in edit mode, and the last committed plan stays, until you fix the highlighted fields or cancel. When analysis of a linked wall finds no openings, SGT shows an information banner, removes stale detected rows and keeps manual openings. Saving edits together An opening commit, a segment flyout edit and a preview edit (snap, gap, delete, merge) each save your other unsaved field edits in the same step; for example, a wall offset you typed just before you clicked another opening row, or a field you changed while the 3D preview was building. While any wall setup, girt or opening field is invalid, SGT refuses such an edit and writes nothing: the opening row stays in edit with its values; the gap editor stays open with the typed gap, also when the preview redraws, until you press Enter again or Esc; a refused flyout choice shows the saved value again; your other unsaved field edits stay; the preview status shows the reason: Fix invalid fields, Fix invalid rows or Preview blocked. Deleting girt rows in the grid, also an invalid row, is never refused. The next sync renumbers the segment group of the deleted row; a group left with one row becomes a plain girt. Undo and Redo Undo and Redo apply to preview edits: drag and snap edits of girt and opening-member handles, typed gap changes, segment deletes and merges. Undo of a typed gap restores the previous override. An accepted typed gap change clears the redo history. Undo and Redo restore the whole plan, so they also replace unsaved field edits, including an invalid field. Bulk edit Double-click a row in either grid to open the Bulk Edit flyout. It is an overlay inside the SGT window, so it stays with the window when you minimize and restore it. Targets: the member roles the operation applies to (Girt, Left Jamb, Right Jamb, Header, Sill). Flip: three states; the indeterminate state leaves Flip unchanged. Apply (N): applies the N selected fields (Type, Rotation, Y, Z, Flip). Ctrl+Enter applies; Esc closes. Preview The preview on the right shows what SGT will place. Mode Content Elevation Front view of girts and openings, seen from the exterior. The wall start is at the right. Section Cross-section of the wall at the section marker (see Section preview) 3D Interactive 3D view The Role Palette shows the role colors: Girt blue, Header green, Sill orange, Left Jamb purple, Right Jamb cyan. In Elevation and Section mode the legend also shows segment types. The mode selector, Zoom to fit and Reset view are at the top right of the preview. Entering 3D, and Reset view, show the exterior home camera: a three-quarter view with a slight downward pitch, also for mirrored or rotated links. Other updates keep your camera. Wheel zoom allows close inspection. Pan and orbit stop on mouse-up and when the window loses focus. Click an element in 3D to select it (gold highlight) and show a tooltip with its role and section name. A click selects on mouse-up; a drag pans. Clicking a wall layer shows layer information and keeps the selection. Clicking empty space clears the selection. When a segment is selected, the other segments of the same member are dimmed slightly and unrelated elements fully. 3D shows wall layers as faint context geometry with the selected layer emphasized, thin outlines of all detected openings and a transparent floor plane. Text, line weights and styling use a fixed visual scale; hit testing (snap thresholds, hit radii) follows the display scaling. Grid markers in Elevation are white bubbles with black labels. Elevation, Section and 3D show the same member positions, orientations and segment order that Place and Update write. Profiles in the preview come from temporary instances placed during analysis, with rotation applied first, then Flip, then justification, like placed members. On a wall that is not at a right angle to the project axes, jambs are analyzed and placed with a small rotation correction; the Rotation column still shows 0, 90, 180 or 270. Section preview The Section mode shows a cross-section of the wall at the position of the section marker. The section marker is the blue dashed vertical line on the Elevation preview. Drag it to change the cut position. The marker snaps to 6" steps along the wall. The filled triangles at its top and bottom point screen-left: the section looks along the wall toward the screen-left side of the Elevation preview (the wall end). Dragging the marker changes the view only. In the section, screen-left is the exterior face of the wall and screen-right is the interior face. Horizontal members (girts, headers, sills) are drawn from their section profiles. When the cut meets a jamb edge, the jamb is drawn as a vertical depth band over its placed height, as Revit places it. For a compound wall, the section draws each layer as a band across the wall thickness, labeled <material> - <thickness>. The layer selected in Layer is highlighted. The section shows only the members whose extent along the wall meets the clip range, like the far clip offset of a Revit section view: the range is 2'-0" long, from the section marker toward the screen-left side of the Elevation preview; the Elevation preview shows the range as a translucent blue band, bounded on the left by a dashed line; girts, headers, sills and jambs that lie fully outside the range are hidden in the section. Editing in the preview Drag handles in the Elevation preview to change girt and opening-member extents. Handles snap only to valid associations: other members, grid lines, opening edges and wall edges. There is no free position along the wall. A drag commits only when it ends within snap distance of an accepted target; until then the border and guide show the invalid state. While you drag, available targets show as dim bands and the active guide as a line: cyan when valid, red when invalid. When several handles overlap, press Tab to cycle them (Shift+Tab reverses), Enter to confirm and Esc to cancel. Openings have no drag handles; edit their geometry in the grid. Segmented opening members have handles per segment; dragging one moves that segment's extent. On a girt split by openings, only the outer endpoints (the start of the first segment and the end of the last) move the girt's extents. The other segment endpoints edit the gap at an opening edge. Each one belongs to its opening and edge, also in a mirrored or rotated link. An opening's lower edge is the edge nearer the wall start; its higher edge is nearer the wall end. A girt's start snaps to the higher edge, and its end to the lower edge, of an opening that crosses the girt. For a girt inside one opening, the start snaps to the lower edge and the end to the higher edge. Edges of an opening the girt bypasses are offered too; snapping to one clears the bypass. An edge that would leave the girt no span of at least 6" (0.5 ft) is not offered. Dragging an interior endpoint of a split girt to the opposite edge of the same opening joins the segments into one girt that bypasses the opening. Jamb, header and sill handles, and girt segment handles other than the girt's own start and end, are offered all eligible opening edges in the preview, not only those of the selected opening row. Snapping a girt endpoint to a new association clears the gap override of that endpoint and edge, so the default gap for the new association applies. Merging adjacent girt segments re-targets opening-member extents that referenced either segment to the merged segment. Right-click a segmented opening member to delete that segment. Row delete commands appear in the row menu. Deleting the last segment of a role removes the role; the opening row stays until all its roles are removed. To limit a girt to grid lines, drag its start or end handle to a grid line that crosses the wall. Drag it to the wall edge to return to the full length. Gaps and segmentation rules A girt whose start is on an opening's lower edge and whose end is on the same opening's higher edge lies inside that opening. Every other girt is split at each opening it crosses, unless it bypasses the opening. An opening splits girts even when all its framing roles are off. Girt pieces shorter than 6" (0.5 ft), for example a narrow pier between two close openings, are left out of the preview and of placement. A girt with no piece of at least 6" cannot be placed. A girt end at an opening edge gets the gap of the jamb at that edge, or 0 when there is no jamb. A girt end on a wall edge or grid line that lies exactly on the edge of an opening the girt stops at also gets that edge's jamb gap. A gap override you set replaces the default. Gap override fields reject NaN and Infinity; negative values are allowed. Invalid overrides fail plan validation before placement. When the opening or grid line a girt end was attached to is removed, or the opening no longer crosses the girt (after an opening edit or a shorter wall), SGT moves that end to the nearest opening edge at least 6" from the girt's other end, or to the wall edge, and clears that end's gap override. A gap override of the edge it moves to is kept. When two segments of one girt then overlap, SGT merges them into the first. When re-segmentation leaves fewer than two segments in a group, SGT turns the group back into one row. If a geometry-based gap cannot be computed (a missing profile or a transform failure), SGT reports an error. Reopen SGT to analyze the wall again. Commands Button Action Cancel Close without placing or updating. Undoes every change made in the window. Place Create all configured members (new system). Update Edit mode: update the existing members. Review Changes Edit mode: open Change Review. Delete System Edit mode: delete all elements tagged with the system ID, including tagged copies, and the stored system. Place and Update are disabled when there is nothing valid to place; the tooltip gives the reason. Keyboard Key Action Tab Grid: next cell. Preview: cycle overlapping handles near the cursor (Shift+Tab reverses). Enter Commit an edit. Delete Delete the selected grid rows. Esc Cancel the current edit, or close a flyout. Ctrl+Enter Apply a bulk edit. Edit an existing system Select a member of the system in Revit. When several SGT systems exist on different walls, select a member of the wall you want to edit. On the Modify | Structural Framing tab, click Edit SGT Wall. Change the configuration in the SGT window. Click Update, or Delete System to remove it. Opening rows show their source, Live or Manual. Editing the position or size of a live opening makes it Manual; its distance from the wall start stays fixed when the wall length changes. Change Review When an edited wall or opening differs from the stored observation, SGT opens Change Review before it writes the update; you can also open it with Review Changes. Each row shows the opening's source name (or Manual opening for an unnamed manual row), its source, its status and its decision. The details pane shows the effects of the selected row. Placement validation messages show the along-wall range of an opening outside the wall bounds. Decisions: Accept adopts the current live observation and applies its framing at the next Update. Keep keeps the placed or manual geometry and framing for this session. Ignore leaves the existing framing unchanged and asks again at a later review. An opening you edited in this session returns to its placed geometry and framing. A manual opening that was never placed stays unframed; choose Keep at a later review in the same session to frame it again. Update does not save an ignored manual opening that was never placed. Saved live openings that are missing from a successful observation need a decision. An incomplete observation shows the opening as Unreadable and never deletes it. Without a live observation, a row offers only Keep and Ignore. The review also lists wall and layer changes, remembered decisions, accepted removals that wait for Update, and girt ends that will be re-anchored. Same as and Pair pair a missing live opening with a current opening. Unpair restores the previous pairing and its draft row. Locate selects the source element when it exists. Relink picks a new wall for a system whose wall reference changed. SGT analyzes the selected wall and rebuilds the review draft before any decision is saved. Delete System removes the stored system and its placed members. Deconstruct removes the stored system and the SGT tags and keeps the members in the model. Confirm saves the review plan and decisions in the current session. It does not change Revit members; click Update afterward. Cancel closes the review without saving its decisions. The main window's Cancel, an error or a forced close undoes these changes, including a confirmed review. Result All changes of one SGT window session become one Super Girt Tool undo entry when the window closes successfully. Cancel, an error or a forced close undoes every change of the session. Place creates the configured members and stores the system with them. Update moves the existing members in place. If a required member cannot be matched or moved, Update stops with an error; it does not delete and recreate members. Place and Update set each girt's Start and End Extension from its end gaps (0 where there is no gap), so placed girts match the preview. They replace a family default extension, and Update replaces an extension typed on a placed SGT girt. If Update must change an extension whose parameter is missing or read-only, it fails and undoes its changes. Delete System deletes the members and the stored system. Deconstruct keeps the members as plain framing. Validation failures are reported before any change. If the stored data of a system uses a format that this SGT version cannot read, SGT removes that stored data and the SGT tags of the system when the window closes successfully. Cancel, an error or a forced close keeps them. The framing members are not deleted. Place the system again. Messages SGT shows its messages in banners titled Super Girt Tool (Change Review for the review window). An error banner starts with the action that failed and a bracketed code, in the form <action>: [<code>] <detail>, for example Member snap failed: [GirtSnap/NoUsableSpan] <detail>. Message Meaning No valid wall was selected. Pick a linked wall or a host wall. The selection is not a supported wall. No eligible structural framing families found (only C/MC channels, Z shapes, ANGLE shapes, and HSS are supported). The project has no supported framing family. Load at least one, for example C Shapes, before you start SGT. No eligible structural framing types (C/MC channel, Z, ANGLE, HSS) available to select a default girt type for <context>. SGT cannot choose a default girt type. Load a supported framing type. Prepared <n> girt rows. Detected <n> openings. Analysis finished. No openings were auto-detected. Add openings manually if needed. Analysis of a linked wall found no openings. Orientation analysis failed for some families (girts: <n> families; openings: <n> role/family groups). Affected types are marked with warning icons and may not have usable defaults. Some types cannot be oriented. Choose another type for the marked rows. Profile warmup failed for <n> family types; placement/update may fail for those types until the family geometry is fixed. The section profile of some types cannot be read. Invalid elevation: '<text>'. Use feet/inches (e.g., 2', 8" or 0.25). The Add Girt elevation cannot be read. See Elevations and offsets. Analyze the wall before adding manual openings. Add Opening was used before the wall analysis finished. Flip Facing is not supported for girt type <type>. The type does not support Flip. Re-anchored <n> girt end(s) to the nearest opening or wall edge. Girt ends moved because their opening or grid line was removed. Merged <n> overlapping girt segment(s) into their neighbors. Segments of one girt overlapped and were merged. Auto-segmentation collapsed <n> girt group(s). Segment groups with fewer than two segments became plain girts. Undo unavailable: the segment group changed after deletion. Edit history was cleared; later changes were kept. A deletion changed the segment group, so the undo history was cleared. Preview blocked: ..., Preview update failed: ... The preview cannot show the current plan. Fix the reported field, or reopen SGT. Member snap failed: ..., Segment snap failed: ..., Gap edit failed: ... A preview edit was refused. The plan is unchanged. Segment deletion failed: ..., Segment merge failed: ..., Opening segment deletion failed: ... A segment edit was refused. The plan is unchanged. Opening sync failed: ... An opening row edit cannot be applied. The plan changed during review. Review Changes again before confirming. The plan changed while Change Review was open. System deleted (<n> elements deleted) Delete System finished. System deconstructed (<n> framing elements retained) Deconstruct finished. Layout preferences were not saved. Model changes were applied. The window layout was not saved. The model changes are kept. No active document. Open a Revit document first. Edit SGT Wall was clicked without an open document. The Place and Update tooltip gives the reason when they are disabled: Run Analyze before placing, Fix enabled opening roles with missing Type, Nothing to place (no valid girts and no enabled opening roles), No eligible girt types available or No eligible opening types available. Place and Update report a failure for each girt segment that cannot be placed, with the same text for both. For example, a girt family without Start and End Extension parameters reports Writer/ExtensionParamMissing when an end gap needs them, and a missing opening framing type reports Plan/EligibleOpeningTypesMissing. A header or sill split position outside the wall makes Place or Update fail with a message that names the opening. Troubleshooting Girts are not where you expect Check Layer: girts align to the selected layer plane. Check Offset. Check Rotation and the justifications, and look at the 3D preview. The preview shows nothing Make sure at least one girt row exists with a valid type. For openings, make sure at least one role is on. Close and reopen SGT to analyze the wall again. Openings are not framed The roles were off, or the opening was not detected. Edit the system, turn on Header, Sill, Left Jamb or Right Jamb, and click Update. Members have the wrong orientation Toggle Flip for the row. Change Rotation (0, 90, 180, 270). Adjust Y Justification and Z Justification. If the preview still looks wrong after you change row settings, close and reopen SGT so the wall and openings are analyzed again before you place. Limitations SGT supports straight walls only. Girts do not follow later wall changes. Edit the system and click Update, or delete it and place it again. If you save the window (by fixing another field or making another edit) while an opening row is still in edit, the row's draft is written too. Esc then shows the old values in the row, but the plan keeps the draft, and a later refresh can show it again. A gap handle of an opening you just deleted can remain on the canvas until the preview redraws. Double-clicking it shows a Gap edit failed banner instead of a gap editor. Zee and angle shapes are for girts only, not for opening framing.

user-guide/tools/tdv.html.title: Transfer Drafting Views | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/tdv.html.summary: Transfer Drafting Views Transfer Drafting Views (TDV) copies drafting views between the open project and a library file. A library is a Revit project (.rvt) that holds standard drafting views. TDV imports views from a library into the open project and exports views from the open project into a library. Synopsis Ribbon: DB Tools > Common. Command Effect Import From Library Copies drafting views from a library into the active project. Export To Library Copies drafting views from the active project into a library. Both commands are disabled while the Library Paths Invalid warning is active (see Library settings). Library settings TDV reads its libraries from DB Tools > Settings > Library Files. Control Effect Add Library File Adds a .rvt file as a library entry. Add Fallback Path Adds an alternate path to the selected entry. TDV uses the fallback only when the main path is not valid. Remove Selected Removes the selected entry or fallback path. Validate Libraries Checks every path. Alias Name shown in the library picker. When empty, the picker shows the file name up to the first _R. A path is valid when the file exists, has the .rvt extension, and was saved in the same Revit version as the running session. A file from another Revit version is rejected with Revit version mismatch (file: <year>, current: <year>). TDV refuses to open a library from another version, so it never upgrades a library file. A file whose saved Revit version cannot be read is invalid on its own: TDV reports Could not read the library file's Revit version metadata. Re-save the library in Revit to fix it. If a saved path is invalid, the warning Library Paths Invalid disables both commands. Correct the paths and save the settings to enable them again. Several libraries can be configured. When you run a command, you choose one library from the picker. The picker lists only valid paths. If some paths are invalid, TDV shows a banner with their number. If no library is configured, the command fails with No library files configured. Configure library paths in Settings. If every path is invalid, it fails with All configured library files are inaccessible (<n> path(s) failed validation). Check library paths in Settings. Usage Run Import From Library or Export To Library. Select a library in the picker. TDV opens it in the background; the project you started from stays active. In the Transfer Drafting Views window, check the views to transfer. Resolve name conflicts (see Conflicts). Click Transfer Selected. Read the result dialog. For an import, the source is the library and the destination is the project. For an export, the source is the project and the destination is the library. Window Control Effect View Type filter Shows only the source views of one drafting view type. All Views shows all. Search box Filters the list by view name. The x button clears it. Transfer checkbox Includes the row in the transfer. View Name Destination name. Click it to edit. The name is trimmed before use. Replace Replaces an existing destination view of the same name. View Type Destination drafting view type. The list holds the types of the destination document. The default, Retain Original, uses the source view's type. Clear Selection Unchecks all rows. Transfer Selected Starts the transfer. It is disabled when no row is checked or a checked row has a conflict. Preview Shows an image of the selected source view. Drag to pan, use the mouse wheel to zoom, and click Zoom Extents to fit it. The preview shows Preview unavailable for the selected view. when the view cannot be exported to an image. Preview updates The preview always shows the current row. When you change the selection quickly, TDV skips the older previews. Errors An expander that lists errors. The status bar shows <views> | Selected: <n> | Replace: <n> | Adds: <n>, and during a transfer the count of finished views. A status icon in front of each name shows the row state: pending, success, failure, or conflict. Success icons appear when the whole transfer is committed, not when a single view finishes. Conflicts A checked row has a conflict, and a warning bar asks you to resolve it before continuing, when: the destination name is empty; the destination already has a drafting view with that name and Replace is off; or two checked rows have the same destination name. Rename the row, or turn on Replace, to resolve it. View types With Retain Original, TDV looks for a destination drafting view type with the source type's name. When it is missing, TDV creates it by duplicating an existing drafting view type of the destination. A row shows a warning mark when the source type name cannot be read; select a type explicitly in that case. With a named type, the type must exist in the destination. TDV does not create it. What is transferred For each checked view the transfer: finds or creates the destination view: a new drafting view, or, with Replace and an existing view of that name, the existing view with its type changed and its content deleted; copies the view scale and the View Description parameter; copies the view's elements with Revit's copy mechanism, one element at a time. Groups are copied as groups. Duplicate type names resolve to the types of the destination; copies the per-element graphic overrides. Not copied: viewports, title blocks, schedules, guide grids, other views, and view templates. The transfer copies the view's type but not a view template assignment. If a family used in the view is missing in the destination, Revit copies the family with the element. A detail array arrives as its groups, without the editable array association. The transfer is processed row by row and is one undo entry named Transfer Drafting Views. A failed view is rolled back alone: nothing from that view is added, and a view you chose to replace keeps its old content. The other views still transfer. If Revit discards the whole transfer, TDV reports All attempted changes were rolled back, and no view is added. You can cancel a running transfer from the progress overlay. The views processed so far are rolled back. Result The dialog title is Transfer Completed or, if any view failed, was not attempted or the run was canceled or rolled back, Transfer Completed with Issues. Its text is: Selected <n>, Processed <n>, Added <n>, Replaced <n>, Failed <n>, Not Attempted <n> followed by (All attempted changes were rolled back) or (Cancelled by user) when that applies. A Per-View Issues table lists each failed view with the error code and reason. Copy Details copies the table to the clipboard. Error code Cause DestinationNameRequired The destination name is empty. DuplicateTargetName Two checked rows have the same destination name. DestinationNameConflict The destination view exists and Replace is off. SourceTypeNameUnavailable, DestinationTypeMissing The destination drafting view type cannot be found or created. CreateViewFailed, ClearDestinationViewFailed The destination view cannot be created, renamed or cleared. MetadataCopyFailed The scale or description cannot be set. CopyElementsFailed Revit cannot copy an element. OverridesFailed A graphic override cannot be copied. TransactionRolledBack Revit discarded the whole transfer. Click Accept and Transfer More to keep the window open, or Close Tool to close it. Import TDV closes the library without saving after the dialog closes. If it cannot close the library, a banner asks you to close it manually. Press Ctrl+Z to undo an import; the transfer is one undo entry unless Revit discarded it. Export After the window closes with at least one view added or replaced: a workshared library is synchronized with central, relinquishing all borrowed elements, with the comment DB TOOLS - ADDED [<n>] DETAILS AND REPLACED [<n>] DETAILS.; a library that is not workshared is saved in place. If the library cannot be saved, synchronized or closed, the export fails and the error report names each failure. TDV then reactivates the project you started from. An export cannot be undone with Ctrl+Z once it is saved or synchronized. If nothing was added or replaced, the library is closed without saving. Library files and worksharing For a workshared library, TDV creates a temporary local copy named <library>_<user>.rvt under %APPDATA%\DBTools\Cache\TDV\LibraryLocals\<id>\, opens it with all worksets, and deletes the copy after it closes. A library that is not workshared is opened directly. If two users export to the same library at the same time, one synchronization can fail. Coordinate export times. To create a library, create a Revit project in the same Revit version, add the drafting view types you need, save it where your team can reach it, and add it in the settings. Limitations The library has to be saved in the Revit version that is running. Only drafting views are listed. A view with an element that Revit cannot copy fails as a whole. The names of the views and types in the destination decide conflicts; there is no rename-on-conflict option. The project and the library must be different documents.

user-guide/tools/vtc.html.title: View Template Comparer | DB Tools
user-guide/tools/vtc.html.summary: View Template Comparer View Template Comparer (VTC) compares two view templates in the open project, side by side. For each differing setting you choose which template's value to keep. VTC then writes the result to one of the templates or to a new merged template. It can also save templates to a library and load them back. Synopsis Ribbon: DB Tools > Testing > View Template Comparer. The Testing panel is shown when Enable Testing Tools is on in the settings (the default). If the project has no view templates, the command shows No view templates found in the document. Usage Select the Left and Right templates. The Swap button exchanges them. Click a value cell in the Settings Comparison tree to choose which side wins for that row. The Inspector has Use Left, Use Right and a clear button for the selected row. For a category row, use Edit Left or Edit Right (in the Inspector, from the row, or from the context menu Edit Override...) to stage a local graphic-override edit. A staged edit is marked Edited. Review the selected rows and eligible staged edits in the Preview tab. Click Process and choose the target. Comparison tree The tree has these top-level groups: Template Parameters, Model Categories, Annotation Categories, Analytical Model Categories, Imported Categories, Filters, Filter Overrides, Revit Links, Worksets and Design Options. Control Effect Search box Filters rows by name. Filter Limits the rows by configuration (see below). Select Left / Select Right Selects all differing rows shown by the current search and filter, taking the value from that side. Wipe Clears all selections and conflict state. Filters are kept. Reset Resets the search, the view filter and the conflict filter. Expand/collapse button Expands or collapses all groups. Show: All, Conflicts, Success After Process, shows all rows, only rows that failed to apply, or only rows that applied. Context menu Select from Left (with children), Select from Right (with children), Clear selection (with children), Edit Override..., and for Revit links Open Revit Link Settings... and Copy Revit Link Settings To.... A category row or a Filter Overrides row is configured in a template when that template hides it or overrides any of its graphics. A Template Parameters row is configured when the template includes the parameter. The Filter modes are: Configured (default): rows configured in either template. Configured in Left and Configured in Right: rows configured in that template. Rows that are not category, filter-override or template-parameter rows are always shown. Select Left and Select Right select every differing row that the filter and search show. Under Configured in Left, Select Left can therefore select a row that both templates hide when only Right overrides its graphics. Processing that row to the right template keeps it hidden and clears those overrides. Process Process applies the selected rows and the eligible staged edits in one batch. A staged edit is eligible when its row has a selected side and that side is the edited side, or when its row is not in the current comparison. An edit on a visible row with no selected side, or with the other side selected, is not applied. The dialog asks Apply changes to: Option Effect Overwrite <Left name> Writes the selected values into the Left template. Overwrite <Right name> Writes the selected values into the Right template. Create Merged Template Creates a new template named in Template Name:. The name is required. A merged template starts as a copy of the Left template, so settings VTC does not compare, such as the view scale, keep the Left values. Use Swap to choose the other base. For a row that has a selected side, the target takes that side's value. When the selected side lacks the setting (it is absent there), the row in the target is reset to its default, instead of keeping the base value. This applies to categories, worksets and Revit link settings. A setting that cannot be applied is reported as a conflict, and the others are applied. Any other failure undoes the whole batch. Overwriting a template is one undo entry. Create Merged Template is one undo entry named Create Merged View Template. If it fails, no template remains, so you can retry with the same name. Imported categories Imported categories (DWG, DXF and other imports) appear under their own Imported Categories group. They use the same compare, edit, preview and process flow as other categories. Revit links Revit link settings appear under Revit Links, grouped by link. Type-level and instance-level link targets are listed separately. VTC lists only the settings that the running Revit version lets add-ins both read and write: Visibility Mode, Linked View, Filters, Nested Links, Object Styles, Color Fill, View Range, Phase, Phase Filter, Detail Level, Discipline. VTC matches links between the two templates by link name. If two links have the same name, VTC stops with an error. Action Effect Open Revit Link Settings... Opens Native Revit Link Settings for one link target. The window always lists all supported settings of that target, even if you opened it from one row. Apply to Template writes the selected settings; it is one undo entry. Copy Revit Link Settings To... Copies the supported settings to other link targets. Linked View, Phase and Phase Filter are matched by name in the target linked model. If the name is unavailable because the linked document is unloaded, the raw id is reused only when source and target reference the same linked model. The copy is one undo entry. A target that cannot accept the settings is reported and the others are copied. Any other failure leaves every target unchanged. Loading a saved template from the library also remaps Linked View, Phase and Phase Filter by name in the target linked model. If the saved name is not found there, the setting fails with a not-found error. If the snapshot holds no name (the linked document was unloaded), the stored id is reused. When only one template contains the link row, VTC uses that template. When both do and you have not selected a side, VTC asks which template to use. Library The Library tab saves template snapshots to disk and applies them back to a template. Save Template > Left Template, Right Template or Merged Template. An optional name field sets the saved name. When blank, the source template name is used. Load applies the selected saved template to the side chosen in Load to:. It first asks for confirmation, because it overwrites the template's settings in Revit. A delete button removes the selected saved template, and a refresh button reloads the list. Snapshots are stored under %APPDATA%\DBTools\Cache\VTC\. VTC creates the folder on the first save. Saved names ignore case and surrounding spaces. Saving under an existing name asks Replace saved template 'X'?; Cancel saves nothing. If VTC cannot check the name, or another Revit session saves that name during your save, the save fails and nothing is overwritten. A snapshot that is incomplete or malformed fails to load with a storage error. VTC does not repair or migrate it. If a save or delete succeeds but the list cannot refresh, VTC shows a warning that names the template. A save or delete that fails shows an error. Result Process, Apply to Template and Copy Revit Link Settings To... each make one undo entry. VTC reports each result in an alert titled View Template Comparer.
